content:
C2  Stress Echo 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
C2 - 3 
Overview 
Prerequisite: A working knowledge of stress echo examinations is necessary before capturing stress 
echo clips. 
Use stress echo to capture and review cardiac clips for predefined mulitple-stage protocols for 
your stress echo workflow. A cardiac clip displays motion from end diastole (ED) to end systole 
(ES) or from R-wave to R-wave as indicated by the R-wave of the ECG trace. 
Use the configuration settings to define stress echo protocols. 
See also: For information about acquiring ECG traces with the physiologic function, refer to 
Chapter C1 in this manual. 
Terminology Used in this Chapter 
Term 
Definition 
compare task 
Displays preferred images and clips in a side-by-side format for analysis. 
If the selection task is incomplete for a view, all acquired images and clips display for 
the view. 
continuous 
A capture method limiting the number of continuous clips to 750 for all stages. 
Continuous capture is always prospective. 
The navigation panel indicates the number of clips acquired during continuous capture. 
exam review 
A review function available for all ultrasound studies. 
non-continuous 
A stage capture method limiting the number of clips per capture. Non-continuous 
capture can be retrospective or prospective. 
preferred 
Indicates a clip or image is identified for review and analysis. 
protocol 
A workflow protocol or predefined checklist for a stress echo study. 
selection task 
Displays all images and clips captured during the stress echo protocol for identifying 
preferred clips and images. 
stage 
A phase within a stress echo protocol, for example, a rest stage. 
Depending on the protocol configuration, you can acquire multiple images during each 
stage. 
stress echo review 
A review function specific to stress echo protocols. 
task 
A defined step in a protocol, for example, acquiring a view or selecting preferred images 
and clips. 
view 
A step within a stage of a stress echo protocol, for example, a short axis view.

C2  Stress Echo 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
C2 - 7 
Activating a Stress Echo Protocol 
You can activate a stress echo study only with compatible transducers and image presets. 
Enter a patient name in the patient registration form before you start a stress echo study. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and image presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use. 
You can create user-defined names when you add a stage or view during a stress echo 
protocol. Names can include alphanumeric characters (A-Z, 0-9), periods (.), and hyphens (-). 
To activate a stress echo protocol: 
1. 
Tap Workflow and then select Stress Echo, if necessary. 
The system displays the Stress Echo tab with the available protocols. 
2. 
Tap the required protocol. 
 
To 
Do This 
Select a protocol stage 
 Tap Stage and then select the required stage. 
Select a view 
 Tap the required view. 
Note: You can change the view during a continuous capture. 
Advance to the next predefined stage 
 Tap Stage and then select the required stage. 
Advance to the next view in the 
protocol stage 
 Rotate FORWARD/BACKWARD clockwise. 
Note: Once the last view in the stage is complete, rotating the control 
advances to the first view in the next stage. 
Show or hide the region of interest 
(ROI) 
 Tap ROI. 
– On shows the ROI. 
– Off hides the ROI. 
Change the position of the ECG trace 
(Available only when the ROI is shown) 
 Tap ECG in ROI. 
– On displays the ECG in the ROI. 
– Off displays the ECG below the image. 
Display an image as a reference for 
the active view 
 Click the arrow next to Reference View in the left panel. 
Note: Image capture acquires only the live image. 
Pause a stress echo protocol 
 Tap Pause Protocol. 
The system hides the ROI and suspends the feature. 
Resume a stress echo protocol 
 Tap Resume Protocol.

C2  Stress Echo 
C2 - 8 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
To 
Do This 
Add a stage during a stress echo 
protocol 
(Available only when clips are not acquired for the next stage) 
1. Tap Add Stage. 
2. Tap the required Stage Property. 
The system duplicates the configuration settings of the selected 
stage. 
3. Enter a unique name in the Stage Name text box. 
4. Tap Save. 
The system adds the new stage to the list of stages for the protocol. 
The system displays a message when the maximum number of 
stages is reached. 
5. To exit without saving the new stage, tap Cancel. 
Add a view during a stress echo 
protocol 
1. Tap Add View. 
2. Tap the required View Property. 
3. Enter a unique name in the View Name text box. 
4. To save the view to the active stage, tap Save. 
The system adds the new view to the list of views for the stage. 
The system displays a message when the maximum number of views 
is reached. 
5. To add the view to all stages, tap Save to all stages. 
6. To exit without saving the new view, tap Cancel. 
End the protocol and exit stress echo 
Note: You cannot modify or resume a completed stress echo study. 
Complete the views, select preferred images and clips, and modify the 
stress echo protocol, if necessary, before ending the study. 
1. Tap End Protocol. 
If any views are incomplete, the system displays a dialog box asking 
if you want to omit the views and end the protocol. 
If a protocol is incomplete, the system displays a dialog box alerting 
you that unselected images will be deleted. 
2. To end the study, click OK. 
If you did not acquire clips, the system displays the protocol list. 
If you acquired clips, the system activates stress echo review. 
3. To cancel and return to the study, click Cancel. 
Cancel the stress echo protocol 
1. Tap Cancel Protocol. 
The system displays the list of available protocols. 
2. To select another protocol, tap the name of the protocol. 
Note: You can only cancel the protocol if the active protocol has no 
captured images. 
Begin a different stress echo protocol 
 Complete the stress echo protocol and then start a new study. 
Note: Only one stress echo protocol is available for each study.

Advanced Imaging Manual 
Capturing Images and Clips during a Stress Echo Protocol 
You can acquire images and clips of anatomical views during a stress echo protocol. You can 
also change views during a continuous capture. 
During clip capture, the system acquires and labels the clip and can start the stage timer for the 
stage. Pausing the protocol does not pause the stage timer. When capture is complete, the 
navigation panel displays an ellipsis (...) by the view and the selection screen can display. 
The system displays an icon on clips captured during a stress echo protocol. 
 
Use the configuration settings to customize capture settings. 
See also: For information about capturing images and playing clips, refer to Chapter 5 in the 
Instructions for Use. 
To acquire an image or clip: 
 
Adjust the region of interest (ROI) and image depth, if necessary. 
Note: The system applies the position, size, depth, and image parameters to subsequent 
acquisitions of the view. 
 
To 
Do This 
Capture an image 
 Press FREEZE and then press CAPTURE. 
Capture a clip during a 
non-continuous stage 
 Press CAPTURE. 
The system stops acquisition of clips as indicated by the settings for 
capture. 
Capture a clip during a continuous 
stage 
1. To start or resume the capture, press CAPTURE. 
2. To start capture of the next view, press UPDATE. 
3. To stop the capture, press CAPTURE again. 
Specify the duration of a recorded 
clip 
1. Press Clip Capture to select a setting. 
– Seconds sets the clip length to seconds. 
– Beats sets the clip length to heart beats. 
2. Rotate Clip Capture to select a duration.

Advanced Imaging Manual 
Selecting Preferred Images and Clips for Analysis 
Use preferred images and clips for comparison and analysis. You can select preferred images 
and clips during stress echo review. 
The system activates the selection task as indicated by the protocol configuration, for example, 
at the end of each view, at the end of each stage, or at the end of all stages. 
The selection screen displays the acquired images and clips for views and stages. Images and 
clips are numbered in the sequence of acquisition. 
If you capture an image or clip from a multiple display layout during stress echo review, the 
system adds the image or clip to the end of the protocol. 
The system deletes all clips and images marked with a red "x" when you end the study. 
Use the configuration settings to setup the selection task.

Comparing a Real-time Image to a Reference Clip 
You can use the reference clip function to compare a real-time image to a clip from a rest stage 
or prior stage during a stress echo protocol. 
During the reference clip function: 
 
The system displays a side-by-side format with the reference clip on the left and the real-
time image on the right. 
 
The system places the region of interest (ROI) on the real-time image in alignment with the 
ROI on the reference clip. 
 
As you advance through the stress echo protocol, if a corresponding reference clip is not 
available for the view, the system displays the message: Not Acquired. 
To compare a real-time image to reference clip: 
Prerequisite: A stress echo protocol is active and a minimum of one stage is complete.  
 
Tap Reference Clip. 
 
To 
Do This 
Select another preferred clip as the 
reference clip 
 Activate the pointer and then click the left or right arrow below the 
reference clip to cycle through available clips. 
Compare the real-time image to 
another stage 
1. Tap Reference Stage and then select an option. 
– Rest indicates the reference clip is from the rest stage. 
– Previous Stage indicates the reference clip is from the prior 
stage. 
– Reference Stage indicates the stage for all reference clips as you 
advance through the stress echo protocol. 
Note: The stage includes the stage name in parentheses, for 
example, Rest (Baseline). 
2. To close the menu, tap Reference Stage again. 
To exit the reference clip function 
 Tap Reference Clip again.

Introduction to the Transesophageal Transducers 
 WARNING: Do not use this transducer unless you are thoroughly trained in transesophageal 
echocardiography and are familiar with the orientation of cardiac images obtained through a 
TEE procedure. The transesophageal transducer should be used only by a licensed physician. 
 WARNING: Before attempting to use this transducer, you should be thoroughly familiar with the 
safe operation of the ultrasound system and this transducer. Refer to the content of this chapter 
and to the Safety and Care chapter in the Instructions for Use manual for ultrasound system and 
transducer-related safety information. 
See also: For general ultrasound system and transducer-related safety information, refer to 
Chapter 2 and Chapter 3 in the Instructions for Use. For information about the articulation 
controls, brakes, on-screen messages, temperature controls, and safeguards for a specific 
transesophageal transducer, refer to the following chapter in this manual: 
– 
Chapter C4, Z6T Transesophageal Transducer 
 WARNING: The leakage current test for transesophageal transducers must be done prior to 
each use in order to reduce the likelihood of harm to the patient. Unsafe leakage current could 
result in electrical burns to the patient during use, including during defibrillation. Refer to the 
manufacturer's instructions included with the tester. 
The transesophageal transducer can be introduced into the esophagus of the patient to obtain 
images of the heart structure. This procedure, known as transesophageal echocardiography 
(TEE), can provide virtually unobstructed views of the heart and surrounding tissue.

C3  Transesophageal Transducer 
C3 - 6 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Inspecting the Transducer 
To inspect the transducer before use: 
1. 
Examine by look and touch the entire surface of the flexible shaft all the way to the distal 
tip for cuts, scrapes, protrusions, holes, dents, or cracks. 
If you discover the surface of the transducer has been compromised, do not use the 
transducer. Contact your local Siemens Healthineers representative. 
2. 
Rotate the flex controls through the full range of motion and observe that the control 
movement is smooth and easy. 
If the range of motion is tight or binding, or if the transducer controls make an unusual 
noise, do not use the transducer. Contact your local Siemens Healthineers representative. 
If the distal tip appears to sag slightly when the flex controls are in the neutral position, this 
may be a sign of stretched or damaged control cables. Do not use the transducer. Contact 
your local Siemens Healthineers representative. 
3. 
Test the brakes: 
– 
Engage the brakes (deflection locking mechanism) by pressing each ratchet button. 
The brakes hold the distal tip at the appropriate articulation angle when locked.

C3  Transesophageal Transducer 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
C3 - 7 
Using a Transducer Sheath (Transducer Cover) 
See also: For information about transducer sheaths, refer to Chapter 3 in the Instructions for Use. 
 WARNING: There have been reports of severe allergic reactions to medical devices containing 
latex (natural rubber). Health care professionals are advised to identify latex-sensitive patients 
and be prepared to treat allergic reactions promptly. For additional information in the U.S.A., 
refer to FDA Medical Alert MDA91-1. 
For greatest patient and operator safety, cover a transducer with a transducer sheath. Siemens 
Healthineers recommends that you use market-cleared transducer sheaths specifically 
designed for TEE applications. Follow the instructions provided by the manufacturer of the 
transducer sheath. 
Disposal 
While wearing protective gloves, remove the transducer sheath from the transducer. Dispose of 
the transducer sheath according to local, state, and regional laws and regulations for 
biohazardous waste. 
Using Protective Drapes 
Follow your hospital's guidelines regarding equipment use in the presence of infectious 
disease. 
Electrical Safety Considerations 
For safe use of this device, ensure an electrical safety procedure is in place for periodically 
inspecting the grounding system in the examination area and that this procedure is performed 
routinely. 
Implantable Devices 
 WARNING: Ultrasound systems, like other medical equipment, use high-frequency electrical 
signals that can interfere with implantable devices such as pacemakers and implantable 
cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs). When using a transesophageal transducer on a patient who 
has an implantable device, pay special attention to the performance of the implantable device. 
Stop the examination if there is interference.

content:
C3  Transesophageal Transducer 
C3 - 8 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Defibrillators 
 WARNING: Disconnect the transducer during defibrillation because a malfunction of the safety 
controls could otherwise result in electrical burns for the patient. Complete the leakage current 
test for transesophageal transducers in order to reduce the likelihood of harm to the patient 
during use. 
The transesophageal transducer is designed to withstand the effects of defibrillation. There are 
no exposed conductive surfaces distal to the handle. Within the flexible shaft, a chassis ground 
shield covers all active circuits and conductors. The shield runs along the entire length of the 
transducer. 
The transesophageal transducer is not tested to meet certification requirements for a Type BF 
defibrillator-proof device per the IEC 60601-1 Standard for Safety of Medical Equipment. 
Transesophageal transducers with this label are not certified as defibrillation proof: 
 
Type BF Applied Part. 
Examples of Risks 
Follow the protocols of your clinic or hospital to determine the safest response for your patient 
before starting defibrillation: disconnecting the transesophageal transducer from the ultrasound 
system or removing the transesophageal transducer from the patient. 
Transducer in the Patient during Defibrillation 
 
Defibrillation might not be as effective because the transesophageal transducer may 
absorb or divert the current required to restart the heart. 
 
If the electrical insulation surrounding the insertable portion of the transesophageal 
transducer becomes damaged during intubation, the patient could suffer burns to the 
esophagus. For example: 
– 
If the bite guard moves during intubation, the patient could bite into the inserted 
portion of the transesophageal transducer, exposing the transesophageal transducer's 
electrical circuitry to the patient's esophagus. 
– 
The inserted portion of the transesophageal transducer could become stressed during 
intubation, introducing cracks in the electrical insulation and exposing the 
transesophageal transducer's electrical circuitry to the patient's esophagus. 
Transducer Removed from the Patient before Defibrillation 
 
Delay in defibrillation while the transesophageal transducer is removed from the patient. 
 
Injury to the esophagus, vocal cords, or teeth resulting from removing the transesophageal 
transducer too quickly.

content:
C3  Transesophageal Transducer 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
C3 - 9 
Punctures or Cracks 
Punctures or cracks in the outer layer of the transducer could expose the patient's esophagus 
to chassis leakage current and cause the patient to be at the chassis ground potential. If this 
occurs, the transducer will no longer meet the requirements of a Type BF classification. The 
transducer would no longer be a "floating" part and would fail a dielectric test. Provided that the 
internal grounding mechanism within the ultrasound system's power cord is intact and the cord 
is connected to a properly grounded wall outlet, there is little hazard to the user or patient from 
the system's leakage current. However, since the patient would now be at ground potential, 
leakage currents from other devices within the patient's environment could travel through the 
patient, compromising the safety to the patient or operator. If punctures or cracks in the outer 
layer of the transducer are observed, contact your local Siemens Healthineers representative. 
Electrosurgical Units 
 WARNING: Use only isolated output electrosurgical units with the transesophageal transducer 
and disconnect the transducer when it is not in use. Failure to follow these procedures can result 
in esophageal burns for the patient, damage to the equipment, and unreliable data. 
Use only electrosurgical units that have isolated outputs. If possible, use 
return-fault/ground-fault detection circuits, which provide extra protection. 
Electrosurgical units and other operating room devices that do not have isolated outputs can 
introduce radio frequency electromagnetic fields or currents into the patient. The transducer is 
susceptible to these radio frequencies, which can interfere with the 2D-mode image and can 
completely override the color flow image, making it useless for diagnostic purposes. 
In addition, any failure to an electrosurgical unit or other device, including the transesophageal 
transducer, could cause electrosurgical currents to return along the transducer's conductors. As 
a result, the patient could suffer from burns to the esophageal membranes. This arcing could 
also damage the transducer. To reduce the risk of leakage currents and electrosurgical 
interference, disconnect the transesophageal transducer from the ultrasound system when it is 
not in use. 
Where isolation of electrosurgical units is in question, consult the manual for each 
electrosurgical unit or contact the biomedical engineering group.

content:
C3  Transesophageal Transducer 
C3 - 10 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Exam Considerations 
Bite Guards 
 WARNING: Follow the bite guard manufacturer's instructions to clean, disinfect, and rinse the 
bite guard if you use a reusable bite guard. Any disinfectant remaining on the reusable bite 
guard can burn the patient's mouth. 
Bite guards are provided with the transducer for use with patients who will be awake during the 
exam. These guards are also available from third-party providers. 
Do not use the provided bite guard with anesthetized patients. Use a separately purchased bite 
guard that has a space for taping an endotracheal tube to the guard. 
Exam Procedures 
 WARNING: Ensure that the friction brakes are unlocked and the flex controls are in the neutral 
alignment position when you insert or withdraw the transducer. Advancing or withdrawing the 
transducer while the transducer tip is bent and/or rigid can result in patient injury or death. 
 WARNING: Do not use excessive force to advance or withdraw the transducer. Using excessive 
force to advance or withdraw the transducer can result in patient injury or death. If you 
encounter strong resistance during transducer articulation, discontinue the procedure. Identify 
and address the cause of the resistance before resuming the procedure. Withdraw and redirect 
the transducer as needed. 
 WARNING: To reduce the risk of pressure necrosis, put the transducer in the neutral position 
when inserting or withdrawing it. Minimize pressure applied to the articulating section and distal 
tip. Do not let the distal tip displace tissue for more than five minutes. 
 WARNING: Do not use the transesophageal transducer for any procedure requiring 
hyperextension of the neck. Improper patient positioning can cause paralysis of the vocal cord. 
 WARNING: Always use a bite guard to prevent damage to the transducer from the patient's 
teeth, which could, as a result, create potential mechanical and electrical hazards for the patient. 
Using a bite guard also protects the patient's teeth.

content:
C3  Transesophageal Transducer 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
C3 - 11 
Exam Procedures 
Prerequisite: Connect the transducer to the ultrasound system and then activate the transducer 
prior to inserting the transducer into the patient. 
1. 
Remove dentures, if present, and place them in a protected area until after the procedure. 
2. 
Place a transducer sheath on the transducer, if needed. 
3. 
Place a bite guard around the distal end of the transducer. 
4. 
Ensure that both friction brakes are unlocked and both flex controls are in the neutral 
alignment position before inserting the transducer so that the transducer can bend to 
accommodate the path of the esophagus. 
5. 
Place the transducer in the patient's mouth, and secure the bite guard into place before 
further advancing the transducer. 
6. 
When the transducer has been inserted, press the array rotation control to change the 
scan plane. 
7. 
As necessary, adjust the anterior/posterior and the left/right deflection using the flex 
controls. Position the transducer for optimal acoustical contact and the required viewing 
scan plane. 
8. 
When the required scan plane is achieved and good acoustical contact is made, engage 
both the anterior/posterior and the left/right friction brakes. 
9. 
Unlock both friction brakes and move both flex controls to the neutral position to acquire 
new echocardiographic views, which necessitate further advancement or withdrawal of the 
transducer, or change in the deflection. 
10. Unlock both friction brakes and move both flex controls to the neutral position to remove 
the transducer.

content:
C3  Transesophageal Transducer 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
C3 - 13 
Cleaning and Disinfecting the Transducer 
 WARNING: To avoid electrical shock and damage to the system, disconnect the transducer 
prior to cleaning or disinfecting. 
 WARNING: Never use Steam Heat or Ethylene Oxide for disinfecting the transesophageal 
transducer. These disinfection methods may damage the jacketing material, the transducer 
array, or the articulation controls, making the device unsafe to use on a patient. 
 WARNING: Never use iodine or solutions containing iodine for cleaning or disinfecting the 
transesophageal transducer. Iodine will cause degradation of the shaft material and of the distal 
tip resulting in a dangerous electrical hazard. 
 Caution: Never clean the transducer with bleach. Cleaning with bleach will damage the flexible 
shaft jacketing material, which will invalidate the manufacturer's warranty and could increase 
leakage current. 
 Caution: The distal tip is very sensitive to pressure. Care must be taken not to damage the tip 
while cleaning and disinfecting the distal tip. 
 Caution: Do not bend the flexible shaft into a curve of less than 30.5 cm in diameter. 
 Caution: The transducers have been designed and tested to be able to withstand high-level 
disinfection as recommended by the manufacturer of the disinfectant product. Carefully follow 
the disinfectant manufacturer's instructions. 
 Caution: Never immerse the entire transesophageal transducer in any solution. Immersion of 
the transducer handle could introduce fluid into the housing and cause damage to the controls or 
steering cables. 
 Caution: Do not clean the transducer with ethanol or methanol. Ethanol and methanol can 
damage the transducer. 
 Caution: Do not immerse the transducer above 100 cm from the distal tip; doing so may 
damage the controls.

C3  Transesophageal Transducer 
C3 - 14 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Cleaning a Transducer at the Point of Use 
Cleaning a transducer immediately after each use prevents soil and contaminants from drying 
on the surface of the transducer and facilitates subsequent cleaning. 
To immediately clean a transesophageal transducer after each use: 
1. 
Disconnect and remove the transducer from the ultrasound system. 
2. 
Remove the transducer sheath. 
3. 
Immediately clean the transducer in close proximity to the point of use. 
a. 
Moisten a clean gauze pad or lint-free cloth with water or an approved cleaner. Or, use 
an approved cleaning wipe or sponge. 
See also: For a list of approved cleaners, refer to page C3-12. 
b. 
Carefully wipe the transducer surface intended for contact with the patient. Avoid 
touching the electrical components on the connector. 
4. 
Perform subsequent cleaning of the transducer according to the next procedure.

content:
C3  Transesophageal Transducer 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
C3 - 15 
Cleaning a Transducer 
Cleaning a transducer removes soil and contaminants from the surface of the transducer and 
prepares the transducer for disinfection. 
To clean a transesophageal transducer: 
Prerequisite: The transducer is disconnected and removed from the ultrasound system. The 
transducer sheath is removed from the transducer. 
1. 
Select an approved cleaner. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for concentration and 
temperature of the solution and contact time when cleaning the surface of the transducer. 
See also: For a list of approved cleaners, refer to page C3-12. 
2. 
Clean the distal tip and flexible shaft of the transducer using one of the following cleaning 
methods. Avoid touching the electrical components on the connector. 
– 
If immersion is required, submerge the distal tip and flexible shaft up to the 100-cm 
mark. Do not allow the handle, controls, cable, or connector to become wet. 
– 
If wiping is required, carefully wipe the distal tip and flexible shaft. 
– 
If spraying is required, do not spray the distal tip and flexible shaft near the ultrasound 
system. Never spray the transducer connector. 
3. 
Clean the handle, controls, cable, and connector of the transducer. Keep the electrical 
components on the connector dry. 
a. 
Moisten a clean gauze pad or lint-free cloth with an approved cleaner. Or, use an 
approved cleaning wipe. 
b. 
Carefully wipe the handle, controls, cable, and connector. 
4. 
Rinse the distal tip and flexible shaft up to the 100-cm mark according to the cleaner 
manufacturer's instructions. Do not rinse the handle, controls, cable, and connector. Keep 
the electrical components on the connector dry. 
Note: If the cleaner manufacturer does not provide rinsing instructions, thoroughly rinse the 
distal tip and flexible shaft up to the 100-cm mark with deionized water at room temperature. 
5. 
Disinfect the transducer.

Disinfecting a Transducer 
Immediately after cleaning, disinfect a transducer to destroy pathogens and other 
microorganisms and to prepare the transducer for storage or the next clinical use. 
 
Submerge only to the 100-cm mark. 
To disinfect a transesophageal transducer: 
Prerequisite: Clean the transducer. 
1. 
Select an approved disinfectant for high-level disinfection. Follow the disinfectant 
manufacturer's instructions for concentration and temperature of the solution and contact 
time when high-level disinfecting the surface of the transducer. 
See also: For a list of approved disinfectants, refer to page C3-12. 
2. 
Disinfect the distal tip and flexible shaft of the transducer using one of the following 
disinfection methods. Avoid touching the electrical components on the connector. 
– 
If immersion is required, submerge the distal tip and flexible shaft up to the 100-cm 
mark. Do not allow the handle, controls, cable, or connector to become wet. 
– 
If wiping is required, carefully wipe the distal tip and flexible shaft. 
– 
If spraying is required, do not spray the distal tip and flexible shaft near the ultrasound 
system. Never spray the transducer connector. 
– 
If a reprocessing device is required, use a device compliant with ISO 15883 and follow 
the reprocessing device manufacturer's instructions.

content:
C3  Transesophageal Transducer 
C3 - 18 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Storing and Handling 
The transesophageal transducer is a mechanically sensitive device. The distal tip is especially 
sensitive to bumps, scrapes, and jarring. Take extreme care when handling and storing the 
transducer. Never move the distal tip by hand. Always use the flex controls. 
When you store the transesophageal transducer, ensure that the friction brakes are off, the 
distal tip is straight, and the cables and flexible shaft are free of kinks. 
Use an approved disposable tip protector on the distal tip during storage. 
Store the transducer in a clean, dry, protected environment. The transesophageal transducer is 
fragile and should not be stored in the transducer holders on the system. 
Transporting the Transducer 
Use the case for shipping or for moving the disinfected transducer from one site to another. 
Take care that the distal tip is straight and that the cable is free of kinks as you carefully place 
the transducer in the foam padding. Before you close the lid, ensure that nothing protrudes from 
the case.

Electrical Safety: Leakage Current Test 
 WARNING: The leakage current test for transesophageal transducers must be performed prior 
to each use in order to reduce the likelihood of harm to the patient. Unsafe leakage current could 
result in electrical burns to the patient during use, including during defibrillation. Refer to the 
manufacturer's operating instructions for the leakage current tester. 
 WARNING: To avoid damage to the transducer, observe the immersion levels. Do not allow the 
transducer handle, controls, strain relief, cable, and system connector to become wet. Keep the 
handle, flex controls, strain relief, cable, and connector dry to prevent introducing fluid into the 
housing and damage to the controls or steering cables. 
 WARNING: To prevent electric shock and possible injury to anyone near the leakage current 
tester, avoid touching the conductivity probe when the tester is on. Refer to the manufacturer's 
operating instructions for the leakage current tester. 
You must perform the leakage current test prior to each use of the transesophageal transducer. 
Passing the test assures the leakage current is within acceptable limits at the time of the test. 
See also: For information about performing the required tests, refer to the manufacturer's operating 
instructions for the leakage current tester.

content:
C3  Transesophageal Transducer 
C3 - 20 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
To prepare for the leakage current test: 
Prerequisite: A compatible leakage current tester and a compatible transducer adapter. 
1. 
Connect the transesophageal transducer to a compatible transducer adapter. 
2. 
Immerse the liquid-tight portion of the transducer into a bath of disinfectant or sterile saline 
solution up to, but not beyond, the last depth mark. Keep the handle, flex controls, strain 
relief, cable, and system connector dry. 
Note: For the Z6T transesophageal transducer, the last depth mark is at 100 cm. 
See also: For a list of approved disinfectants, refer to page C3-12. 
3. 
Place the conductivity probe in the disinfectant or sterile saline solution bath to a minimum 
depth of 25 mm (1 inch). 
4. 
Connect the transducer adapter and conductivity probe to the leakage current tester as 
indicated in the manufacturer's operating instructions for the leakage current tester. 
 
To perform the leakage current test: 
Prerequisite: Prepare for the leakage current test. 
1. 
Carefully follow the manufacturer's operating instructions for the leakage current tester as 
you perform all required tests, for example: 
a. 
Enter the required test voltage and leakage current test values. or, Select the default 
test settings for the Z6T transducer. 
b. 
Test the leakage current tester. 
c. 
Test the bath conductivity, if necessary. 
Note: Your compatible leakage current tester may simultaneously test the bath conductivity 
and the transesophageal transducer. 
d. 
Test the transesophageal transducer. 
2. 
Obtain the leakage current results for the transducer. 
– 
A passing result indicates you can prepare the transducer for use. 
– 
A failing result indicates the transducer did not pass the leakage current test. Check all 
connections and then re-test the transducer. If a failure occurs again, do not use the 
transducer for a patient study and contact your Siemens Healthineers service 
representative. 
3. 
To prepare the transducer for use, rinse the distal tip and flexible shaft of the transducer up 
to the 100-cm mark according to the disinfectant manufacturer's instructions. Do not rinse 
the handle, flex controls, strain relief, cable, and connector. Keep the electrical 
components on the connector dry. 
Note: If the disinfectant manufacturer does not provide rinsing instructions, thoroughly rinse the 
distal tip and flexible shaft up to the 100-cm mark with deionized water at room temperature. 
Service and Repair 
Do not attempt to repair or alter any part of the transesophageal transducer. Contact your local 
Siemens Healthineers service representative office immediately if your transducer appears to 
be damaged or malfunctions in any way.

Transducer Articulation Controls 
 Caution: Do not use your hands or fingers to bend or manipulate the articulating section of the 
transesophageal transducer. To avoid severe damage to the articulating mechanism, use only 
the transducer controls to change the articulation angle. 
The flex controls, smart controls, and friction brakes are located on the handle of the 
transducer.

1

4

C4  Z6T Transesophageal Transducer 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
C4 - 5 
Flex Controls 
The flex controls manipulate the movement of the distal tip. 
 
Example of markings located on the flex controls. 
Anterior/Posterior Deflection 
For anterior deflection (anteflexion) of the distal tip, rotate the flex control toward the A marking 
to move the tip anteriorly. 
For posterior deflection (retroflexion) of the distal tip, rotate the flex control toward the P 
marking to move the tip posteriorly. 
Right/Left Deflection 
For right deflection of the distal tip, rotate the flex control toward the R marking to move the 
tip right. 
For left deflection of the distal tip, rotate the flex control toward the L marking to move the 
tip left. 
Neutral Position 
To place the distal tip in the neutral position, rotate the anterior/posterior flex control and the 
right/left flex control to align the raised reference lines with the raised reference line on the 
handle of the transducer.

C4  Z6T Transesophageal Transducer 
C4 - 12 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Temperature Controls and Safeguards 
 WARNING: Disconnect the transducer if the system displays the message indicating that the 
maximum thermal limit is exceeded. (The transducer temperature is 43°C or higher.) Failure to 
disconnect a transesophageal transducer that has exceeded the maximum thermal limit can 
burn the patient's esophagus. Reconnect the transducer after the transducer has cooled. Or, 
use a different transducer. 
Because some concerns have been raised about possible thermal injury to the esophagus due 
to the local buildup of heat during transesophageal echocardiography, the transesophageal 
transducer incorporates a shut-off mechanism in the interest of patient safety in the unlikely 
event overheating should occur. For additional information on temperature limitation, refer to 
EN 60601-2-37 and IEC 60601-2-37. 
Temperature Sensor 
A temperature sensor mounted in the distal tip of the transducer monitors the temperature of 
the scanning array. 
The ultrasound system displays the lens temperature in the imaging parameters. 
 
Example of the lens temperature display. 
When the temperature is 37°C or below, the system displays the temperature as <37°C. 
When the temperature is above 37°C, the system displays the actual temperature. 
If the transducer temperature is not yet 42.5°C and your patient has a temperature or is slightly 
warm, you can use a software setting to cool down the transducer. This allows you to continue 
imaging in 2D-mode or 2D-mode with color and 4D-mode or 4D-mode with color. 
Note: This software setting is not available during M-mode or Doppler. 
To activate the cool down setting during 2D-mode or 4D-mode: 
1. 
Tap Cool Down. 
2. 
To exit, tap Cool Down again.

Advanced Imaging Manual

Transducer Temperature Limit 
When the transducer temperature reaches 42.5°C, the system activates the cool down state 
and reduces the temperature, allowing you to continue imaging. For example, during 2D-mode 
or 2D-mode with color imaging, the system reduces the frame rate, and during 4D-mode or 
4D-mode with color imaging, the system reduces the volume rate. 
At 43°C, the system displays a warning message, stops imaging, and shuts down all power to 
the transducer.

Temperature Sensor Failure 
 WARNING: Disconnect the transducer if the system displays the message indicating a 
temperature monitor failure. Remove the transducer from the patient. Failure to disconnect and 
remove a transesophageal transducer with faulty temperature sensor can burn the patient's 
esophagus. Contact your Siemens Healthineers service representative. 
If the system detects a temperature sensor failure, the system stops imaging and displays the 
following message: 
A temperature monitoring error has occurred. Disconnect the transducer. Remove the 
transducer from the patient. Contact your Siemens service representative. 
Note: The system is not operable until you disconnect the transesophageal transducer or cycle 
power to the system.

C4  Z6T Transesophageal Transducer 
C4 - 14 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Additional Thermal Safeguard 
 WARNING: Disconnect the transducer if the system displays the message indicating that the 
acceptable thermal limit is exceeded. Remove the transducer from the patient. Failure to 
disconnect and remove a transesophageal transducer that has exceeded the maximum thermal 
limit can burn the patient's esophagus. Contact your Siemens Healthineers service 
representative. 
If the system's hardware detects the lens surface temperature is above the acceptable limit, the 
system stops imaging and displays the following message: 
The transducer temperature is above the acceptable limit. Disconnect the transducer. 
Remove the transducer from the patient. Contact your Siemens service representative. 
You must observe the steps in the on-screen message. 
Note: The system is not operable until you disconnect the transesophageal transducer or cycle 
power to the system. 
Managing the Lens Surface Temperature 
You can reduce the acoustic output to lower the lens surface temperature. 
To reduce the acoustic output: 
 
Rotate Transmit Power counterclockwise to lower the transmit power. 
See also: For information about imaging functions that change acoustic output, refer to Chapter 2 in 
the Instructions for Use. 
Optimizing Imaging 
You can reposition the volume and adjust imaging parameters during volume imaging and 
review. 
See also: For information on optimizing a cardiac volume, refer to Chapter D2 in this manual.

Imaging with AI Assist during a Transthoracic 
Echocardiogram 
AI Assist for a transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) recognizes anatomy for transthoracic views 
of the heart, for example, the mitral valve (MV) in a view of the parasternal short axis (PSAX). 
The feature performs the following functions: 
 
During color imaging, positions and sizes the color region of interest (ROI) over the cardiac 
anatomy on the image, for example, the mitral and aortic valves. 
 
During Doppler imaging, positions the Doppler gate on the image. 
 
Displays the name of the cardiac view and the selections for anatomy area, for example, 
apical three chamber (A3C). 
 
Progresses through a predefined sequence of anatomy areas. 
Use the configuration settings to select the default activation for the feature and to define the 
anatomy and sequence for each cardiac view. 
See also: For a list of supported cardiac views and anatomy areas, refer to Appendix D in the 
System Reference. 
You can activate AI Assist for TTE only with compatible transducers and image presets. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and image presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 3 
Overview 
Prerequisite: To avoid technique-related artifacts, you must be thoroughly familiar with the 
techniques of 3D and 4D imaging. Read this entire chapter before performing 3D or 4D imaging. 
The cardiac volume imaging feature includes controls and parameters for optimizing three-
dimensional (3D) images and 4D continuously acquired clips. 
Volume imaging is a collection of sequential, parallel 2D-mode images also referred to as a 
volumetric data set. You can acquire the data in a continuous acquisition (4D). The volumetric 
data set creates a volume rendering and multiplanar reconstructions. 
Multiplanar reconstructions are two-dimensional image planes of the volume for simultaneous 
visualization of orthogonal scan planes and include imaging planes not obtainable by adjusting 
the transducer position during 2D-mode imaging, for example, the short axis (SAX) plane. A 
multiplanar reconstruction is also referred to as a plane or an arbitrary slice of the volume. 
Volume imaging includes settings and tools for defining the multiplanar reconstructions and 
volume, including shaping the volume and repositioning planes and volumes for visualization of 
otherwise occluded anatomical structures. The multislice function also provides simultaneous 
review of the anatomy of interest in parallel slices. 
You can activate cardiac volume imaging only with compatible transducers and studies. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and image presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use. 
See also: For instructions on using a catheter transducer, refer to the manufacturer's user manual for 
the catheter.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 4 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Workflow 
The clinical workflow for cardiac volume imaging includes setup, acquisition, and post-
acquisition steps. 
Step 1: Setting Up for Acquisition 
 
Connect a compatible transducer to the ultrasound system. 
 
Optimize the image while scanning during 2D-mode or 2D-mode with color. 
– 
Select a cardiac image preset. 
– 
Adjust the imaging parameters for the transducer. 
 
Define the volume and planes. 
– 
Size and position the region of interest to acquire large or small areas within the 2D 
field of view and volume rendering (VR). 
– 
Adjust the orientation of the volume and multiplanar reconstructions. 
Note: The area of interest in 4D acquisition matches the orientation of the 2D-mode image. 
Step 2: Acquiring and Viewing the Volume 
 
During 4D imaging, the ultrasound system processes the imaging data and simultaneously 
displays the volume and multiplanar reconstructions in real-time. 
– 
Optimize 4D images, for example, resize the VR and adjust imaging parameters to 
emphasize volume data. 
– 
Temporarily pause 4D acquisition to review the volume in CINE playback. 
– 
Store volumes and clips. 
Step 3: Reviewing and Storing Volumes 
 
Review the volume in CINE playback. 
 
View and define anatomical structures in the multiplanar reconstructions and volume. 
 
Measure structures in the multiplanar reconstructions. 
 
Annotate multiplanar reconstructions or volumes. 
 
Store volumes and clips.

Each 4D acquisition produces a volume rendering and multiplanar reconstructions. 
4D Acquisition 
During 4D acquisition, the ultrasound system processes the volume data and displays a volume 
rendering, providing a real-time view of the three-dimensional image as you scan. 
You can adjust settings during 4D acquisition to enhance visualization of anatomy within the 
volume rendering. You can also temporarily pause volume acquisition to play back and review 
CINE data at any time during 4D acquisition.

Prerequisite: Set up for acquisition of a 4D volume. 
1. 
Press 4D, if necessary. 
The ultrasound system continuously acquires and displays the volume and multiplanar 
reconstructions on the image screen.

Reviewing a Volume in CINE Playback 
You can review a volume in CINE playback from a paused or completed 4D acquisition, or a 
retrieved stored volume. 
Cardiac volume imaging supports the following CINE functionality: 
 
Adjusting the left and right margin of the CINE frame set. 
 
Selecting frames or beats for CINE review. 
 
Viewing the current position of the end diastole or end systole. 
 
Playing back and editing clips and volumes, including adjusting the playback speed. 
 
Repositioning the current frame marker on the ECG trace when playback is paused. 
Note: A horizontal line displays on the time axis when ECG trace data is unavailable. 
 
Capturing clips and static volumes.

Blue

of the MPRs on the volume

views

the volume

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 12 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Rotating the Volume and Multiplanar Reconstructions 
Rotation of the volume enables visualization of an anatomical structure from any angle. The 
volume rotates independently of the multiplanar reconstructions. 
In each multiplanar reconstruction, the rotation of a plane is along the intersecting axis of 
another plane. You can synchronize the position of the volume to the position of any multiplanar 
reconstruction. 
Note: When imaging with a transesophageal transducer in Dual V, the volumes rotate in opposite 
directions. 
To 
Do This 
Freely rotate the volume 
 Rotate a control: 
– X rotates the volume around the x axis. 
– Y rotates the volume around the y axis. 
– Z rotates the volume around the z axis. 
Rotate the volume on the X-Y axis 
1. Press a trackball key to select 3D Rotate, if necessary. Or, position 
the pointer over the inner 90% of the volume viewport to activate 3D 
rotation and then press a trackball key. 
The 3D rotate icon displays on the volume image. 
 
2. Roll the trackball to rotate the volume. 
3. To deactivate the tool, press a trackball key. 
Rotate the volume around the Z axis 
1. Press UPDATE, if necessary, to select Pointer. 
2. Position the pointer over the outer 10% of the volume viewport. 
The volume Z rotation icon displays on the volume image. 
 
3. Press a trackball key and then roll the trackball. 
4. To deactivate the tool, press a trackball key.

Magnifying or Panning an Area of Interest 
You can magnify or pan an area of interest in the volume during 4D acquisition or review.

volume

of intersection.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 16 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Enhanced Resolution Imaging 
The 4D Zoom feature enhances the lateral and elevational resolution of the volume rendering. 
The 4D Z indicator displays below the image when 4D Zoom setup or 4D Zoom is active. 
To enhance the volume: 
1. 
Tap 4D Zoom. Or, during volume imaging, press ZOOM. 
An orange icon on the touch screen button indicates 4D Zoom setup is active. 
2. 
Reposition or resize the region of interest (ROI), if necessary. 
a. 
Press a trackball key, if necessary.  
 
Position indicates the trackball is assigned to repositioning the ROI. 
 
Size indicates the trackball is assigned to resizing the ROI. 
 
Elev Size indicates the trackball is assigned to resizing the elevation of the ROI. 
b. 
Roll the trackball to adjust the ROI and then press a trackball key. 
c. 
To adjust the ROI elevational position of the right plane, rotate Elev Position. 
3. 
Tap 4D Zoom again to display the 4D Zoom image. Or, press UPDATE. 
A white icon on the touch screen button indicates 4D Zoom is active. 
4. 
To return to 4D Zoom setup, tap 4D Zoom again. 
An orange icon on the touch screen button indicates 4D Zoom setup is active. 
5. 
To exit 4D Zoom to 4D, press ZOOM.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 17 
Adjusting Imaging Parameters 
You can adjust the imaging parameters to optimize the volume. 
See also: For information about adjusting general and color imaging parameters, refer to Chapter 8 
in the Instructions for Use. 
To adjust imaging parameters: 
 
Select the required tab, if necessary. 
– 
4D provides optimization selections during 4D volume imaging. 
– 
Color (4D) provides optimization selections during 4D volume imaging with color. 
Note: Imaging selections available for optimization are indicated on the touch screen in color; 
dimmed selections are unavailable. 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the gain (increase or decrease 
the brightness of the displayed image) 
 Rotate 4D. 
Adjust the overall contrast resolution 
(dynamic range) 
 Rotate DR. 
Select a processing curve for assigning 
echo amplitudes to gray levels in the 
image 
 Press Maps to select an option and then rotate the control to select 
a map. 
– MPR applies the selected map to the multiplanar 
reconstructions. 
– Volume applies the selected map to the volume. 
Optimize the volume rendering 
 Tap Volume Enhance and then select a setting. 
The system excludes low-level signal data and adjusts the opacity 
and transparency of the volume image. 
Change the thickness of the slices 
 Rotate MPR Thickness to select a setting: 
– Off indicates a thickness of zero. 
– Thickness settings are in 1 mm increments and range from 0 mm 
to 20 mm. 
Activate biplane imaging 
 Tap Bi-Plane+. 
See also: For information about biplane imaging, refer to 
Chapter D6 in this manual. 
Activate the 4D Heart AI feature 
(Available only during CINE playback or exam review) 
 Tap 4D Heart AI. 
See also: For information about 4D Heart AI, refer to Chapter D4 in 
this manual.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 19 
Displaying Parallel Slices with Multislice 
The multislice function enables simultaneous review of anatomy of interest in multiple parallel 
slices of a multiplanar reconstruction. 
You can view slices of a 3D volume or freeze and then view a 4D volume CINE sequence with 
the multislice function. 
The point of intersection is the location of the central slice and is relative to the active 
multiplanar reconstruction. Parallel slices displaying in the multislice layout are planes in front of 
and behind the central slice. 
 
Example of the reference MPR with lines representing the slices available for viewing. 
1 
Numbers on the lines correspond to the numbers on the slices shown in the layout. 
2 
MPR line indicators with arrows indicating the view direction 
3 
A yellow line indicates the position of the active slice. 
In this example, the active slice is labeled with a zero to indicate the relationship of the other slices 
available for viewing. 
4 
White lines indicate the slices shown in the selected layout. 
A dashed white line indicates the slice is not visible in the selected layout.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 21 
Removing Data from a Volume 
Remove data to enable visualization of anatomical structures within a volume. Rotation of the 
volume and planes can help you visualize an anatomical structure and determine the position of 
the shapes to draw and remove from the volume. 
Shaping a Volume with Cut Plane 
The cut plane function enables removal of 4D data from the volume rendering (VR) using a 
plane oriented and synchronized with a multiplanar reconstruction (MPR). 
To shape a volume with cut plane: 
1. 
Tap Cut Plane. 
A border representing the MPR displays in the volume viewport. The color of the border 
identifies the MPR. 
2. 
Roll the trackball to pan the MPR line and remove extraneous data from volume. 
3. 
To show or hide the wireframe border around the volume rendering, tap Cut Plane 
Wireframe. 
Shaping a Volume with Color Crop 
The color crop function aligns the cropping of color data to the cropping of 4D data in the VR. 
To shape a volume with color crop: 
Prerequisite: Activate color during cardiac volume imaging. Shape a volume with cut plane. 
1. 
Tap Color Crop. 
The system crops color data outside the cut plane in the volume rendering. 
2. 
To disable the function, tap Color Crop again.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 22 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Shaping a Volume with Free Plane 
The free plane function enables visualization within a volume rendering of anatomy of interest 
visible in a multiplanar reconstruction but not visible on the surface of the volume. 
As you reposition the free plane, the system crops the volume rendering to enable visualization 
of the anatomy of interest. Retaining the crop shapes and updates the volume rendering. 
The position of the free plane on the volume rendering displays as a synchronized line on each 
multiplanar reconstruction. 
The color of the free plane indicates the orientation of the plane in relation to the volume. 
 
Orange indicates the free plane is behind the volume. 
 
Turquoise indicates the free plane is in front of the volume. 
To shape a volume with free plane: 
 
Tap Free Plane. 
The free plane displays to the left of the volume. 
 
To 
Do This 
Visualize anatomy of interest within 
the volume 
1. Press UPDATE to select Free Plane, if necessary. 
– Pointer indicates the trackball is assigned to the pointer function. 
– 3D Rotate indicates the trackball is assigned to rotating the 
volume on the X-Y axis. 
– Free Plane indicates the trackball is assigned to the free plane for 
shaping the volume. 
– (Available only during CINE playback or review) Cine indicates the 
trackball is assigned to scrolling CINE data. 
2. Roll the trackball to rotate the volume or reposition the free plane. 
Define the distance of the plane from 
the center of the volume 
 Rotate Position Plane. 
Rotate the free plane 
 Press Rotate Plane to select an option and then rotate the control to 
rotate the free plane. 
– X rotates the free plane around the X axis. 
– Y rotates the free plane around the Y axis. 
Reshape the volume by removing the 
cropped data 
 Tap Retain Crop. 
Note: You can retain multiple crops to visualize the anatomy of 
interest within the volume. 
Restore the most recently cropped 
data to the volume rendering 
(Available only after retaining a crop) 
 Tap Undo Crop. 
Remove all cropping and display the 
original volume rendering 
 Tap Reset Cropping.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 23 
Shaping a Volume with Single V 
The Single V function enables a region of interest (ROI) box for shaping the volume rendering 
during real-time imaging, on a frozen image, or in review. 
Note: The Dual V function is available after activating Single V. 
To shape a volume with Single V: 
1. 
Tap Single V. 
The start point displays on MPR A. 
2. 
Define the shape of the volume. 
a. 
Roll the trackball to position the start point and then press a trackball key. 
Note: You can adjust the width and orientation after setting the start point. 
b. 
Roll the trackball to position the end point. 
 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the width of the volume 
 Rotate Box Width. 
Rotate the volume 
See also: For information about rotating the volume, refer to 
page D2-12. 
Note: During Dual V, the two volumes rotate in opposite directions. 
Reshape the volume 
1. Press UPDATE to activate Edit Single V. 
2. Press a trackball key to select an option, if necessary. 
– Set Start indicates the trackball is assigned to repositioning the 
start point of the ROI box. 
– Set End indicates the trackball is assigned to repositioning the 
end point of the ROI box. 
Turquoise identifies the active point on the ROI box. 
3. Roll the trackball to adjust the ROI box and then press a trackball 
key. 
4. Accept the shape and position. 
Restore the volume to the original 
shape and position 
 Tap Reset to Start. 
 Tap Single V. 
 Tap Dual V. 
Note: During Dual V, both volumes reset to the start position. 
Accept the shape and position and 
exit the feature 
 Press UPDATE to select Accept. 
 Tap Single V again.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 25 
Storing and Printing Images 
You can convert a volume to a DICOM multi-frame clip and store clips of the currently displayed 
volume. 
You can capture and store single-frame volumes. 
You can print individual images of a multiplanar reconstruction or a volume. A volume is a 
sequence of multiple-frame images and cannot be printed as a range of images. 
Use the patient browser to transfer volumes to external storage devices. 
See also: For additional information on capturing images and clips, refer to Chapter 5 in the 
Instructions for Use. 
See also: For information on recording a patient study, refer to Chapter 13 in the Instructions for 
Use. 
To store a volume as a clip: 
 
Press CAPTURE. Or, press the control assigned to the clip store function. 
The system displays an icon on the image. 
 
See also: For information about CINE and clip capture settings, refer to Chapter 7 in the Instructions 
for Use. 
Use the configuration settings to define additional clip capture settings for 4D volumes. 
To save a single frame of a volume: 
Note: The volume data is not stored when you store or print an image. You must store the volume for 
future review of the volume. 
 
Press FREEZE and then press CAPTURE. 
The system displays an icon on the image.

D2 - 26 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Exporting a Volume as an Image 
See also: For information about exporting and importing patient data, refer to Chapter B2 in this 
manual. 
Retrieving Stored Volumes 
You can select a patient study from the local database for review of multiplanar reconstructions 
and volume renderings. 
See also: For information on loading a patient study for review, refer to Chapter 5 in the Instructions 
for Use. 
Exporting and Importing Acoustic Data 
Use the DICOM configuration settings for exporting and importing acoustic data with images or 
clips. 
Exporting 3D Cartesian Data 
Use the DICOM configuration settings to export cardiac 3D single-frame volume images as 
Cartesian data. 
Performing a Measurement 
You can perform a 2D-mode measurement on an individual multiplanar reconstruction while an 
acquisition is frozen, after acquisition is complete, or during review. You cannot perform a 
measurement on a volume. 
See also: For information about performing a measurement, refer to Chapter 10 in the Instructions 
for Use. 
See also: For information about using the 3D Caliper tool, refer to Chapter 11 in the Instructions for 
Use. 
Creating a User-Defined Image Preset 
You can create a user-defined image preset to capture the optimized 3D and 4D imaging 
settings. 
See also: For information on creating or editing a user-defined image preset, refer to Chapter 8 in 
the Instructions for Use.

D3  2D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D3 - 3 
Overview 
 WARNING: This feature uses ultrasound data collected prior to analysis. The quality of the data 
collected and used as input could have an effect on the output of this feature. Variability in 
ultrasound system performance, operator technique, patient characteristics, and other factors 
may affect the output. At all times, the clinician is advised to carefully review the output and 
confirm the information presented with clinical judgment and any other relevant sources of data. 
2D Heart AI 
The 2D Heart AI feature performs left and right heart volume measurements using 2D-mode 
data from two image frames. The feature detects and traces the contours of the endocardial 
borders on the end-diastolic (ED) and end-systolic (ES) images in an apical four-chamber 
(A4C), apical three-chamber (A3C), or apical two-chamber (A2C) view. 
Use the 2D Heart AI feature to perform the following tasks: 
 
Detect, contour, and analyze the left ventricle, right ventricle, left atrium, and right atrium. 
 
Detect and analyze end diastole (ED) and end systole (ES) and display ED-ES images in a 
side-by-side format. 
 
Edit or manually trace the contours. 
 
Analyze the results summary. 
2D Heart+ AI 
The 2D Heart+ AI feature includes all 2D Heart AI functionality. 
The 2D Heart+ AI feature visualizes, measures, and assesses myocardial motion and 
mechanics using acquired 2D clips during live imaging or from review. 
2D Heart+ AI tracks and estimates tissue velocity and other motion and deformation 
parameters on every frame in the cardiac cycle and illustrates tissue velocity and direction and 
provides quantitative data for velocity, displacement, strain, and strain rate. 
The tracking results summary, curve graph, and bullseye plot are based on every frame in the 
cardiac cycle. 
Use the 2D Heart+ AI feature to perform all tasks available with 2D Heart AI and the following 
tasks: 
 
Detect the apical two, three, and four chamber views. 
 
Track the contours of the left ventricle and the left atrium throughout the cardiac cycle. 
 
Analyze and compare up to three clips. 
 
Analyze the tracking results summary, curve graph, and bullseye plot. 
 
Perform strain analysis with contrast for the left ventricle. 
See also: For information about contrast agent imaging, refer to Chapter A3 in this manual.

content:
D3  2D Heart AI 
D3 - 4 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Workflow 
The clinical workflow includes the following steps. 
Step 1: Acquiring Cardiac Views 
 
During imaging, acquire clips of cardiac views with an ECG trace (a physio signal is 
present). 
Acquire up to five heart beats for analysis and include a minimum of one full R-R capture. 
Note: If available, include an additional heart beat or R-R acquisition. If necessary, optimize the 
ECG trace before activating the feature. 
See also: For information about using the physiologic function, refer to Chapter C1 in this 
manual. 
 
During imaging, acquire clips of cardiac views without an ECG trace (no physio signal). 
Note: If the feature does not identify ED and ES frames, you must identify the required end 
diastolic (ED) and end systolic (ES) frames to obtain analysis with contours and results. The 
feature analyzes a single beat without physio.  
 
During review, open the required cardiac clips. 
Step 2: Detecting and Analyzing the Cardiac Chambers 
 
To analyze the left and right heart chambers, freeze the image. 
 
To analyze the heart chambers, review a previously acquired cardiac clip, a group of 
chamber views, or an individual chamber view. 
 
2D Heart AI detects the view, places contours, analyzes the 2D ultrasound data, and 
displays the results. 
Note: Available results are dependent on the acquired views. 
Step 3: Reviewing, Adjusting, and Saving the Results 
 
2D Heart AI 
– 
Displays a two-frame analysis with contoured heart chambers in the ED-ES view. 
 
2D Heart+ AI 
– 
Displays apical chamber viewports (A4C, A2C, A3C). 
– 
Displays global longitudinal strain (GLS) in a curve graph and bullseye plot for the left 
ventricle and left atrium. 
– 
Displays tracking results, including volume, ejection fraction, cardiac output, stroke 
volume, GLS, quantitative data, for example, velocity and strain rate. 
– 
Provides viewports, a curve graph, a bullseye plot, and a tracking results summary for 
review. 
 
Confirm the contour placement and manually edit the contours, if necessary. 
 
Confirm and adjust the tracking parameters, if necessary. 
 
Save the tracking results.

content:
D3  2D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D3 - 9 
Activating 2D Heart AI 
You can activate 2D Heart AI from the review function or during imaging with a compatible 
transducer and imaging preset. 
See also: For information about activating review, refer to Chapter B1 in this manual. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and imaging presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use. 
Prior to activating the feature, perform the following prerequisites, as applicable. 
 
During live imaging in 2D-mode, obtain an apical view and then freeze the image. 
– 
When an ECG trace is not available, the ED-ES Assist feature assesses a single beat, 
and the ED and ES frames are determined by largest and smallest sizes of the left 
ventricle. 
See also: For information on obtaining a physio signal, refer to Chapter C1 in this manual. 
 
Cardiac clips include at least five frames of 2D-mode data. If the clip contains more than 
700 frames, the feature analyzes the first 700 frames acquired. 
 
Single heart beat analysis requires confirmation of the end diastolic and end systolic 
frames. 
 
For 2D Heart+ AI, select up to three apical views to analyze the left ventricle and 
left atrium. 
To activate 2D Heart AI: 
To 
Do This 
Analyze the heart chambers in CINE 
1. During live imaging in 2D-mode, acquire the required apical view and 
then press FREEZE. 
2. Tap 2D Heart AI. 
The ultrasound system displays a progress bar as the feature 
activates, and the feature detects the contours, calculates the results, 
and displays the ED-ES view layout. 
Analyze a single clip or view in review 
Prerequisite: Acquire the required cardiac clips. 
1. Activate review. 
2. Tap Single Select. 
3. Select only one of the following apical views: A4C, A3C, A2C. 
4. Tap 2D Heart AI. 
The ultrasound system displays a progress bar as the feature 
activates, and the feature detects the contours, calculates the results, 
and displays the ED-ES view layout.

D3  2D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D3 - 11 
Detecting ED and ES Frames with ED-ES Assist 
The ED-ES Assist feature assesses a single beat and determines the end diastolic (ED) and 
end systolic (ES) frames using the largest and smallest sizes of the left ventricle. 
The feature activates during 2D Heart AI when an ECG trace is not available. 
You can also activate ED-ES Assist to analyze the final three seconds of a clip and obtain 
system-identified ED and ES frames. 
If the ED or ES key frames are not detected, you can analyze manually set key frames. 
To set key frames with ED-ES Assist: 
 
Tap ED-ES Assist. 
The feature detects the ED and ES key frames, displays a notification indicating the 
key frames are set by ED-ES Assist, and updates the results. 
If the feature is unable to detect the key frames, the system prompts you to set the 
key frames. 
To analyze manually set key frames: 
Prerequisite: Select the ED and ES key frames. 
See also: For information about positioning and assigning ED and ES frames, refer to Chapter 7 in 
the Instructions for Use. 
 
Tap Analyze. 
The system displays the summary view and the results.

content:
D3  2D Heart AI 
D3 - 12 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Analyzing the Results 
Saving the Results 
You can save the results to the patient report. After edits and updates are complete, be sure to 
reconfirm the results before saving the results to the report. 
To save the results to the report: 
1. 
Perform manual adjustments to the contours or tracking parameters, if necessary, and then 
confirm the results. 
2. 
Press the control assigned to the clip store function. 
Adjusting the Tracking Parameters 
Use the configuration settings to define the default parameters for analysis. 
Note: An asterisk (*) displays next to results with manual adjustments. 
To 
Do This 
Analyze a different number of heart beats 
(Available only for multiple beats) 
 Tap Beats Analyzed and then select the number of beats, up to five. 
The results display an average of the selected number of beats or an 
individual beat analysis. 
Note: Increasing the number of beats moves the ECG margin to the 
left to include prior beats. If the clip does not include the selected 
number of beats, the system analyzes the available beats. 
Exclude a heart beat from the analysis 
(Available only for multiple beats) 
 Select the beat and then tap Exclude Beat. 
The system removes the selected beat, including the contour and 
results. 
The results identify the excluded beat, for example, if the second beat 
is excluded, the results display *Beats Excluded: 2. 
 To include the beat, tap Exclude Beat again. 
Analyze an average of heart beats 
 Tap Average Result. 
An average of the beats displays in the results. 
The results indicate the number of beats averaged, for example, 
Average (3 beats). 
 To analyze individual beats, tap Average Result again. 
The results indicate the beat analyzed, for example, Beat 3 of 3. 
Analyze another heart beat  
1. Press Cine to select Beats, if necessary. 
2. Rotate Cine to select another location in the ECG trace. 
The beat in analysis displays in the viewports. 
Select the end diastolic and end systolic 
frames 
See also: For information about repositioning ED and ES markers and 
assigning ED and ES frames, refer to Chapter 7 in the Instructions for 
Use.

content:
D3  2D Heart AI 
D3 - 14 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
To 
Do This 
Select the timing or phase for the bullseye 
view 
(Available only for the left ventricle) 
1. Tap Curve and then select Segmental Strain. 
2. Tap Timing / Phase and then select an option. 
– Peak Systolic Strain (PSS) displays the peak strain value during 
systole as measured before aortic valve closure. 
– End Systolic Strain (ESS) displays the strain value at end systole 
measured at aortic valve closure. 
– Time to Peak (TTP) displays the time to reach peak strain. 
– Post Systolic Strain (PS) displays the strain value after end 
systole as measured after aortic valve closure. 
– Post Systolic Indexed (PSI) displays the ratio between strain 
(deformation) after end systole divided by total strain. 
Select the curve for the bullseye view 
 Tap Curve and then select an option. 
Note: All options are available for the left ventricle. Only Volume and 
Global Strain are available for the left atrium. 
– Volume displays the change in chamber volume from end diastole 
to end systole as derived from the left ventricle and left atrium. 
– Segmental Strain displays the average strain value in each 
segment of the cardiac chamber, for example, the left ventricle. 
Note: Selecting segmental strain when the left ventricle is 
disabled, changes the curve to volume. 
– Global Strain displays the overall global strain or deformation for 
the left ventricle and left atrium. 
– Strain Rate indicates the rate of strain or how fast the deformation 
occurs for the left ventricle.

content:
D3  2D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D3 - 15 
Editing the Contours 
The 2D Heart AI feature displays contours for editing only on the end diastolic and end systolic 
frames for each heart chamber in the ED-ES view. You can manually adjust or delete and 
redraw the system-generated contours. When the contour is complete, the system reanalyzes 
the contour and updates the results. 
Note: You can also manually draw the contours if the system could not detect the contours. 
To edit a contour: 
 
Click the required viewport in the ED-ES view. 
 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the brightness of the contour 
 Rotate Contour Brightness. 
Show or hide the contours 
 Tap Hide Contours. 
Edit a contour 
1. Click the required viewport, if necessary. 
2. Position the pointer to activate the required segment of the contour. 
The segment displays in yellow with the active section in red. 
3. Move the pointer to adjust the contour and then click the image to 
anchor the contour. 
– To edit a smaller section of the contour, move the pointer near the 
contour. 
– To edit a larger section of the contour, move the pointer further 
from the contour. 
The segment displays in green(LV), blue (LA), yellow (RV), or 
turquoise (RA) as you adjust the contour.  
4. Click a trackball key to anchor the placement. 
Delete a contour 
 Tap Delete Contour and then select the chamber: LA, LV, RA, RV. 
The system deletes the selected contour and then displays options 
for manually adding a contour. 
Draw a contour 
1. Select a chamber and then tap Add Contour, if necessary. 
The system displays a message at the bottom of the image screen 
instructing the points to mark for drawing the contour. 
See also: On-Screen Messages, page D3-20 
2. Roll the trackball to position the first marker and then press a 
trackball key to set the position. 
3. Roll the trackball to position the second marker and then press a 
trackball key to set the position. 
4. Roll the trackball to position the third marker and then press a 
trackball key to set the position. 
The system draws the contour on the selected chamber. 
Undo the previous edit, deletion, or 
addition to a contour 
 Tap Undo. 
Note: You can undo up to ten changes.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D4 - 3 
Overview 
 WARNING: This feature uses ultrasound data collected prior to analysis. The quality of the data 
collected and used as input could have an effect on the output of this feature. Variability in 
ultrasound system performance, operator technique, patient characteristics, and other factors 
may affect the output. At all times, the clinician is advised to carefully review the output and 
confirm the information presented with clinical judgment and any other relevant sources of data. 
The 4D Heart AI feature is a four-dimensional (4D) image processing feature for detecting, 
evaluating, and quantifying the shape, size, and function of the heart chambers. The feature 
provides volume and strain analysis. 
4D Heart AI detects the cardiac view, identifies borders (contours), and measures cardiac 
function for the left ventricle, left atrium, right ventricle, and right atrium. Contours indicate the 
positions of the three-dimensional (3D) model for the multiplanar reconstructions (MPR) or 
volume slice. 
Measurement results are based on contours from the end diastole (ED) and end systole (ES) 
frames. 
Use the feature to perform the following tasks: 
 
Visualize the left ventricle and left atrium and quantitative analysis of ejection fraction, 
volumes, and mechanical dyssynchrony. 
 
Visualize the right ventricle and right atrium for evaluation and quantification of size and 
function. 
 
Confirm the contour placement and make any adjustments, if necessary. 
 
Analyze measurement results based on 4D volume ultrasound data. 
Data is available in multiple formats: a curve graph for measurements over time, a bullseye 
plot with a graphical representation of the heart, and a textual report format. 
 
Analyze a single heart beat after confirming end diastole and end systole frames. 
 
Analyze all frames of the cardiac cycle for multiple beats captured during a physio study 
using a visual representation of heart motion and function. 
See also: For information about using the physiologic function, refer to Chapter C1 in this 
manual. 
Use the configuration settings to customize the default settings for the 4D Heart AI feature. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and imaging presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
D4 - 4 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Workflow 
The clinical workflow includes the following steps. 
Step 1: Acquiring Cardiac 4D Volumes 
 
During cardiac 4D volume imaging, freeze the image. 
 
During review, open the required cardiac 4D volume clips. 
Note: For volume clips in review, tracking is only available for the left ventricle and left atrium 
chambers. 
 
4D volume imaging or clips can include an ECG trace (a physio signal is present) or 
exclude an ECG trace (no physio signal). 
See also: For information about using the physiologic function, refer to Chapter C1 in this 
manual. 
Note: Without a physio signal, the feature analyzes only one beat. You must identify the ED and 
ES frames and select analyze for detection. 
Step 2: Detecting and Analyzing the Cardiac Chambers 
 
4D Heart AI detects the view, places contours across all frames for the selected beats, 
analyzes the 4D ultrasound data, and displays the results. 
Note: Available results are dependent on the acquired views. 
Step 3: Reviewing, Adjusting, and Saving the Results 
 
Analyze the results for single or multiple heart chambers. 
 
Select a heart chamber or beat to analyze. 
 
Select different view layouts: ED-ES, detailed, or bullseye. 
Note: Bullseye view is only available for cardiac 4D volume clips in review. 
 
View the multiplanar reconstruction or volume from another orientation. 
 
Redefine the diastolic or systolic frame. 
 
Edit, delete, or redraw contours on the LV, LA, RV, or RA. 
 
Reanalyze the views to update the results. 
 
Review the clips or volume in playback. 
 
Save the tracking results.

Advanced Imaging Manual 
Activating 4D Heart AI 
You can activate 4D Heart AI during 4D cardiac volume imaging or from the review function. 
See also: For information about cardiac volume imaging, refer to Chapter D2 in this manual. 
See also: For information about activating review, refer to Chapter B1 in this manual. 
To activate 4D Heart AI: 
To 
Do This 
Analyze the heart chambers during live 
imaging in 4D-mode 
1. Activate cardiac volume imaging. 
2. Acquire the required view and then press FREEZE. 
3. Tap 4D Heart AI. 
The ultrasound system displays a progress bar as the feature activates, 
and the feature detects the contours, calculates the results, and displays 
the ED-ES view. 
Analyze the heart chambers during 
review 
Prerequisite: Acquire the required cardiac clips. 
1. Activate review. 
2. Select the required volume clip. 
 
Example of an icon identifying a volume clip in the thumbnail panel. 
3. Tap 4D Heart AI. 
The ultrasound system displays a progress bar as the feature activates, 
and the feature detects the contours, calculates the results, and displays 
the ED-ES view.
