content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D4 - 11 
Analyzing the Results 
Saving the Results 
You can save the results to the patient report. After edits and updates are complete, be sure to 
reconfirm the results before saving the results to the report. 
To save the results to the report: 
1. 
Confirm the results after performing any manual adjustments to the contours or tracking 
parameters, if necessary. 
2. 
Press the control assigned to the clip store function. 
Adjusting the Analysis Parameters 
Use the configuration settings to define the default parameters for analysis. 
Note: An asterisk (*) displays next to results with manual adjustments. 
To 
Do This 
Analyze a different number of 
heart beats 
(Available only for multiple beats) 
 Tap Beats Analyzed and then select the number of beats, up to five. 
The results display an average of the selected number of beats. 
Note: Increasing the number of beats moves the ECG margin to the left 
to include prior beats. If the clip does not include the selected number of 
beats, the system analyzes the available beats. 
Exclude a heart beat from the analysis 
(Available only for multiple beats) 
 Select the beat and then tap Exclude Beat. 
The system removes the selected beat, including the contour, results, 
aortic valve closure (AVC) time, pre-atrial (Pre-A) contraction time, and 
bullseye plot. 
The results identify the excluded beat, for example, if the second beat is 
excluded, the results display *Beats Excluded: 2. 
 To include the beat, tap Exclude Beat again. 
Analyze an average of heart beats 
 Tap Average Result. 
An average of the beats displays in the results. 
The results indicate the number of beats averaged, for example, 
Average (3 beats). 
 To analyze individual beats, tap Average Result again. 
The results indicate the beat analyzed, for example, Beat 3 of 3. 
Analyze another heart beat 
 Rotate Cine to select another location in the ECG trace and then tap 
Analyze. 
The beat in analysis displays in the viewports.

Advanced Imaging Manual 
To

Select the end diastolic and 
end systolic frames 
See also: For information about repositioning ED and ES markers and 
assigning ED and ES frames, refer to Chapter 7 in the Instructions for Use. 
Show or hide the left ventricle (LV) 
epicardium 
Prerequisite: Display the LV viewport. 
 Tap LV Epi. 
The model shows the epicardium in mesh, and the LV mass updates in 
the results. 
 To remove the mesh, tap LV Epi again. 
Excluding the mesh enables visualization of the segments on the LV 
endocardium model. 
Adjust the aortic valve closure time 
(Available only for the left ventricle when the clip is frozen in bullseye view) 
 Rotate AVC to adjust the time in milliseconds (ms). 
The values update in the report summary. 
Note: During analysis of multiple beats, the aortic valve closure time 
displays only for the current beat. 
Adjust the pre-atrial contraction time at 
the onset of the P-wave 
(Available only for the left atrium when the clip is frozen in bullseye view) 
 Rotate Pre-A to adjust the time in milliseconds (ms). 
The values update in the report summary. 
Note: During analysis of multiple beats, the pre-atrial contraction time 
displays only for the current beat. 
Perform a single-beat analysis 
Prerequisite: Acquire volumes with a minimum of one cardiac cycle. 
1. Position the ED and ES markers, if necessary. 
The system calculates and displays the results after you verify the ED 
and ES frames. 
See also: For information about positioning the ED and ES markers, 
refer to Chapter 7 in the Instructions for Use. 
2. Tap Analyze. 
The system displays a progress bar, calculates the results, and updates 
the results summary.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D4 - 13 
To 
Do This 
Select the timing or phase for the 
bullseye view 
(Available only for the left ventricle) 
1. Tap Curve and then select Segmental Strain. 
2. Tap Timing / Phase and then select an option. 
– Peak Systolic Strain (PSS) displays the peak strain value during 
systole as measured before aortic valve closure. 
– End Systolic Strain (ESS) displays the strain value at end systole 
measured at aortic valve closure. 
– Time to Peak (TTP) displays the time to reach peak strain. 
– Post Systolic Strain (PS) displays the strain value after end systole 
as measured after aortic valve closure. 
– Post Systolic Indexed (PSI) displays the ratio between strain 
(deformation) after end systole divided by total strain. 
Select the curve for the bullseye view 
Prerequisite: The left ventricle is required for Segmental Strain. The left 
ventricle and/or left atrium are required for Volume and Global Strain. 
 Tap Curve and then select an option. 
Note: All options are available for the left ventricle. Only Volume and 
Global Strain are available for the left atrium. 
– Volume displays the change in chamber volume from end diastole to 
end systole as derived from the left ventricle and left atrium. 
– Segmental Strain displays the average strain value in each segment 
of the cardiac chamber, for example, the left ventricle. 
Note: Selecting segmental strain when the left ventricle is disabled 
changes the curve to volume. 
– Global Strain displays the overall global strain or deformation for the 
left ventricle and left atrium. 
Change the direction of strain analysis 
for the bullseye view 
(Available only for the left ventricle) 
1. Tap Curve and then select Segmental Strain. 
2. Tap Direction and then select an option. 
– Longitudinal displays the strain results in the longitudinal direction. 
– Circumferential displays the strain results in the circumferential 
direction.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
D4 - 14 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Editing the Contours 
You can manually adjust or delete and redraw the system-generated contours. After the 
contour is drawn, the system reanalyzes the contour and updates the results. 
Note: You can also manually draw the contours if the system could not detect the contours. 
To edit a contour: 
To 
Do This 
Show or hide the contours in the 
selected viewport 
 Tap Hide Contours. 
Edit a contour 
1. Tap Edit Contour. 
2. Select a viewport. Or, press UPDATE. 
3. Position the pointer to activate the required segment of the contour. 
The segment displays in yellow with the active section in red. 
The model displays with mesh. 
4. Move the pointer to adjust the contour and then click the image to 
anchor the contour. 
– To edit a smaller section of the contour, move the pointer near the 
contour. 
– To edit a larger section of the contour, move the pointer further from 
the contour. 
The segment displays in green (LV), blue (LA), yellow (RV), or turquoise 
(RA) as you adjust the contour. 
The mesh on the model repositions as you adjust the contour. 
5. Click a trackball key to anchor the placement. 
Adjust the distance between the 
epicardium mesh and the left ventricle 
(Available only when the left ventricle epicardium mesh is shown) 
1. Tap Edit Contour. 
2. Rotate LV Epi Offset and then select a setting.

D4  4D Heart AI 
D4 - 16 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Changing the Image Screen Layout 
Use the configuration settings to select the default layouts for the 4D Heart AI feature. 
See also: For additional information about changing the image screen layout, refer to Chapter D2 in 
this manual. 
To 
Do This 
Hide or show the volume data in the 
model viewport 
 Tap Hide VR. 
Hide or show the model on the volume 
 Tap Hide Model. 
Show or hide the right ventricle 
 Tap RV. 
Show or hide the right atrium 
 Tap RA. 
Show or hide the left ventricle 
 Tap LV. 
Show or hide the left atrium 
 Tap LA. 
Activate the next viewport 
 Press UPDATE. 
Display the detailed view layout 
 Tap Detailed View. 
Display the ED-ES view layout 
 Tap ED-ES View. 
Display the bullseye view layout 
Prerequisite: Select the left ventricle, or select both the left ventricle and 
the left atrial. Select a heart cycle of one to five beats. 
 Tap Bullseye View. 
See also: For information about the bullseye view, refer to page D4-18. 
Rotating the Volume and Multiplanar Reconstructions 
Rotation of the volume enables visualization of the anatomical structure from any angle. The 
volume rotates independently of the multiplanar reconstructions (MPR). 
During rotation of a multiplanar reconstruction, the rotation of the three orthogonal planes is 
synchronized along the axis of the active plane. You can synchronize the position of the volume 
to the position of any multiplanar reconstruction. 
The axis markers display in the ED-ES and detailed views. 
See also: For information about rotating the volume and multiplanar reconstructions, refer to 
Chapter D2 in this manual. 
Magnifying or Panning an Area of Interest 
(Not available for the bullseye view) 
You can adjust the magnification level for the volume model viewports. You cannot magnify the 
bullseye view. 
See also: For information about rotating the magnifying or panning an area of interest, refer to 
Chapter D2 in this manual.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
D4 - 18 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Reviewing Results in a Bullseye Plot 
(Available only during review) 
Each segment in the bullseye view is represented by a curve in the curve view. 
Note: If all four chambers are active, selecting the bullseye view hides the right ventricle (RV) and 
right atrium (RA). The RV and RA are shown again when accessing the ED-ES or detailed view. 
See also: For information about 4D Heart AI result labels, refer to Appendix D in the System 
Reference. 
To review results in a bullseye plot: 
Prerequisite: Select the left ventricle, or select both the left ventricle and the left atrial. Select a 
heart cycle of one to five beats. 
 
Tap Bullseye View. 
 
To 
Do This 
Activate or deactivate individual 
segments on the bullseye plot 
 Click the required segments in the bullseye plot. 
The analysis results include segments in color and exclude segments 
in gray. The deactivated segments are excluded from the segmental 
strain curve. The deactivated segments display in gray on the volume 
model. 
Display a corresponding segment in 
the volume model and segmental 
strain curve

D5  ICE Workflow 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D5 - 3 
Overview 
The intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) workflow streamlines image optimization and 
measurements during use of a 2D ICE catheter by providing simplified selections on the 
touch screen. 
Access to full controls is available during the study, for example, image optimization selections 
for adjusting the flow angle or the angle of the Doppler cursor. 
You can activate the ICE workflow only with compatible transducers and studies. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and image presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use. 
 
Example of the touch screen with the ICE workflow function during 2D-mode with color. 
1 
Lock screen 
Locks the touch screen and trackball. Pressing the freeze key unlocks the touch screen and trackball. 
2 
Imaging mode, freeze, and capture selections 
3 
Selection for accessing full controls or the ICE workflow 
4 
Size and position controls 
During imaging, provides pinch control for sizing the region of interest (ROI) and drag control for 
positioning the ROI or Doppler cursor 
During the measure function, displays an image of the trackball with a reminder to use the trackball 
when performing measurements 
5 
Plus and minus buttons 
Performs fine adjustments to the region of interest (ROI) 
6 
Slide controls

content:
D5  ICE Workflow 
D5 - 4 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Activating the ICE Workflow 
See also: For information about preparing the catheter and connector for use in an ultrasound exam, 
refer to the instructions for use shipped with your catheter and your catheter connector. 
See also: For information about beginning a study and registering the patient, refer to Chapter 5 in 
the Instructions for Use. 
To activate the ICE workflow: 
Prerequisite: Power on the ultrasound system. Prepare the catheter and connector for use in an 
ultrasound exam. Register the patient and begin the study. 
 
Connect a compatible catheter to the ultrasound system. 
The ultrasound system displays the ICE workflow selections on the touch screen. 
Note: If the selections are not available, activate ICE from the additional selections. 
Freezing the Image 
Freeze the image when the catheter is not in use or prior to performing a measurement. 
To freeze or unfreeze ultrasound imaging: 
 
Tap Freeze. 
 
Tap Freeze again to unfreeze the image and resume imaging. 
Selecting Imaging Modes 
Activate an imaging mode for access to the associated image optimization settings. 
 
2D imaging activates a two-dimensional grayscale image and a grayscale bar on the image 
screen. 
 
Color imaging applies color to the velocities and directions of blood flow within the region of 
interest and displays the color bar on the image screen. 
 
Pulsed wave (PW) Doppler imaging displays a Doppler spectrum below the 2D image and 
Doppler cursor and gate on the image. The cursor represents the acoustic line for 
gathering Doppler information, for example, volume flow data. 
Note: Tap more than one selection to activate combined imaging modes. 
To 
Do This 
Activate 2D imaging 
 Tap 2D. 
Activate or exit color imaging 
 Tap Color. 
 To exit color imaging, tap Color again. 
Activate or exit pulsed wave (PW) Doppler 
 Tap PW. 
 To exit PW Doppler, tap PW again.

D5  ICE Workflow 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D5 - 5 
Optimizing Images 
The ultrasound system retains the image optimization settings when you freeze or unfreeze the 
image or optimize the image with full controls and then activate the ICE workflow. 
Prerequisite: Activate the ICE workflow and begin imaging. Activate the required imaging mode. 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the imaging depth 
 Adjust the Depth setting. 
– Drag the dot on the slide control. 
– Tap a new location on the slide control. 
– Tap the plus button to increase the depth. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the depth. 
Adjust the 2D gain (increase or decrease 
brightness of the image) 
 Adjust the Image Gain setting. 
– Drag the dot on the slide control. 
– Tap a new location on the slide control. 
– Tap the plus button to increase the brightness. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the brightness. 
Adjust the color gain (increase or 
decrease flow detection in the image) 
(Available only during color imaging) 
 Adjust the Color Gain setting. 
– Drag the dot on the slide control. 
– Tap a new location on the slide control. 
– Tap the plus button to increase the amount of color. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the amount of color. 
Enhance the cardiac image 
 Select an Enhance Image setting.

content:
D5  ICE Workflow 
D5 - 6 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Optimizing the Doppler Spectrum 
To display the real-time Doppler spectrum: 
Prerequisite: Activate PW Doppler. 
 
Tap Activate Doppler. 
 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the Doppler gain (increase or 
decrease brightness of the spectrum) 
 Adjust the Doppler Gain setting. 
– Drag the dot on the slide control. 
– Tap a new location on the slide control. 
– Tap the plus button to increase the brightness. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the brightness.  
Adjust the scrolling speed of the Doppler 
spectrum 
 Adjust the Speed setting. 
– Tap the plus button to increase the speed. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the speed. 
Adjust the velocity scale factor of pulse 
repetition frequency (PRF) 
Note: Adjusting PRF may improve velocity range sensitivity or control 
aliasing. 
 Adjust the Scale setting. 
– Tap the plus button to increase PRF. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease PRF. 
Adjust the display of blood flow velocity 
 Adjust the Baseline setting. 
– Tap the plus button to move the baseline upward for emphasis of 
negative velocities. 
– Tap the minus button to move the baseline downward for 
emphasis of positive velocities. 
Adjust the Doppler audio volume 
 Tap a volume selection. 
 
– Tap the plus button to increase the volume. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the volume. 
Note: Activate full controls to access the mute option. 
Pause the Doppler spectrum and refresh 
the 2D image 
 Tap Update.

D5  ICE Workflow 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D5 - 7 
Positioning and Resizing the Area of Interest 
Note: You can also access full controls to perform additional adjustments, for example, adjust the 
angle of the Doppler gate. 
Prerequisite: Activate the imaging mode, if necessary: 2D for the region of interest (ROI), color for 
the color ROI, or Doppler for the Doppler cursor and gate. 
To 
Do This 
Reposition the region of interest (ROI) or 
the color ROI 
 Drag the ROI on the touch screen. 
 Roll the trackball. 
Resize the region of interest (ROI) or the 
color ROI 
Note: When the color ROI is active, the plus and minus buttons include 
the following label: Color Size. 
 Pinch and drag the ROI representation on the touch screen. 
– Vertical pinch and drag resizes the height. 
– Horizontal pinch and drag resizes the width. 
– Angled pinch and drag resizes both the height and width. 
 To perform fine adjustments, press the plus and minus buttons below 
the ROI. 
Reposition the Doppler cursor 
 Drag the Doppler cursor on the touch screen. 
 Roll the trackball. 
Reviewing CINE Playback 
You can review CINE playback on a frozen image. 
To play back CINE data: 
Prerequisite: Freeze the image. 
To 
Do This 
Start continuous playback 
 Tap the play icon. 
 
Stop continuous playback 
 Tap the pause button. 
 
Display one frame to the left 
 Tap the frame-left button. 
 
Display one frame to the right 
 Tap the frame-right button. 
 
Scroll the frames 
 Drag the dot on the slide control.

content:
D5  ICE Workflow 
D5 - 8 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Performing a Measurement 
When you activate the measurement function during the ICE workflow, an image of the 
trackball displays on the touch screen with the prompt: Use Trackball. 
Prerequisite: Freeze the image. 
To 
Do This 
Measure a distance 
(Available during 2D or 2D with color imaging) 
1. Tap New Measure. 
The system places a measurement marker on the frozen 2D image 
and prompts you to use the trackball. 
2. Roll the trackball to position the first marker and then tap 
Set Measure to anchor the marker. 
3. Roll the trackball to position the second marker and then tap 
Set Measure. 
Measure the velocity of a peak waveform 
on a Doppler spectrum (peak velocity) 
(Available during PW Doppler or PW Doppler with color) 
1. Tap Measure Velocity. 
The system places a measurement marker on the frozen waveform 
and prompts you to use the trackball. 
2. Roll the trackball to position the marker on the Doppler waveform and 
then tap Set Measure. 
Delete a measurement 
 Tap Delete Measure. 
Storing Images 
You can capture and store images or clips during the ICE workflow. 
 
During live imaging, you can acquire and save a clip. 
 
During system freeze, you can save an image of the current CINE frame. 
 
During CINE playback, you can save a clip from the current CINE margins. 
To store an image or clip: 
 
Tap Capture. 
An icon briefly displays on the touch screen indicating the capture is complete.

D6  Single Plane and Biplane Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D6 - 3 
Overview 
You can image a single plane or two planes with a 4D volume transducer during a study. 
 
Single plane imaging displays a scan plane indicator on the image screen. 
– 
The starting angle of a single plane is 0°. 
 
Biplane imaging displays a scan plane indicator and two scan plane images in side-by-side 
format on the image screen. 
– 
The image on the left is the reference plane. The reference plane displays the tilt line 
and tilt indicator in turquoise. 
– 
The image on the right rotates and tilts in relation to the reference plane. 
You can activate biplane imaging only with compatible transducers and studies. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and image presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use. 
Adjustment of the rotation and tilt angle is dependent on the transducer. 
Use the configuration settings to specify the default rotation and angle settings for each volume 
transducer. 
Scan Plane Indicator during Single Plane Imaging 
A scan plane indicator displays on the image screen with the orientation of the scan direction 
for the plane and rotation angle.  
The dot on the angle indicator indicates the starting point for image acquisition.

default scan plane.

clockwise.

mirrored scan plane.

Advanced Imaging Manual 
Rotating the Scan Plane 
(Not available for the AcuNav Lumos 4D ICE catheter) 
You can rotate the scan plane during imaging with a volume transducer. The scan plane start 
position is 0° and includes rotation from 0° to 359°. 
As the scan plane rotates, the system updates the rotation angle and angle indicator on the 
scan plane indicator. 
Use the configuration settings to limit or extend the range of scan plane rotation. 
To rotate the scan plane: 
Prerequisite: Select a compatible transducer and image preset. Select the 2D or Color tab. 
1. 
Press Angle, if necessary, to select an option. 
– 
1° adjusts the angle in one-degree angle increments. 
– 
30° adjusts the angle in 30-degree angle increments. 
2. 
Rotate Angle. 
 
Note: For a transesophageal transducer, you can press the smart control on the transducer handle 
assigned to rotating the scan plane. 
See also: For information about the smart controls on a transesophageal transducer, refer to 
Chapter C4 in this manual. 
Use the configuration settings to set up the smart controls on the handle of a transesophageal 
transducer.

D6  Single Plane and Biplane Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D6 - 7 
Imaging with the Biplane Function 
The biplane imaging function scans two planes with different rotation and tilt angles. You can 
adjust the planes individually or simultaneously. Individual adjustment includes adjustment of 
the tilt and rotation of the scan plane or image gain. 
The planes rotate together or independently during biplane imaging. 
Note: The ED-ES Split feature is not available during biplane imaging. 
Use the configuration settings to specify the default tilt line display and biplane rotation angles. 
When biplane imaging is configured with the default rotation angles of 0° for the reference 
plane and 90° for the right (lateral) plane, the scan planes are equivalent to the following planes 
during volume imaging: 
Scan Plane during Biplane Imaging 
Multiplanar Reconstruction (MPR) 
during Volume Imaging 
Color 
Reference plane 
Plane A 
Red 
Right plane 
Plane B 
Green 
See also: For information about cardiac volume imaging, refer to Chapter D2 in this manual. 
To image with the biplane feature: 
Prerequisite: Select a compatible transducer and image preset. Select the 2D tab. 
 
Tap Bi-Plane+. 
 
To 
Do This 
Select only the reference plane 
 Tap Left. 
 Press UPDATE to select Go to Left. 
Select only the right plane 
 Tap Right. 
 Press UPDATE to select Go to Right. 
Select both planes 
 Tap Both. 
Rotate the scan plane 
Prerequisite: Select the reference plane, right plane, or both. 
See also: For information about rotating the scan plane, refer to 
page D6-6. 
Rotate the right plane by 180° 
 Tap Right Invert. 
Rotate the right plane perpendicular 
(90°) to the reference plane 
(Not available for the AcuNav Lumos 4D ICE catheter) 
 Tap Perpendicular.

Advanced Imaging Manual 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the tilt angle 
(Not available for the AcuNav Lumos 4D ICE catheter) 
Prerequisite: Select the reference plane, right plane, or both. 
 Rotate Tilt Angle to adjust the tilt in 1° increments. 
 Press a trackball key, if necessary to select Tilt and then roll the 
trackball to freely adjust the tilt. 
A tilt icon below the reference plane indicates the tilt direction. 
 
A double tilt icon indicates the planes are parallel. 
 
Reset the tilt angle to the original 
position 
(Not available for the AcuNav Lumos 4D ICE catheter) 
 Press Tilt Angle. 
Reset the reference plane to 0° and 
the right plane to the default setting 
 Tap Reset Angle. 
Adjust the field of view (FOV) 
Prerequisite: Select the reference plane, right plane, or both. 
Note: You can adjust the size of the FOV on both planes at once, but 
you can only reposition the FOV on one plane at a time. 
1. Press a trackball key, if necessary. 
– Position indicates the trackball is assigned to repositioning the 
FOV. A dashed line outlines the FOV. 
– Size indicates the trackball is assigned to adjusting the width of 
the FOV. A dotted line outlines the FOV. 
– (Available only for the AcuNav Lumos 4D ICE catheter) 
Set indicates the trackball is no longer assigned to adjusting the 
FOV. The system removes the outline from the FOV. 
2. Roll the trackball to adjust the size or position and then press a 
trackball key. 
Exit biplane imaging 
 Tap Bi-Plane+.

content:
System Reference 
v 
Typographical Conventions 
The following typographical conventions are in descriptions and procedures within your user 
and reference manuals. Use the conventions to identify the location of a control or selection on 
the ultrasound system. 
Control or Selection 
Description 
Controls on the Control 
Panel 
Controls located on the control panel are indicated by uppercase boldface type. 
Examples: 
 Rotate 2D to adjust the 2D gain. 
 Press ABC to activate or exit the annotation function. 
 Double-click UPDATE to display the 2D image. 
Trackball and Trackball Keys 
Right and left trackball keys are located on the control panel. The function assigned to 
the trackball and trackball keys is indicated by labels on the image screen. 
Examples: 
 Adjust the size or position of the field of view and then press a trackball key. 
 Position the measurement marker and then press a trackball key. 
 Press the right trackball key. 
Selections on the Image 
Screen 
On-screen selections are indicated by boldface type.  
Roll the trackball to position the pointer on the control or object on the image screen 
and then press a trackball key. 
Examples: 
 Click Correct on the patient registration form. 
 Double-click a thumbnail. 
 Select the check box for the required entries and then click Delete. 
Controls on the Control 
Panel for the Touch Screen 
Press and rotate controls on the control panel are labeled on the touch screen. The 
selection assigned to these controls is indicated by boldface type. 
Examples: 
 Rotate Tint. 
 Press Steer. 
Selections on the Touch 
Screen 
Touch screen selections are indicated by boldface type. 
Tap the touch screen to access a selection. Drag an object on the touch screen to 
reposition the object. Swipe the screen to display a separate page of selections. 
Examples: 
 Tap Workflow. 
 Drag the tail of the arrow on the touch screen to adjust the length.

1  Configuration Settings 
System Reference 
1 - 3 
Overview 
You can use the configuration settings to modify factory (default) settings or customize the 
current settings. 
The configuration settings are organized into categories, for example, ultrasound system 
settings, imaging settings, and networking settings. 
Note: Some changes may not take effect until you restart the ultrasound system. The system 
displays a message to remind you to restart the system. 
To access the configuration settings: 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click the name of the category on the left side of the image screen. 
The settings display on the right side of the image screen. 
3. 
Modify the settings. 
4. 
To save your changes, click the name of another category. Or, exit the configuration 
settings. 
5. 
To restore the factory settings, click Restore Defaults. 
Note: Restoring default factory settings deletes your changes.

content:
1  Configuration Settings 
1 - 12 
System Reference 
Selection 
Description 
Clip Length 
Provides measurement options for the duration of a recorded clip. 
Time 
Defines the length of the clip to capture. 
 Seconds displays a list of predefined clip lengths. 
 Custom (1 ~ 300) defines a clip length in seconds. 
Beats 
Defines the length of the clip to capture. 
 Beats displays a list of predefined heart cycles. 
 Custom (1 ~ 300) defines a clip length in heart beats. 
 First R-Wave Offset indicates the user-defined number of frames to capture before 
the first R-wave. 
 Last R-Wave Offset indicates the user-defined number of frames to capture after 
the last R-wave. 
Enable Compression 
When enabled, the ultrasound system compresses the clip at the time of capture.  
Note: Compression reduces image quality, and the original quality of the images in the 
clip cannot be restored. The quality factor is stored in the DICOM tag of the clip. Quality 
factor is the degree of loss during compression, where 2 is the lowest compression with 
the highest quality image and 255 is the highest compression with the lowest quality 
image. When this option is disabled, clips include lossless images with a quality factor 
of 0. 
Compression Level 
Specifies the level of clip compression. 
 Low provides the lowest level of compression while retaining a high-quality image, 
for example, to a quality factor of 10. 
 Medium provides a moderate level of compression while reducing the image quality, 
for example, to a quality factor of 25. 
 High provides the greatest compression with the greatest loss of image quality, for 
example, to a quality factor of 35. 
Capture Definition 
Provides options for decreasing the file size of a clip. 
Limit Clip Capture 
Rate to 30Hz 
When enabled, limits the clip capture frequency to 30 Hz. 
Note: Limiting the frequency stores files at a lower frame rate and creates a smaller file 
size. When this option is disabled, the ultrasound system captures and stores files at a 
higher frame rate.

When enabled, the ultrasound system compresses the clip at the time of capture.  
Note: Compression reduces image quality, and the original quality of the images in the 
clip cannot be restored. The quality factor is stored in the DICOM tag of the clip. Quality 
factor is the degree of loss during compression, where 2 is the lowest compression with 
the highest quality image and 255 is the highest compression with the lowest quality 
image. When this option is disabled, clips include lossless images with a quality factor 
of 0. 
Compression Level 
Specifies the level of clip compression. 
 Low provides the lowest level of compression while retaining a high-quality image, 
for example, to a quality factor of 10. 
 Medium provides a moderate level of compression while reducing the image quality, 
for example, to a quality factor of 25. 
 High provides the greatest compression with the greatest loss of image quality, for 
example, to a quality factor of 35. 
4D Capture Settings 
Provides options for capturing clips during 4D imaging for the selected image preset. 
Note: The 4D and default capture settings are identical with the following exceptions: 
The maximum clip length for 4D volumes is 10 seconds.

Importing and Exporting Protocols 
To import or export a protocol: 
1. 
Connect an external storage device to the ultrasound system. 
2. 
Activate the configuration settings. 
3. 
Select a method. 
– 
Click Features and then click Protocols. 
– 
For a stress echo protocol, click Features and then click Stress Echo. 
4. 
To import a protocol, click Import. 
5. 
To export a protocol, click Export. 
6. 
Select the protocol. 
7. 
To transfer all protocols in the list, click Select All. 
8. 
Click OK. 
9. 
To cancel the import or export, click Close. 
Configuring Protocols on a Personal Computer 
You can use your personal computer to edit an existing workflow protocol or to create a new 
protocol. 
To configure a protocol on a personal computer: 
1. 
Export one or more protocols from the ultrasound system to an external storage device. 
The system copies the selected protocols and the protocol editor software tool to the 
external storage device. 
2. 
Insert the external storage device into your personal computer. 
3. 
Double-click OfflineProtocolEditor.exe. 
The offline protocol editor software provides the same Protocol selections as the 
configuration menu on the ultrasound system. 
4. 
Use the selections to edit an existing protocol or create a new protocol. 
5. 
Import the protocols from the external storage device to the ultrasound system.

content:
1  Configuration Settings 
System Reference 
1 - 31 
Automatic Deletion of Transferred Patient Studies 
You can configure the system to automatically manage disk space by deleting transferred 
patient studies when space falls below the automatic deletion threshold. 
When automatic disk management is enabled and the amount of used storage space on the 
local database reaches a system-defined threshold, the system automatically deletes the oldest 
studies transferred to a PACS. 
Criteria for Deletion 
Note: Siemens Healthineers recommends that you limit automatic deletion to data that has been 
sent to a PACS or archive devices only. 
To qualify for deletion through automatic disk management, a study must fulfill the following 
requirements: 
 
The date on which the study (or most recent series object within the study) was stored to 
the system is outside the delay threshold. The delay threshold is the number of days prior 
to the most recent storage date that qualifies for the deletion process. 
 
All series objects and all images within the study are unprotected (system default). 
 
The study's work status meets at least one (not necessarily all) of the criteria specified for 
automatic disk management. 
Study Deletion Process 
With automatic disk management enabled, the system begins study deletion as a background 
operation when the amount of used storage space reaches the system's automatic deletion 
threshold. 
Storage space is checked every time an examination ends. 
The system deletes older studies first, ignoring the most recently stored studies according to 
the system's delay threshold. 
The storage date of the most recent series object within the study matches the date of the study 
("study date"). Use the patient browser to view the study date. 
Note: If no studies exist for a patient after the study deletion process, then the system automatically 
deletes the empty patient folder.

Assigning an Exam Association to a Procedure Description 
You can assign a default exam association to a procedure description. The default exam 
displays on the patient registration form scheduled procedures. Scheduled procedures require 
a network connection to a worklist server. 
You can also export a file from the ultrasound system, and use a personal computer to edit 
procedure descriptions. 
See also: Exporting and Importing Files with Customized Configuration Settings, page 2-34 
To assign an exam association to a procedure description: 
Prerequisite: Obtain procedure descriptions from your PACS administrator. 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Workflow Enhancement. 
3. 
Click Procedure Configuration. 
The system lists procedure descriptions and a list of image presets assigned to the 
procedure descriptions. 
4. 
Enter a procedure description in the Requested Procedure Description text box and then 
click Add. 
Note: The maximum number of characters including spaces is 40. 
5. 
To assign an exam association to a procedure description, select a procedure description 
and then click exam name. 
6. 
To remove a procedure description, select the procedure description and then click Delete.

content:
2  Workflow Configuration Settings 
System Reference 
2 - 11 
Customizing Annotations 
An annotation package is a collection of use-specific body markers or text labels. 
You can select and then customize a body marker package or a text package on the ultrasound 
system using an annotation package as a base and then delete, group, and rearrange the 
position of the annotations on the touch screen. You can also add custom text to a text 
package. 
To customize an annotation package: 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Annotations. 
3. 
Select the type of annotation. 
– 
Body Markers provides options for configuring a collection of body markers by exam 
association. 
– 
Text provides options for configuring a collection of text labels by use. 
 
To 
Do This 
Create an annotation package 
1. To copy an existing annotation package, select a name in the list of 
annotation packages and then click Create Package. 
2. To create a new annotation package, click Create Package. 
3. Enter a unique name in the Package Name text box. 
4. Select a Root Package, if necessary. 
5. To save the package, click OK. 
The system displays the Touch Screen Layout Editor tab. 
See also: For information on modifying the touch screen layout of an 
annotation package, refer to page 2-13. 
Rename a custom package 
1. Select a custom package. 
2. Enter a unique name in the Package Name text box. 
The prior name displays in the list until you select another name. 
Show or hide an annotation package 
on the touch screen 
 To include a package in the list, select the checkbox next to the 
package name. 
 To hide a package, clear the checkbox next to the package name. 
 To show all packages, select the Show All check box. 
 To hide all packages, select and then clear the Show All check box. 
Reorganize the list of annotation 
packages on the touch screen 
Note: The order of the package names in the list identifies the order of 
packages on the touch screen when the annotations feature is enabled. 
 Select the package name and then click the up arrow or the down 
arrow to reposition the name in the list.

Modifying the Touch Screen Layout 
You can modify the organization of body markers or text labels on the touch screen by 
rearranging body markers or labels, adding categories or groups of labels, and organizing 
pages of annotations. 
You can add a group of anatomical or modifier labels, for example, prox, mid, and dist, where 
only a single label in a group is selectable at a time during the annotation function. 
To modify the touch screen layout: 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Annotations. 
3. 
Click Body Marker or Text. 
4. 
Select the name of the annotation package. 
5. 
Click the Touch Screen Layout Editor tab. 
 
To 
Do This 
Add a body marker 
 Click a body marker in the library and then click a button. 
Remove a body marker 
 Double-click the body marker button. 
Select body markers from another 
package 
Note: The default library of body markers or text annotations is the 
package designated as the Root Label for the custom package. 
 Select a different package from the Body Marker Package list. 
Add a new page of annotations 
 Click New Page. 
Delete a page of annotations 
 Click Delete Page. 
Add a text label 
 Click any button and then enter text using the keyboard. 
Remove a text label 
 Click the text label on a button and then repeatedly press backspace 
on the keyboard to delete the text. 
Add a group 
1. Click Add Group. 
2. Add a text label. 
Add a label category 
1. Click Add Label. 
2. Add a text label. 
Reposition a text group 
1. Click a button in the text group. 
2. To reposition the text group to the left, click the move left button. 
 
3. To reposition the text group to the right, click the move right button. 
 
Add additional buttons to the 
text group 
1. Click a button in the text group. 
2. Click the add button. 
 
The system adds a new column to the right of the selected button in 
the text group. 
Note: You can add up to six columns of buttons on each page.

Customizing Measurements 
The configuration settings include selections for predefining measurement and report 
preferences.

Tap the configuration button.

Click Measurement & Report. 
3. 
Click the required selection. 
– 
Measurement includes general and use-specific measurement configuration options. 
– 
Touch Screen Measurement Config includes options for repositioning, displaying, 
and hiding measurement labels on the touch screen. This selection also includes 
options for creating and editing custom measurement categories. A measurement 
category is a group of measurement labels based on their use. 
– 
Custom Measurement Label includes options for creating and editing user-defined 
measurement labels. 
– 
Custom Calculations includes options for creating and editing user-defined formulas. 
–

–

estimated fetal weight tables. 
See also: For information about customizing obstetric measurements, refer to Chapter 3 in 
this manual.

content:
2  Workflow Configuration Settings 
System Reference 
2 - 17 
Configuring Measurement Tools and Measured Results 
You can configure default settings for measurement tools and the presentation of measured 
results for each measurement package. 
To configure measurement tools and measured results: 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Measurement & Report. 
3. 
Click Measurement. 
4. 
Click the Exam Package tab. 
5. 
Select the required measurement package from the Exam Package list. 
 
To 
Do This 
Show or hide measurement markers 
during CINE 
 To show the markers, select the Erase in CINE check box. 
 To hide the markers, clear the check box. 
Specify default measurement tools 
 For volumes, select an option from the Volume Tool list, for 
example, three distance measurements or an ellipse and a distance 
measurement. 
 For area percentage stenosis, select an option from the Area 
%Stenosis Tool list, for example, ellipse or trace. 
 For area ratios, select an option from the Generic Area Ratio list, for 
example, ellipse or trace. 
 For Doppler measurements, select an option from the Default Tool 
list, for example, velocity or acceleration. 
 For volume flow: 
a. Select a 2D measurement tool from the Volume list, for example, 
distance or ellipse. 
b. Select a Doppler measurement tool from the Flow list, for 
example, heart cycle. 
Assign the unit of measure 
 Select an option from the Unit list, for example, millimeters or 
centimeters. 
Specify the precision for the 
measured result using whole 
numbers or decimals (in tenths or 
hundredths) 
 Select an option from the Precision list, for example, 0 or 0.00, 
where zero represents the measured value. 
Show or hide a result on the image 
screen 
 To show the result, select the check box next to the result name. 
 To hide the result, clear the check box next to the result name. 
See also: For additional information about measurement tools, refer to Chapter 10 in the Instructions 
for Use.

Configure settings for obstetric use

 Select a setting for the Prostate Specific Gravity, for example, 1.0 
or 1.05.

carotid artery and common carotid 
artery 
1. Select a setting for the Carotid Ratio numerator, for example, 
proximal or distal internal carotid artery.

middle or maximum common carotid artery.

measured during a cardiac study by 
AI Measure

spectrum.

M-mode sweep.

System Reference 
Customizing a Measurement Package 
A measurement package is a collection of use-specific measurement labels. 
You can select and then customize a measurement package on the ultrasound system. The 
package selected for customization is called a root package. 
 
Root Package identifies the base library of use-specific measurement labels for the 
custom package. 
 
A Root Package of None indicates there is no base measurement package. All libraries of 
measurement labels are available for the custom package. 
To customize a measurement package: 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Measurement & Report. 
3. 
Click Touch Screen Measurement Config. 
 
To 
Do This 
Create a measurement package 
1. To copy an existing measurement package, select a name in the list 
of Measurement Packages and then click Create Package. 
The system appends the name of the copied measurement package 
with a number, for example, Abdomen (2). 
2. To create a new measurement package, click None in the list of 
Measurement Packages and then click Create Package. 
3. Click Package Name and then enter a unique name. 
4. To save the package, click OK. 
The system displays the Touch Screen Layout Editor tab. 
See also: For information on modifying the touch screen layout of a 
measurement exam package, refer to page 2-22. 
Rename a custom package 
1. Select the package name. 
2. Click Package Name and then enter a unique name. 
The prior name displays in the list until you select another name. 
Show or hide a measurement 
package on the touch screen 
 To include a measurement package in the list, select the check box 
next to the package name. 
Note: Included measurement packages are accessible on the touch 
screen by activating the measurement function and then tapping 
exam package. 
 To hide a measurement package, clear the check box next to the 
package name. 
 To show all measurement packages, select the Show All check box. 
 To deselect all packages, select and then clear the Show All 
check box.

You can modify the organization of measurement labels on the touch screen by rearranging 
labels, adding categories and subcategories of labels, and organizing pages of label selections. 
See also: For an overview of the touch screen during the measurement function, refer to Chapter 10

labels

System Reference 
Creating User-defined Measurement Labels 
You can create user-defined measurement labels by defining a label root and then adding 
system-defined modifiers and segments, for example, left, right, proximal, middle, distal, origin. 
The ultrasound system indicates user-defined measurement labels with an asterisk (*) in 
configuration settings. 
Note: The following labels cannot be copied, edited, or remapped: length label, width label, and 
anterior-posterior labels. 
To create a user-defined measurement label: 
Prerequisite: Knowledge of operating modes, measurement tools for the ultrasound system, and 
DICOM structured reporting. 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Measurement & Report. 
3. 
Click Custom Measurement Label. 
4. 
To create a new measurement label: 
a. 
Click New. 
b. 
Enter a label name, excluding modifiers and segments, in Label Root. 
Note: The ultrasound system displays the name on the touch screen when the selected 
measurement exam package is active. 
5. 
To use an existing measurement label as a template: 
a. 
Select a label. 
 
Selection

Mapping a Measurement Label for DICOM Structured Reporting 
You must map a user-defined measurement label to include the measured result in DICOM 
structured reporting (SR). The ultrasound system provides sections and codes for mapping a 
measurement label to a DICOM SR template structure. 
You can edit the SR mapping of system-defined measurement labels, except Stenosis labels. 
To include a measurement label in DICOM structured reporting: 
1. 
Tap the configuration button.

Description

Identifies the DICOM structured reporting (SR) template. 
 OB-GYN selects template identification (TID) 5000 OB-GYN Ultrasound Procedure 
Report. 
 Fetal Echo selects TID 5220 Pediatric, Fetal and Congenital Cardiac Ultrasound 
Reports. 
 Vascular selects TID 5100 Vascular Ultrasound Procedure Report. 
 Cardiac selects TID 5200 Echocardiography Ultrasound Procedure Report. 
Note: The ultrasound system displays the structured reporting template for the selected 
measurement exam package. When more than one measurement exam package is 
selected, you must select one structured reporting template.

Lists available sections for the selected SR template. 
Note: If the template identification (TID) sections are not applicable to the 
measurement label, a user-defined results section is available.

3  Obstetric Measurement Configuration 
System Reference 
3 - 3 
Overview 
You can modify features of obstetric and early obstetric measurements, including the default 
author used for obstetric calculations. You can also create, edit, and delete custom gestational 
age tables and fetal growth tables (growth curves). 
The ultrasound system places an asterisk (*) next to the author's name for custom tables and 
measurements. 
 
An asterisk before the author's name identifies user-defined tables and measurement 
labels. 
 
An asterisk after the author's name identifies factory-defined custom tables, for example, 
a table without standard deviation data. 
See also: For information about customizing general measurements, refer to Chapter 2 in this 
manual. 
Designating the Reference Author 
Each author uses a specific range of values to calculate gestational age, gestational analysis 
data, and estimated fetal weight. 
You can change the default reference author for a fetal measurement label. 
To change the default author: 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Measurement & Report. 
3. 
Click OB Tables. 
4. 
Click the Default OB Author tab. 
5. 
Select an author for the measurement label. 
– 
For simple gestational age, select an author from the Gestational Age list. 
– 
For composite gestational age, select an author from the US Age (Ultrasound Age) 
list. 
– 
For fetal growth charts, select an author from the Growth Analysis list. 
– 
For estimated fetal weight, select an author from the EFW (Estimated Fetal Weight) 
list. 
6. 
To calculate the average of existing valid simple gestational ages, excluding the estimated 
fetal weight, select Average from the US Age (Ultrasound Age) list.

Description

(Applies only to growth curves) 
Selects the range for the fetal growth pattern. 
 5%/95% indicates a low range of 5% and a high range of 95%. 
 10%/90% indicates a low range of 10% and a high range of 90%. 
 +/-1.5SD indicates a standard deviation of plus or minus 1.5. 
 +/-1SE indicates a standard error of plus or minus 1.0. 
Row 
Identifies the row of values in the table. 
The system renumbers the rows when you add or delete a row. 
(Fetal measurement 
labels) 
Identifies the variable values for the reference author. 
The lower limit for the variable value is in the first row of the table. 
The upper limit for the variable value is in the last row of the table. 
Include a table row for every variable value between the lower and upper limits. 
Variable values must be less than the values in the prior row. 
For example, if you specify a range from 10.0 (lower limit) to 11.0 (upper limit) for a 
gestational age table, you must create rows for 10.0, 10.1, 10.2, progressively up to 
11.0. 
Note: The ultrasound system does not recognize measurements corresponding to table 
values outside the indicated range.

(Available only for gestational age tables) 
 Weeks indicates the gestational age in weeks. 
 Days indicates the gestational age in days. 
2SD Days 
(Available only for gestational age tables) 
Specifies the number of days for the standard deviation (SD). An entry is not required. 
GA 
(Available only for growth curves) 
Specifies the gestational age in weeks and days. 
(ranges) 
(Available only for growth curves) 
Identifies the limits of the growth curve. 
 Mean indicates the limits for the average mean. 
 Low indicates the limits for the lower range. 
 High indicates the limits for the upper range.

3  Obstetric Measurement Configuration 
3 - 8 
System Reference 
Customizing the Display of Fetal Information 
You can customize the display of fetal data on the image screen, on the touch screen, and in 
the patient report. 
To customize the display of fetal information: 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Measurement & Report. 
3. 
Click Measurement. 
4. 
Click the Exam Specific tab. 
 
To 
Do This 
Display fetal information on the image 
screen 
 Select the check boxes next to the required selections. 
– LMP/DOC displays the date of the last menstrual period or date of 
conception. 
– Clinical Age displays the estimated gestational age. 
– EDD displays the estimated date of delivery. 
– EFW displays the estimated fetal weight. 
Display the SD or GA on the touch 
screen 
 Select an option from the Display Averaged GA or ±SD on Touch 
Screen list. 
– GestationalAge displays the averaged gestational age (GA). 
– StandardDeviation displays the standard deviation (SD). 
– None excludes the SD and the averaged GA from the touch 
screen. 
Display the SD or GA with the 
measured results 
 Select an option from the Display Averaged GA or ±SD in 
Measured Results list. 
– GestationalAge displays the averaged gestational age (GA). 
– StandardDeviation displays the standard deviation (SD). 
Select the upper limit of the range for 
the SD 
 Select an option from the Display Out of Range list. 
– Off displays the gestational age instead of the standard deviation 
(SD). 
– 1.5 indicates the upper limit of the SD is 1.5. 
– 2 indicates the upper limit of the SD is 2.0. 
– 2.5 indicates the upper limit of the SD is 2.5.

content:
4  Clinical Applications Configuration 
4 - 4 
System Reference 
Configuring Workflow Protocol Settings 
You can create, edit, and delete protocols and views for a workflow. 
You can create custom names for a workflow protocol or view. Unique names can include 
alphanumeric characters (A-Z, 0-9), periods (.), and hyphens (-). 
See also: For information about additional protocol and view selections, refer to Chapter 1 in the 
System Reference. 
To customize protocols and views for a workflow: 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Features. 
3. 
Click Protocols. 
4. 
To customize a protocol: 
 
To 
Do This 
Copy a protocol 
1. Select the required protocol from the Protocols and View list and 
then click Copy. 
The system appends the name of the copied protocol with a number, 
for example, Abdomen 2. 
2. Enter a unique name in the Protocol Name text box. 
Add a protocol 
1. Click Add Protocol. 
The system displays a temporary name for the protocol, for example, 
Protocol 8. 
2. Enter a unique name in the Protocol Name text box. 
Rename a protocol 
 Select the required protocol and then enter a unique name in the 
Protocol Name text box. 
Change the protocol sequence 
 Select the required protocol from the Protocols and View list and 
then click a navigation button. 
Show or hide the navigation panel 
during a protocol 
 Select the required protocol and then clear or enable the Collapse 
Left Panel check box. 
Select the progression by view for a 
protocol 
 Select the required protocol and then select an option. 
– Automatic indicates the system activates the next stage in the 
protocol. 
– Manual indicates you must select the next stage in the protocol. 
End a protocol when all views are 
complete 
 Select the required protocol and then enable the Automatically end 
when all views completed check box. 
Activate the AI Abdomen workflow 
protocol after selecting a compatible 
transducer and image preset 
 Enable the Enable AI Abdomen check box.

Configuring Stress Echo Settings 
You can create, edit, and delete stress echo protocols. 
You can create user-defined names for a stress echo protocol, stage, or view. Names can 
include alphanumeric characters (A-Z, 0-9), periods (.), and hyphens (-). 
Customizing a Stress Echo Protocol 
You can customize the image display area, activation method for progression of stages, and 
review settings for a stress echo protocol. 
To customize a protocol: 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Features. 
3. 
Click Stress Echo. 
The configuration screen displays the Stress Echo tab. 
 
To 
Do This 
Copy a protocol 
1. Select the required protocol from the Protocols list and then click 
Copy. 
The system appends the name of the copied protocol with a number, 
for example, Treadmill 2. 
2. Enter a unique name in the Protocol Name text box. 
Add a protocol 
1. Click Add. 
The system displays a temporary name for the protocol, for example, 
User Defined. 
2. Enter a unique name in the Protocol Name text box. 
Rename a protocol 
 Select a protocol and then enter a unique name in the Protocol 
Name text box. 
Change the protocol sequence 
 Select the required protocol from the Protocols list and then click a 
navigation button. 
Customize the image display area for 
a protocol 
 Select a protocol and then select the required Protocol Settings 
options. 
– Display ROI displays the region of interest on the stress echo. 
– Allow selection of multiple clips per view allows for selection of 
multiple clips for each view. 
– Hide the navigation panel on the main screen as default hides 
the navigation panel.

content:
4  Clinical Applications Configuration 
4 - 8 
System Reference 
Customizing a Protocol Stage 
You can customize the stages of a stress echo protocol. 
The reference view is configurable for all stages except the first stage. 
To customize a protocol stage: 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Features. 
3. 
Click Stress Echo. 
4. 
Select the required protocol from the Protocols list. 
5. 
Select the required stage from the Stages list. 
 
To 
Do This 
Copy a stage 
1. Click Copy. 
The system appends the name of the copied stage with a number, for 
example, Rest 2. 
2. Enter a unique name in the Stage Name text box. 
Add a stage 
1. Click Add. 
The system displays a temporary name for the stage, for example, 
User Defined. 
2. Enter a unique name in the Stage Name text box. 
Rename a stage 
 Enter a unique name in the Stage Name text box. 
 Select a name from the drop-down list. 
Change the stage sequence 
 Select the required stage from the Stages list and then click a 
navigation button. 
Select the capture settings for the 
stage 
1. To specify the direction for capturing data, select a Clip Capture 
option in the Stage Capture Settings section: 
– Prospective saves newly acquired images. 
– Retrospective saves previously acquired images. 
– Continuous saves continuously acquired images. 
2. To specify the number of clips stored for a non-continuous stage, 
select a setting from the Clips Per Capture list. 
3. To define the type and length of clip: 
a. Select the Clip Type. 
 Beats captures clips for the indicated number of heart cycles 
 Time captures clips for the indicated number of seconds 
b. Press the Clip Length plus button to increase the length of the 
clip and the minus button to decrease the length of the clip. 
4. To apply the capture settings to all stages, click Apply to All Stages.

content:
4  Clinical Applications Configuration 
System Reference 
4 - 13 
Configuring 4D Heart AI Settings 
You can use the configuration settings to customize the 4D Heart AI feature. 
To customize the 4D Heart AI settings: 
1. 
Tap the configuration icon. 
 
2. 
Click Features. 
3. 
Click 4D Heart AI. 
4. 
Select the default settings for the feature. 
 
To 
Do This 
Select the initial heart chambers for 
contour view 
 Enable the required Contours check boxes. 
– Left Ventricle shows the contour of the left ventricle. 
– Left Atrium shows the contour of the left atrium. 
– Right Ventricle shows the contour of the right ventricle. 
– Right Atrium shows the contour of the right atrium. 
Show or hide the left ventricle (LV) 
epicardium 
 Select a required LV Epicardium option. 
– Show shows the LV epicardium. 
– Hide hides the LV epicardium. 
Select the heart chamber results to 
include in the results 
 Select a required Chambers option. 
– Left Ventricle (max 6) displays a maximum of six results for the 
left ventricle. 
– Left Atrium (max 4) displays a maximum of four results for the left 
atrium. 
– Right Ventricle (max 4) displays a maximum of four results for 
the right ventricle. 
– Right Atrium (max 4) displays a maximum of four results for the 
right atrium. 
Note: Capture sends all available measurements to the report. If the 
results view is limited, fewer results may display on the image screen. 
Select the measured results to 
include in the results and report 
Note: Available labels in the Measurements list are dependent on the 
selected heart chambers. 
 To include a measurement, enable the check box. 
 To exclude a measurement, clear the check box. 
Display measurements as body 
surface area (BSA) indexed values 
 Enable the Display Measurements as BSA Indexed (BSA suffix in 
above table) check box. 
Note: Enter the height and weight to obtain BSA indexed values. The 
height and weight are required on the patient registration form for the 
system to calculate BSA indexed values.

content:
4  Clinical Applications Configuration 
4 - 14 
System Reference 
To 
Do This 
Select the number of heart beats to 
analyze 
 Select the number of beats. 
Note: If the clip includes fewer than the selected number of beats, the 
system analyzes the available beats. 
Analyze results as individual beats or 
an average of beats 
 Select a Results Format option. 
– Individual Beat displays the results as individual beats, for 
example, Beat 1 of 3. 
– Average of Beats displays the results as an average of the 
selected number of beats, for example, Average (3 beats). 
Requires a selection of two or more beats for analysis. 
Select the direction of speckle 
tracking during strain analysis 
 Select a Default Direction for Speckle Tracking option. 
– Longitudinal displays left ventricle (LV) strain results in the 
longitudinal direction in the bullseye view. 
– Circumferential displays LV strain results in the circumferential 
direction in the bullseye view. 
Select the curve to display after 
speckle tracking 
 Select a Default Curve After Speckle Tracking option. 
– Volume displays the change in chamber volume from end diastole 
to end systole as derived from the left ventricle and left atrium. 
– Segmental Strain displays the average strain value in each 
segment of the cardiac chamber, for example, the left ventricle. 
– Global Strain displays the overall global strain or deformation for 
the left ventricle and left atrium. 
Select the timing or phase to display 
after speckle tracking for the left 
ventricle 
 Select a Default Timing/Phase After Speckle Tracking option to 
change the bullseye view. 
– End Systolic Strain (ESS) displays the strain value at end systole 
measured at aortic valve closure. 
– Peak Systolic Strain (PSS) displays the peak strain value during 
systole as measured before aortic valve closure. 
– Time to Peak (TTP) displays the time to reach peak strain. 
– Post Systolic Strain Indexed (PSI) displays the ratio between 
strain (deformation) after end systole divided by total strain.

measured at aortic valve closure. 
– Peak Systolic Strain (PSS) displays the peak strain value during 
systole as measured before aortic valve closure. 
– Time to Peak (TTP) displays the time to reach peak strain. 
– Post Systolic Strain (PS) displays the strain value after end 
systole as measured after aortic valve closure. 
– Post Systolic Strain Indexed (PSI) displays the ratio between 
strain (deformation) after end systole divided by total strain.

scan plane

imaging.

– Rotate Forward (press-and-hold function) rotates the scan 
plane clockwise (forward). 
– Rotate Backward (press-and-hold function) rotates the scan 
plane counterclockwise (backward). 
– Increase Tilt Angle (press-and-hold function) increases the tilt 
angle. 
– Decrease Tilt Angle (press-and-hold function) decreases the tilt 
angle.

5  Network Configuration 
System Reference 
5 - 3 
Overview 
Prerequisite: A working knowledge of networking principles is beneficial for configuring network 
connections. 
You can connect the ultrasound system (the local host) to a local area network (LAN) through a 
wired or a wireless connection. When both wired and wireless connections are configured and 
available, the ultrasound system gives priority to the wired LAN connection. 
See also: For information on creating and editing DICOM configuration profiles, refer to Chapter 6 in 
this manual. 
Configuring a Wireless Network Connection 
The ultrasound system uses network profiles to store wireless network configurations. The 
profile names list displays the name of the network profile for the wireless network. 
Note: The ultrasound system connects only to wireless networks with saved network profiles. 
To configure a connection to a wireless network: 
Prerequisite: A USB storage device with a transport layer security (TLS) or secure socket layer 
(SSL) certificate, if necessary. 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
Click Connectivity & Network. 
3. 
Click Wireless Network. 
4. 
To enable connections to wireless networks, click Enable WiFi. 
5. 
If the wireless network is not listed, click Refresh. 
6. 
To create a new network profile, click Add and then enter the required settings. 
Note: Consult your network administrator for the required settings. 
Selection 
Description 
SSID 
Specifies the SSID (Service Set Identification) of the wireless network. 
Channel 
Specifies the required channel. 
Security 
Specifies the authentication method. 
Encryption 
Specifies the encryption method. 
Signal Strength 
Displays the signal strength of the wireless network. 
Profile Saved 
 True indicates the profile has been saved. 
 False indicates the profile has not been saved. 
Network Key 
The security password, if required. 
EAP Type 
Specifies the Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) authentication method, if 
required. 
 None indicates that no EAP authentication is required. 
 TLS indicates transport layer security 
 PEAP indicates protected extensible authentication protocol

Configuring a Virtual Workstation 
A virtual workstation on the ultrasound system provides remote access to a facility's archival 
and information system. 
The virtual workstation uses either a web browser or a remote desktop connection. A remote 
desktop connection requires importing a secure socket layer (SSL) certificate for the wireless 
network connection. 
See also: For information on importing a certificate, refer to page 5-3. 
To configure a virtual workstation on the ultrasound system: 
Prerequisite: Connect to a wireless network. Upload an SSL certificate for a remote desktop 
connection. 
1. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
2. 
(Available only for the ultrasound system administrator) Enable the NetBIOS port, if 
necessary. 
a. 
Click System Management and then click Security. 
b. 
Click Detail for the Ports. 
c. 
Enable the port assigned to the NetBIOS. 
3. 
Click Connectivity & Network and then click Virtual Workstation. 
4. 
Select a connection option in the Access Type list. 
– 
Browser enables access to your archival and information system from a web browser. 
– 
Remote Desktop enables access to your archival and information system using a 
remote desktop session. 
5. 
To modify an existing virtual workstation, select a workstation from the list. 
6. 
To add a new virtual workstation, click Add. 
7. 
Enter or edit the properties for connecting the virtual workstation to the archival and 
information system. 
 
Selection 
Description 
Name 
Specifies a unique name for the virtual workstation. 
URL 
(Available only for the web browser) 
Specifies the universal resource locator (URL), or web site address, of the archival and 
information system. Requires hypertext transfer protocol secure (https) format. 
Host 
(Available only for the remote desktop) 
Specifies the Internet protocol (IP) address, or domain name, of the archival and 
information system's server. 
Username 
(Available only for the remote desktop) 
Specifies the domain name of the archival and information system's server. 
Password 
(Available only for the remote desktop) 
Specifies the domain password for the archival and information system's server. 
8. 
Click Ping to confirm the connection. 
9. 
To delete an existing virtual workstation, select a workstation from the list and then click 
Delete.

6  DICOM Configuration 
System Reference 
6 - 3 
Overview 
The ultrasound system has integrated networked communication capability to support 
communication with DICOM archive, worklist, and documentation devices. 
The networked communication on the ultrasound system is in compliance with the Digital 
Imaging Communications in Medicine (DICOM) 3.0 standard (also known as ACR/NEMA 3.0). 
You can select encrypted DICOM communications by importing a certificate and configuring the 
ultrasound system for a secure study transfer. 
Prerequisites 
(Available only for the network administrator) 
 
Connect the ultrasound system, or local host, to a local area network (LAN) through a 
wired or a wireless connection. 
 
A working knowledge of networking principles is necessary and beneficial for completing 
network configuration. An understanding of DICOM principles is necessary and beneficial 
for completing DICOM configuration. 
 
Check the storage server for compatibility with the ultrasound system settings. 
 
Requires the following DICOM configuration settings for each device. 
– 
The host name, Application Entity (AE) title, and port number for the ultrasound 
system. 
– 
Media type and duplex mode for connection to the host. 
– 
Alias, AE title, IP address, and port number for each DICOM device. 
Note: If you are using Dynamic Host Control Protocol (DHCP), you are not required to provide 
the IP address, subnet mask, or default gateway information.

6  DICOM Configuration 
6 - 6 
System Reference 
Configuring DICOM Storage Locations 
To configure a DICOM storage location: 
1. 
Access the DICOM configuration settings and then click the DICOM Service tab, if 
necessary. 
2. 
Click DICOM Storage from the Server Type drop-down list. 
3. 
Configure a DICOM storage location. 
– 
To configure a new DICOM storage location, click Add. 
– 
To configure an existing DICOM storage location, select the name of the required 
storage device in the Server Name list. 
4. 
Enter or modify configuration settings for the device. 
Note: The IP Address and the Port Number settings must be correct for the Ping and Verify 
tests to work. Confirm this setting with your network administrator. 
Selection 
Description 
Alias 
Specifies the name the ultrasound system uses to identify the storage device in the 
user interface 
IP Address 
Specifies the IP address of the storage device 
AE Title 
Specifies the AE Title for the storage device 
Port Number 
Specifies the network port the storage device uses to communicate with the ultrasound 
system 
5. 
Configure the advanced options for the DICOM storage location, if necessary. 
 
Selection 
Description 
Transfer Syntax 
Configures how data is sent to the server. You must select at least one of the Transfer 
Syntax options. 
Implicit Little 
Endian 
Implicit (without) value representation (string, integer, and date). When enabled, the 
value representation for each attribute is not sent in the image header and needs to be 
added at the destination using a data dictionary file. 
Little Endian means the least significant byte is sent first. 
Explicit Little 
Endian 
Explicit (with) value representation (string, integer, and date). When enabled, the value 
representation for each attribute is sent in the image header. 
Little Endian means the least significant byte is sent first. 
Explicit Big 
Endian 
Explicit (with) value representation (string, integer, and date). When enabled, the value 
representation for each attribute is sent in the image header. 
Big Endian means the most significant bit is encoded first. 
Transfer 
--- 
Send/Receive 
Acoustic Data 
(Available for volume imaging and for cardiac studies during 2D-mode or 2D-mode with 
contrast) 
When enabled, includes acoustic data with images or clips sent to or retrieved from the 
storage location. 
Enable DICOM 
GSDF 
When enabled, selects the DICOM Grayscale Standard Display Function (GSDF). 
This selection applies an image quality standard to images exported from the 
ultrasound system to an offline review station.

7  Security Configuration 
System Reference 
7 - 3 
Overview 
The security package provides configuration options for managing user accounts and providing 
data access permissions and functional privileges. 
The ultrasound system administrator can access the configuration settings on the ultrasound 
system to manage user accounts and establish data access permissions and functional 
privileges. The ultrasound system administrator can also connect the ultrasound system to an 
Active Directory domain controller with the assistance of the domain controller administrator. 
Prerequisites: 
 A working knowledge of networking principles is necessary and beneficial for completing the 
network configuration. 
 A working knowledge of Microsoft Active Directory is necessary for configuring users and groups 
on the domain controller.

content:
7  Security Configuration 
7 - 4 
System Reference 
Terminology Used in this Chapter 
Term 
Definition 
User account 
A login account assigned to each user to log in to the ultrasound system. User 
accounts are configured to restrict access to functional privileges and patient 
information on the ultrasound system. 
Ultrasound system 
administrator 
An administrative account with permissions to configure the ultrasound system for use 
in a networked environment. This person also manages access to functional privileges 
and patient data on the ultrasound system by configuring user accounts, groups, and 
roles and manages the audit trail. 
The ultrasound system administrator can also connect the ultrasound system to the 
Active Directory domain controller, with the assistance of the domain controller 
administrator. 
Privilege 
A restriction of access to functions or tasks on the ultrasound system, for example, 
sending data. User accounts can be assigned to roles to manage privileges. 
Privileges are also referred to as Functional Privileges. 
Note: The assignment of privileges to roles is not stored or editable on the Active 
Directory domain controller. 
Permission 
A restriction of access to patient data on the ultrasound system. User accounts can be 
assigned to a group to manage permissions. 
Permissions are also referred to as Data Access Permissions. 
Permissions include the following options: 
 No Access indicates the user account does not have access to patient data in the 
specified patient group. 
 Full Control indicates the user account has access to patient data in the specified 
patient group, including the following functions: 
– Creating a study 
– Viewing a study 
– Updating or modifying data; for example, correcting the patient's name 
– Deleting data 
– Changing the security level of data, for example, hiding patient identifying 
information from the screen 
User 
A single user, identified on the system with a user account. 
Group 
A classification for a user account, providing access to patient data on the ultrasound 
system. Groups include user groups and patient groups. 
The following list includes the default groups: 
 Administrator and SecurityAdmins provides access to patient data in all patient 
groups and access to configure the ultrasound system. This group includes the 
ultrasound system administrator. 
 EmergencyAccess provides access without a password for emergency login. The 
accounts have limited access. 
 Standard provides access to all patient groups except service. The standard group 
and role cannot be deleted.

content:
7  Security Configuration 
System Reference 
7 - 5 
Term 
Definition 
User group 
A group of user accounts requiring similar access; for example, users from the same 
team or department. One or more user groups can be assigned to a patient group. 
Patient group 
A group of user accounts requiring the same access to patient data. 
Role 
A classification for a user account, providing access to functions or tasks on the 
ultrasound system. 
The following list includes the default groups and roles: 
 Administrator/SecurityAdmins provides access to patient data in all patient 
groups and access to configure the ultrasound system. This group and role includes 
the ultrasound system administrator. 
 EmergencyAccess provides access without a password for emergency login. The 
accounts have limited access. 
 Standard provides access to all patient groups except service. The standard group 
and role cannot be deleted. 
 DICOM_Group provides access for processing DICOM services. This role is a 
virtual account for transferring network data. 
 syngoServiceUsers provides access for remote service from your service 
representative. 
Audit trail 
A collection of security log files. The security log file tracks user actions, including 
powering on the ultrasound system, logging in, accessing files, modifying patient data 
and images, and powering off the ultrasound system. 
Only authorized users can view the security log files. Security log files are saved to the 
system hard disk, a storage device, or a network location. Saving the security log file is 
also referred to as archiving the audit trail. 
Domain 
A group of computers in a network with a common file database. 
Groups and roles can be managed within domains on a network, for example, a 
Hospital Information System/Radiology Information System server. 
Federal Information 
Processing Standard 
(FIPS) 
The Federal Information Processing Standard is a United States government computer 
security standard used to accredit cryptographic modules. 
Active Directory domain 
controller 
Microsoft Active Directory is a domain server for controlling access to Windows 
resources, for example, enabling user account management, authenticating user logon 
requests, and providing access to network resources, for example, data and printers on 
the local area network. 
Active Directory domain controller is also referred to as domain controller. 
Domain controller 
administrator 
The person designated in your organization to configure user accounts and groups on 
the domain controller. This administrator also creates a user account for the domain 
controller on the ultrasound system. 
Service representative 
A Siemens Healthineers representative who configures the ultrasound system during 
initial installation, supports troubleshooting activities, and repairs the system.

System Reference 
Connect to an Active Directory Domain Controller 
You must complete all steps of this multiple-step procedure to connect the ultrasound system to 
an Active Directory domain controller. In the final step, the service representative must be 
present to map an administrator group and a user group from the domain controller to the 
security settings on the ultrasound system and reinstall the system management controls. 
Step 1: Renaming the Ultrasound System 
(Available only for the ultrasound system administrator) 
Each ultrasound system connected to the domain controller must have a unique host name. 
To create a unique host name: 
1. 
Access the configuration settings. 
a. 
Tap the configuration button. 
 
b. 
Click System Management and then click Service. 
2. 
Click Local Service and then click OK. 
3. 
Click Configuration. 
Note: If this is the first time configuring the TCP/IP LAN setting, you may be required to click 
Next repeatedly to access the setting. 
4. 
Click TCP/IP LAN. 
5. 
Enter a unique host name for the ultrasound system in the Computer Name text box. 
Note: The default host name for the ultrasound system is US2015. 
6. 
Click Save. 
7. 
Click OK to confirm the changes can result in a loss of communication. 
Note: Precisely follow the steps in this procedure, including clicking the home button, to prevent 
loss of communication. 
8. 
Click OK to acknowledge your agreement to validate the host name. 
The ultrasound system displays status messages in the lower left and lower center of the 
screen, for example, please wait, ready, and reboot system pending.
