content:
Appendix A  EMC Publication 
System Reference 
A - 3 
Electromagnetic Compatibility 
The electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) testing of this system was performed according to the 
international standard for EMC of medical devices (IEC 60601-1-2). This International 
Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standard has been adopted in Europe as the European 
Norm (EN) standard (EN 60601-1-2). The ultrasound system from Siemens Healthineers meets 
the requirements of the standard and is suitable for a professional healthcare environment. 
Compliance with test limits does not guarantee that a particular installation will be free from 
electromagnetic interference. 
The system was also tested according to the recommendations of the IEC Technical Report 
(TR) 60601-4-2. 
The following is the definition for the essential performance of the ultrasound equipment: 
 
The image display is free of noise or distortion of the image or numerical value errors 
which may cause misdiagnosis. 
 
The image display is free from incorrect safety-related indications, for example, MI or TI. 
 
The device is free from unintended or excessive ultrasound output, transducer surface 
temperature, or uncontrolled motion of transducer assemblies intended for intra-corporeal 
(endocavity) use. 
Avoiding Electromagnetic Interference 
 WARNING: Operating the ultrasound system in close proximity to other equipment can cause 
reciprocal interference. You should observe and ensure normal operation of the ultrasound 
system and other equipment. 
 Caution: This equipment is not intended for use in residential environments and may not 
provide adequate protection to radio reception in such environments. 
Medical devices either generate (emit) or receive electromagnetic interference. The EMC 
standards describe tests for both emitted and received interference. Emission tests address 
interference generated by the device being tested. The ultrasound system from Siemens 
Healthineers meets the standard for radiated emissions. 
Radio frequency (RF) is a form of electromagnetic energy tested by the EMC standards. 
Ultrasound systems and ultrasound transducers operate in the range of RF frequencies and are 
therefore susceptible to interference generated by other RF energy sources. Sources of RF 
interference include medical devices, information technology products, and radio/television 
transmission towers. To reduce interference from an RF energy source: 
 
Increase the separation (distance) between the ultrasound equipment and the interfering 
device (RF energy source). 
 
Connect the ultrasound equipment and the interfering device (RF energy source) to 
separate outlets on separate circuits, if possible. 
In some environments, it is difficult to identify the source of radiated interference. To identify the 
source of the interference, determine the answers to these questions and then contact your 
service representative with the information you have collected. 
 
Is the interference intermittent or constant? 
 
Is the interference present with only one transducer or with several transducers? 
 
Do two different transducers operating at the same frequency have the same problem? 
 
Is the interference present if the ultrasound system is moved to a different location in the 
facility? 
 
Is the interference mode-dependent? That is, does the interference occur only in one 
mode, such as during Doppler? 
 
Can the EMC coupling path be attenuated? For example, does placing a transducer close 
to an ECG cable increase electromagnetic interference? Does moving the cable or other 
medical equipment away from the transducer result in reduced electromagnetic 
interference?

content:
Appendix A  EMC Publication 
A - 4 
System Reference 
Electrosurgical Units 
Electrosurgical units (ESUs) and other devices intentionally introduce radio frequency 
electromagnetic fields or currents into patients. Because ultrasound imaging frequencies are 
coincidentally in this radio frequency range, ultrasound transducer circuits are susceptible to 
radio frequency interference. When an ESU is in use, expect the ultrasound image to 
experience severe interference that may make the image unusable. This interference stops as 
soon as the ESU is powered off. 
Restrictions for Use 
If RF interference is detected, then the physician must determine if an artifact caused by the 
interference will negatively impact image quality and the subsequent diagnosis. 
Immunity Level Test Results 
Immunity is defined in the standard as the ability of a system to perform without degradation in 
the presence of electromagnetic disturbance. The EMC standards require manufacturers of 
patient-coupled equipment to specify immunity levels for their systems. The standards 
recognize that ultrasound equipment is designed to receive and amplify low-level signals in the 
same bandwidth as the interference. Therefore, it is reasonable to expect image noise during 
electromagnetic disturbance. 
Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) Note: Operating the ultrasound imaging system in close 
proximity to sources of strong electromagnetic fields, such as radio transmitter stations or similar 
installations, as well as portable and mobile RF (radiated frequency) may lead to temporary 
degradation or interference visible on the monitor screen. A lightening of image background may be 
noticed while visualizing hypoechoic structures, or color spectral interference, or jitter, or horizontal 
lines in the image screen may occur. However, the device has been designed and tested to 
withstand such interference and will not be permanently damaged. Wait until the interference 
disappears or restart the ultrasound system. 
When comparing immunity levels of different ultrasound systems, recognize that although the 
EMC standard does define the test methodology, it does not specify the criteria to assess 
degradation. Degradation assessment may vary by manufacturer. 
A qualitative assessment of degradation in image quality is subjective. Noting when the first 
sign of an artifact is seen in the image minimizes the issue of subjectivity and also provides for 
stringent test results. 
The results of emissions testing and immunity testing are provided in the accompanying tables. 
The standards used in testing are also provided in the tables. Testing was performed on a 
typical ultrasound system configuration. The values in the compliance level column of the tables 
specific to transducers is the level at which the RF interference is no longer discernable from 
the ambient background noise.

Appendix B  Patient Data Access 
System Reference 
B - 3 
Overview 
You can access patient data from patient registration and from the patient browser. 
Patient registration includes selections for scheduling a new patient or searching for a study 
saved to a worklist server or the ultrasound system. Use patient registration to update patient 
information or select the study. 
The patient browser displays a list of patient studies saved to a worklist server, the ultrasound 
system, or an external storage device. Use the patient browser to manage patient data, 
including correcting patient information or transferring a patient study. 
See also: For information about patient registration and beginning a study, refer to Chapter 5 in the 
Instructions for Use. 
Location of Patient Data 
You can access patient data from the patient browser screen or the patient registration screen. 
The location of patient data is dependent on the screen. 
Note: The patient registration screen includes a patient browser in a condensed layout.

Also displays the space available in the database.

content:
Appendix B  Patient Data Access 
B - 4 
System Reference 
Accessing Studies from Source Media 
You can change the source media from the local database to a server connected to the 
ultrasound system. 
To view a patient study saved on an external storage device, you must import the study to the 
local database on the ultrasound system. 
See also: For information about importing patient data, refer to Chapter B2 in the Advanced Imaging 
Manual. 
To select source media and a time period: 
1. 
Select a new location from the Source Media list. 
The study list populates with patient data from the selected location. 
2. 
To select a custom period for the studies: 
a. 
Select the Custom Range check box. 
b. 
Select a Start Date and End Date. 
Note: You can click the icon to access a calendar to select a date. 
3. 
To select a defined period for the studies: 
a. 
Deselect the Custom Range check box.

Appendix B  Patient Data Access 
System Reference 
B - 5 
Patient Browser Selections 
The following selections are available on the patient browser screen. 
Patient browser selections display on the touch screen on a contextual workflow basis. 
Selection 
Description 
Source Media 
Indicates the current storage location of patient data in the study list, for example, the 
local database or a connected server. 
Query/Retrieve 
Queries and retrieves patient data from a connected DICOM archive, worklist, or 
picture archiving and communication system (PACS). 
Print Preview 
Displays an image preview from a connected DICOM print server. 
See also: For information about printing patient data, refer to Chapter 13 in the 
Instructions for Use. 
Job Status 
Displays the status of patient data transferring to a connected DICOM server. 
Search 
Displays criteria for searching for patient data stored in the source media, for example, 
patient name, accession number, operator, patient identification, date of birth, and 
gender. 
Study List 
Displays a list of patient studies stored in the current storage location. 
Delete 
Deletes the selected patient data from the current storage location. 
Print 
Prints the selected studies. 
See also: For information about printing images, refer to Chapter 13 in the Instructions 
for Use. 
Send 
Sends the selected studies to a connected server. 
Export 
Exports the selected studies to storage media on a connected external device. 
See also: For information about exporting patient data, refer to Chapter B2 in the 
Advanced Imaging Manual. 
Load to Review 
Loads the selected patient study and activates review. 
See also: For information about reviewing a patient study, refer to Chapter B1 in the 
Advanced Imaging Manual. 
New Study 
Populates the patient registration form with patient data from the selected study. 
See also: For information about selecting an existing patient and beginning a new 
study, refer to Chapter 5 in the Instructions for Use. 
Append Study 
Available for 24 hours after a study ends. Loads the selected study as the active study.

content:

B - 6 
System Reference 
Searching for Patient Studies 
Patient registration and patient browser screens include a keyword search text box. Patient 
registration also includes a search panel for locating specific study information. 
Icon 
Description 
 
Expands the search panel. 
 
Hides the search panel. 
To find a patient study using the search panel: 
Prerequisite: Access the patient browser. 
1. 
Enter the required search criteria, for example, patient name, accession number, operator, 
patient identification, date of birth, and gender. 
2. 
Click Search. 
3. 
To clear the selected criteria, click Clear. 
Deleting a Patient Study 
Deleting a study removes all content in the study from the local database on the ultrasound 
system, for example, all images saved with the study. 
You cannot delete active, locked, or paused studies. 
To delete a study: 
1. 
Tap Patient. 
2. 
Tap Patient Browser. 
3. 
Select the check box next to each required study. 
4. 
Click Delete. 
5. 
To confirm the deletion, click OK. 
6. 
To cancel the deletion, click Cancel.

Adjusting the Study List 
The study list displays the list of patient data for the current location, for example, the local 
database or a connected server.

and changing the column widths. 
To adjust the study list: 
Prerequisite: Access the patient browser. 
To 
Do This 
Sort the study list 
 Click a column heading. 
Add or remove a column 
1. Click the column display selection icon. 
 
2. To display a column in the study list, enable the check box for the 
selection. 
Note: You can choose up to six selections. 
3. Click OK. 
Change the width of a column 
1. Access the pointer and then roll the trackball to position the pointer 
over the required column heading until the resize icon displays in the 
column. 
 
2. Press a trackball key and then drag the icon to resize the column.

Appendix C  Measurement and Calculation Labels 
System Reference 
C - 3 
Overview 
The ultrasound system calculates the value when the required labeled measurements have 
been made. 
The measurement label for the required measurements can include the location, view, or 
dimension of the anatomy. 
Note: Installed features determine the availability of measurement and calculation label packages. 
Use the configuration settings to select measurement labels to display on the touch screen. 
Modifiers for Measurement Labels 
(Not available for the cardiac exam) 
You can configure the display of measurement labels. 
Measurement labels are organized on the touch screen as specified in the configuration 
settings. Measurement labels can include the location, view, or dimension of the anatomy, for 
example, proximal or distal. 
Abdomen and Pediatric Abdomen 
The ultrasound system organizes the measurement labels into the following categories and 
sub-categories: 
 
General includes general measurements. 
– 
Abdomen lists abdominal measurement labels. 
– 
Miscellaneous lists general measurement labels. 
 
Abdominal Vascular includes vascular measurements. 
– 
Aorta-iliac lists labels for measuring the iliac aorta. 
– 
Hepatoportal/TIPS lists labels for measuring the liver. 
– 
Liver Transplant lists measurement labels for measuring a liver transplant. 
– 
Mesenteric lists labels for measuring abdomen vessels (Doppler). 
 
Renal Vascular includes renal vascular measurements.

Cleaning and Disinfecting the Ultrasound System  
v1 2020-03-27 
 
Complete instructions, including warnings and cautions, for cleaning and disinfecting 
your ultrasound system are available in the Instructions for Use for your system. 
▪ ACUSON Sequoia 
▪ ACUSON Redwood 
▪ ACUSON Juniper 
▪ ACUSON P500 
▪ ACUSON S Family 
▪ ACUSON SC2000 
▪ ACUSON NX2 and ACUSON NX2 Elite 
▪ ACUSON NX3 and ACUSON NX3 Elite 
▪ ACUSON Freestyle 
Warnings 
▪ To avoid electric shock and damage to the system, always power off and disconnect 
the equipment from the AC power source before cleaning and disinfecting. 
▪ The use of any disinfectants other than those specified in the Instructions for Use may 
damage the ultrasound system and accessory surfaces and, as a result, may create 
electrical hazards for the patients and/or users. 
 
Cautions 
▪ Do not clean the system with chlorinated or aromatic solvents, acidic or basic 
solutions, isopropyl alcohol or strong cleaners such as ammoniated products, as these 
can damage the surface of the system. Use the recommended cleaning procedure. 
Isopropyl alcohol exception: It is acceptable to use isopropyl alcohol only when 
recommended for cleaning the trackball assembly; refer to the Instructions for Use for 
your ultrasound system. 
▪ Do not use spray cleaners on the ultrasound system as this may force cleaning fluid 
into the system and damage electronic components. It is also possible for the solvent 
fumes to build up and form flammable gases or damage internal components. 
▪ Do not pour any fluid onto the ultrasound system surfaces, as fluid seepage into the 
electrical circuitry may cause excessive leakage current or system failure. 
▪ To avoid the possibility of static shock and damage to the ultrasound system, avoid the 
use of aerosol spray cleaners on the monitor screens. 
▪ Prior to cleaning or disinfecting the system, you must disconnect and remove 
transducers from the ultrasound system. Unintended contact with disinfectants 
approved only for use with the system can result in damage to the transducers.

Cleaning the System 
To clean the ultrasound system, use a clean gauze pad or lint-free cloth, lightly 
moistened with a mild detergent, to wipe the surface of the ultrasound system to ensure 
areas are free of gel and any other visible residue. 
▪ Gently wipe the glass surfaces, for example, the touch screen and monitor. 
▪ Take particular care to clean the areas near the trackball, touchpad, soft keys, rotary 
knobs, and the slide controls. 
▪ Ensure that fluids do not seep into any openings on the ultrasound system, for 
example, the seams on the control panel, the keyboard, or a DVD slot. 
 
Disinfecting the System 
To disinfect the ultrasound system, use an approved disinfectant wipe to disinfect the 
ultrasound system and accessories. Follow the disinfectant manufacturer's instructions. 
See also: For a list of additional disinfectant wipes and detailed instructions for cleaning 
the trackball assembly, transducer holders, gel warmer, and transducer ports, refer to 
the Instructions for Use for your ultrasound system.

content:
2 Release description
The Advanced Visualization Workspace (AVW) is an advanced visualization platform that offers
a single integrated solution, spanning clinical domains and modalities, with the power to
visualize, diagnose, and communicate with one consistent, guided and automated workflow.
This continuously evolving solution is tailored to the needs of the physicians and the hospital
network, designed for seamless integration with other information systems and offers a wide
variety of clinical applications.
Advanced Visualization Workspace offers customers the following:
• AVW provides tools to assist in the diagnosis of multiple clinical questions based on multi-
modality imaging with capabilities designed for optimized results sharing between the
imager and the treating physician.
• AVW offers clinical depth and innovation with comprehensive set of more than 70 clinical
applications spanning across clinical domains including oncology, cardiovascular, neurology,
pulmonology and others, addressing different clinical needs while focusing on optimizing
user experience and efficiency.
• The AVW environment enables launching of CT ASPECTS, NM Suite, AV Viewer, and AV
Cardiovascular Suite positioned as SaMD applications.
• AVW offers a solution which is tailored for the enterprise needs and can scale up to fit large
scale hospitals and integrated delivery networks (IDNs).
• AVW introduces a single multi-modality and multi-vendor solution which provides a
comprehensive single-source view of the patient-related information. AVW allows the
patient information to be accessible from anywhere within the organization and also
enables maintaining consistent applications, workflow and user preferences.
• Service offering which gives a steady stream of clinical and IT innovation through ongoing
software upgrades and updates, allowing to cope with the rapid changes of advanced
analysis environment and stay at the forefront of clinical innovation. Clinical training,
support on demand and consulting services are offered as part of the end-to-end service
offering.
• AVW helps to maximize resources to support productivity through optimized performance,
efficient workflows and machine learning capabilities.
Advanced Visualization Workspace V16
Advanced Visualization Workspace version 16 (AVW V16) replaces AVW V15 and introduces
advancements in clinical functionality, user experience, interoperability, and workflow
automation. AVW V16 introduces AV Viewer and AV Cardiovascular Suite, and integrates
enhanced AI capabilities, improved image analysis algorithms, and enterprise interoperability
with Philips Image Guided Therapy (IGT) systems. AVW V16 continues Philips’ strategy to
deliver an integrated platform designed to support precision diagnosis, efficient planning, and
collaborative care delivery across modalities and clinical domains.
AVW V16 introduces enhancements to core applications such as:
• CT Liver Analysis
– AI segmentation of liver and spleen with direct results integration to PACS

3 Main new features and enhancements
Advanced Visualization Workspace V16 provides new applications, features, and enhancements
which are described in the following sections.
V16.0.3
Viewer
• Added the functionality "Add to Running Application", where you can open new studies in
an existing viewer session.
Spectral Magic Glass
Interactively explore spectral information within a localized region of interest while maintaining
the surrounding anatomical context. The Spectral Magic Glass enables fast, intuitive
comparison of spectral results without switching between series, supporting more efficient
image review and interpretation. Additional improvements include:
• Save batches of spectral results as original images with burned-in labels.
• New factory hanging protocols for improved workflow consistency.
• Selected spectral curve is now maintained when switching between spectral results.
• SBI pictorial image now displays anatomical reference information.
• SBI series are identified with a dedicated spectral icon for easier recognition.
Control curve visibility in the viewer
Show/Hide the CL curve using a checkbox on the Curve list. When you select a new curve, it is
automatically shown.
Grid overlay
Display a grid on Slab and 3D viewports, either using the right-click shortcut menu's Image
Options, or the G keyboard shortcut. You can adjust grid spacing using the floating Grid Spacing
control.
Optimizations to Hanging Protocols
• When loading a study to the viewer, only the valid hangings for the loaded study appear in
the dropdown list.
• You can define your favorite Hanging Protocols (HPs) fand even define several favorites. For
example, for Cardiac MR your favorite hanging may be “Functional”, for CT your favorite
hanging may be "Slab CT" and for Spectral, a spectral Hanging Protocol.
– Upon loading a study, the application selects the first valid, favorite HP.
• You can define an HP with fusion, i.e. CT-PET.
• 3D orientation is retained as part of the HP.
Cardiovascular Suite
You can save the motion-corrected source images and map as a batch.

1 Before you begin
About the product
Performance characteristics
The AV Cardiovascular Suite is a software medical device that allows users to access clinical
multimodality (including spectral CT) viewing and clinical applications & tools from within a
hosting platform (e.g., Advanced Visualization Workspace).
The AV Cardiovascular Suite consists of three sub-suites: AV Vascular, AV Cardiac CT and AV
Cardiac MR.
• AV Cardiac CT:
– CT Coronary Analysis
- CT PCI Planning (a planning feature accessible via a licensed add-on within CT Coronary
analysis)
– CT Functional Analysis
• AV Vascular
• AV Cardiac MR:
– Functional Analysis LV/RV
– Long Axis Functional Analysis
– Quantitative Mapping
– Perfusion Analysis
– Late Gadolinium Enhancement (LGE)
– QFlow
The AV Cardiovascular Suite processes clinical images from different modalities and timepoints
and enables advanced visualization of the images. When used by qualified personnel, it
provides useful diagnostic & pre-procedural information. The AV Cardiovascular Suite can be
used by multiple users with compatible devices.
The physician retains the ultimate responsibility for making the final diagnosis and procedure
plan.
NOTE
Screenshots in the Instructions for Use (IFU) can differ in detail from the User Interface
screens. The screens captured in this IFUs may not reflect the latest User Interface coloring of
the product, however the Instructions for Use remain applicable in all other aspects.

About the Instructions for Use
This instruction for use is intended to assist users and operators in the safe and effective
operation of the product described.
• The “user” is considered to be the body with authority over the product.
• The "operators" are those persons who actually handle the product.

Intended use/purpose
The AV Cardiovascular Suite is intended to assist a qualified user in viewing, processing,
analysis, and quantification of cardiovascular imaging datasets and in pre-procedural planning
of cardiovascular interventions.
Intended data
The AV Cardiovascular Suite is intended to be used for viewing multi-modality imaging: CT
(including spectral CT), MR, NM, PET, SPECT, CBCT, Ultrasound, iXR and DXR images.
The AV Cardiac CT  applications are intended to be used on gated CT acquisitions of the heart.
Gated CT data is used for coronary, functional, and structural heart applications.
The AV Vascular applications support volumetric CTA datasets with proper enhancement in the
arteries, and no or minimal enhancement in veins. 
The AV Vascular applications support both contrast-enhanced volumetric MR data types
(MobiFlex, 4D Trak Brain & Lower Legs, Aorta & Renal MRA, Carotids MRA) as well as non-
contrast-enhanced volumetric MR data types (Inflow/Time of Flight (TOF) MRA, Phase Contrast
Angiography (PCA), B-TRANCE, and TRANCE).
The AV Cardiac MR applications are intended to be used on cardiovascular MR acquisitions of
the heart and surrounding vessels.
Intended patient population
The AV Cardiovascular Suite and its clinical applications are intended for a cardiovascular
patient population and the related medical conditions to be diagnosed, treated and/or
monitored.
Indications for use
The AV Cardiovascular Suite is indicated to be used for the diagnosis and analysis of patients
with cardiovascular disease or heart disease.
The AV Cardiac CT applications are intended to assist the user in viewing, processing, and
analysis of CT datasets and in preparation of cardiac interventions:
• The CT Coronary Analysis application is indicated to assist radiologists, cardiologists, and 3D
technologists in the analysis of coronary artery anatomy for patients with suspected or
diagnosed cardiac disease including coronary artery disease.
• The CT Functional Analysis application assessment is indicated to assist radiologists,
cardiologists, and 3D technologists in the analysis of heart anatomy and function, for
patients with suspected or diagnosed cardiac diseases.
AV Vascular is indicated to assist users in the visualization, assessment and quantification of
vascular anatomy on CTA and/or MRA datasets, in order to assess patients with suspected or
diagnosed vascular pathology and to assist with pre-procedural planning of endovascular
interventions.

The AV Cardiac MR applications are indicated to assist users in the analysis of cardiac MR
studies for patients with heart disease including cardiomyopathies, heart failure, coronary
artery disease and structural heart disease.
• Cardiac MR Functional LV & RV Analysis application is indicated to support users with
assessment of LV and RV function using multi-slice short axis and axial cardiac MR cine data.
• Cardiac MR Functional LA Analysis application is indicated to assist users with an
assessment of LV function from single and multi-slice long axis cardiac Cine data.
• Cardiac MR Perfusion Analysis is indicated to assist users with review and analysis of
individual rest or stress acquisitions and/or rest-stress comparison of multi-slice dynamic
cardiac MR acquisitions in one application.
• Cardiac MR Late Gadolinium Enhancement (LGE) application allows review, segmentation
and quantification of T1w and T2w multi-slice, single-phase short axis MR images. The
application is indicated to support the user with assessment of myocardial tissue
characteristics that may point to pathologies on the tissue level, such as fibrotic tissue.
• Cardiac MR Quantitative Mapping application allows to load, review and quantify MR T1
native, T1 Enhanced, T2 and T2* MR data and to generate parametric maps. The application
is designed to visualize and quantify signal differences for regions of interest within or
between acquisitions. It is indicated to support users with detecting abnormalities that
affect the myocardium in a diffuse fashion, such as edema, fat buildup or storage diseases.
• QFlow Analysis application supports the visualization and quantification of blood flow
dynamics by assisting in the review of MR phase-contrast data.

NOTICE
When using a virtualization solution, images should be reviewed by a responsible physician to
ensure appropriate clinical image quality.
NOTICE
When loading several phases with different scan and/or reconstruction parameters (for
example: different zoom, pan, image number, FOV, matrix), the application performs
automatic alignment between the phases. Image quality may be reduced due to this
alignment.
Measurement accuracy
The AV Cardiovascular Suite image processing technology is state of the art, and therefore
provides sufficient accuracy to be utilized as a medical device for clinical purpose.
A major factor in determining the accuracy of manual measurements is the ability to accurately
place a measurement control point on an image displayed on a monitor. In addition, the
measurement accuracy is also impacted by the image quality and the user’s interpretation of
the image.
Factors impacting image quality
• Scanner’s calibration and quality control program, including the geometric accuracy,
homogeneity, artifacts, contrast resolution, positioning and sensitometry when applicable.
• Imaging protocol, including spatial resolution (e.g., in-plane resolution, slice thickness),
region of interest, reconstruction algorithm, data corrections (for example scatter), contrast
agent, gating and acquisition sequences when applicable.
• Adherence to patient management and handling procedures, including contrast
administration, scan scheduling, positioning and fixation protocols.
• Pre-existing patient comorbidities
• Residual patient motion and other motion artifacts, such as organ motion.
The following aspects are contributing factors to the user's interpretation of an image
• Image viewing settings (e.g., window setting, zoom)
• Visualization options (e.g., MPR, MIP, or MinIP, volume rendering)
• Extent of the users' knowledge on performing measurements.
• Other relevant factors
Based on their knowledge and experience, clinical users are responsible for:
• Assessing the quality and relevance of the input image interpreting the image for a proper
measurement
• Judging the accuracy of the measurements based on the given image quality
• Accurately positioning the measurement control points with the mouse point

Calculation of cardiac volumes
The default volume computation method is the common sum-of-discs method. This method
computes a volume as the sum of the products of areas (of the contours drawn in each slice)
and slice separations (sum of the slice thickness and the inter-slice gap). Alternatively, volume
computation according to Simpson’s rule can be selected.

4 AV Vascular
Philips Medical Systems' AV Vascular application is intended for visualization, assessment, and
quantification of vessels in conventional and spectral CTA and MRA data with a unified
workflow for both modalities.
For CTA data, it provides both automatic and manual bone removal and vessel segmentation
including extraction of vessel centerlines, lumen contours and vessel contours.

procedural measurements.

finalizing diagnosis.

standard reconstruction orientation Left on Right is supported.

Workspace System Instructions for Use (Before You Begin > Measurement Accuracy).
Measurement errors based on the aorto-iliac outer wall segmentation, shown as mean bias and

obtained at different energy levels, as well as tissue composition properties based on
Hounsfield Units, attenuation and effective atomic number.
Indications for Use
AV Vascular is indicated to assist users in the visualization, assessment and quantification of
vascular anatomy on CTA and/or MRA datasets, in order to assess patients with suspected or
diagnosed vascular pathology and to assist with pre-procedural planning of endovascular
interventions.
Intended Users
AV Vascular is intended to be used by adequately trained and qualified medical professionals,
including but not limited to physicians and medical technicians. The main clinicians or medical
and para-medical professionals who may use the AV Vascular are listed below:
• Radiologists
• 3D technologists
• Endovascular interventionalists (interventional radiologists or vascular surgeons)
Intended Patient Population
The AV Vascular application is indicated for all patients that had a CTA or MRA as part of their
imaging exam.

Benefits
When used as specified in the Intended Use, under the circumstances and conditions as
specified in the Indications for Use, the application assists the user with interpreting the clinical
image data on par with the state of the art thus realizing a positive impact on diagnosis or
patient management.
More specifically, the AV Vascular application assists the user with viewing and interpreting of a
CTA or MRA vascular dataset to confirm or rule out the presence of any vascular pathology and
to assist in planning of endovascular interventions. The expected patient benefits are:
With the resulting radiological conclusion, the referring physician can advise the patient with
options to prevent reoccurrence or worsening of the presenting symptoms and optionally (if
diagnosed) control the evolution of the vascular disease by taking action in controlling risk
factors with heart-healthy lifestyle changes and/or medicine or further investigations.
Optionally, the markers and measurements can assist the interventional user to prepare a
vascular stenting procedure if this treatment option is chosen.
Contraindications
None.
Limitations for Use
Notices and Warnings for All AV Vascular Studies
NOTICE
Always use the original images to correlate existing pathology and/or anatomical study.
NOTICE
AV Vascular should not be used as the SOLE incontrovertible basis for clinical diagnosis and/or
treatment planning.
NOTICE
Increasing the slice thickness in slab mode also increases the possibility of partial-volume
averaging artifacts.

Notices and Warnings for AV Vascular Studies using Skull Removal
NOTICE
A thin layer of residual bone in the siphon can mimic calcium plating along a vessel. Use
Curved MPR as a cross reference to verify correct segmentation.
NOTICE
Results do not include soft plaques or calcium deposits within the lumen contour boundaries.
Use Curved MPR and Cross-sectional Cuts as a cross reference to verify correct segmentation.
NOTICE
Strong dental or metal artifacts may impair the accuracy of the segmentation. This may
compromise vessel quality near affected regions. Use Curved MPR and Cross-sectional Cuts as
a cross reference to verify correct segmentation.
NOTICE
Automatically extracted centerlines may be less accurate at subclavian artery kinks and may
need manual editing.
NOTICE
Artifacts in the subclavian vein, caused by highly concentrated contrast material injected in
the(especially right) arm, may have an effect on the accuracy of centerline extractions in
theadjacent subclavian artery.
NOTICE
Proper contrast timing is required for good results. Poor contrast timing can cause veins to
have higher HU than arteries. Contrast in the jugular vein, for example, can cause it to be
extracted, instead of the artery.
WARNING
Vessels that are very close to bony structures might be missed by the automatic
segmentation. Use the MPR images to verify correct segmentation.
Automatic segmentation may force a connection even through a completely occluded vessel.
Use Curved MPR as cross reference to verify correct segmentation and accurate vessel
delineation.

content:
Run Processing (Option for CT Studies Only)
When CTA data is launched to AV Vascular, a bone removal algorithm separates the vessels and
the bones, segmenting the main vessels (arteries), finding their centerline and labeling them as
much as possible.
Processing is performed in the background, while you work on other tasks (a processing
indication appears in the upper right corner). Viewing operations can be performed while
processing is in progress. The results are saved in the Directory. When the study is loaded with
the result series, it opens with the bones removed.
NOTICE
The bone removal algorithm for Body CTA cases may not complete successfully in scenarios
where arms are not positioned upwards or when the scan width does not cover the whole
range of the body width.
The algorithm takes the Z slices above the aortic arch position and adds a splitting line 50 mm
above the aortic arch slice. An exam with an acquired range covering less than 30 cm from the
aortic arch may not be processed by the algorithm.
NOTICE
Depending on your system configuration, using the Run Processing option might cause system
slowness.
Launching MR Data
You can launch MRA on 4D data.
• Use the arrow keys to navigate between time points.
• Default rendering mode for MR is MIP, though you can change to volume rendering and use
one of the MRA presets.
• There is no automatic centerline extraction on MR data. You can define centerlines and
then use them in a similar way to the CT data (same operations available in CT with a
different algorithm). See “Create & Edit Centerlines” on page 52.
• You can also use cases without results and create Vessel Inspection measurements (see
“Vessel Inspection” on page 60).

Whole Body Scans
The application automatically detects whether a scan covers both the Head & Neck and Body
regions by identifying the position of the aortic arch within the volume. This is determined
using the following thresholds:
• Depth required above the aortic arch (X): 100 mm
• Depth required below the aortic arch (Y): 120 mm
If these thresholds are met, the scan is classified as a whole-body scan. 
Once detected, the application behaves differently depending on when the segmentations are
performed:
Split Mode (On-the-Fly Segmentations)
If the original series is launched without a pre-processed result series, the application enters
Split Mode:
• A splitting line is automatically placed 50 mm above the aortic arch slice. You can manually
adjust this line.
• You can choose which algorithms to run:
– Body algorithm only
– Head & Neck algorithm only
– Both algorithms
If both algorithms are selected, the application opens:
1.
A tab for Head & Neck
2.
A tab for Body
3.
A tab for the full volume (without automatic results, only bone structures removed)
This allows separate or combined analysis of the regions in parallel instances.

Viewports
The following types of viewports are available in the application:
• Volume viewport: Volumetric image. Users can select between Volume rendering and
other options such as MIPs
• cMPR (curved MPR) of the selected vessel: A reformatted image that follows the selected
centerline along the vessel. The curved view is intended to show the entire vessel along the
centerline. Users can perform the following operations:
– Review by rotating around the centerline
– Refine centerline by moving the seeds on the cMPR
– In Cut and Extend, users can mark the location to cut on the cMPR
• Cross sectional: A reformatted image allows scrolling along the slices that are perpendicular
to the selected centerline (in correlation to the cursor location on the volume). Users can
scroll along the centerline on the cross sectional; the tracker on the volume image and on
the cMPR image reflects the location of the cross sectional image.
• Axial/Coronal/Sagittal viewports: Standard original orientations of the acquired data (no
reformat).
• sMPR: Straighten MPR shows the centerline as a straight line; this allows easy inspection of
the contour changes along the centerline. Users can rotate around the vessel and edit the
lumen and wall contours if needed.
• Longitudinal MPR: Used when no centerline exists. Based on the location of the cursor, this
shows a view of the longitudinal vessel around the location of the cursor.

chunk_id: Copy of Av Cardiovascular_p47_c60
content:
The Diagnosis mode provides the following functionalities:
• Review and clean the vessel volume
• Review centerlines, using volume,cMPR, cross-sectional and MPRs images as needed
• Correct (edit) centerlines that require editing
• Create centerlines for vessels that were not detected during automatic processing
• When necessary, the Volume and Tissue Editing option is available within the Diagnosis
mode.
• Inspect vessels and create measurements to assist with analyzing vascular problems.
Vessel extraction is slightly different for CT studies and MR studies. The system automatically
recognizes the type of data set that you are viewing, and provides tools as appropriate.
Diagnosis Mode Task Guidance
Diagnosis mode offers the following main functionalities:
1.
Verify vessel extraction
– Edit centerline tools
– Create new centerline tools
– Volume & Tissue Editing
– Comment box
2.
Create diagnosis measurements
Image Types
In the main viewport, you can choose to view from among all spectral results. Pause the pointer
on the name of the data type to see the options; and click to make your selection. In addition,
you can adjust the MonoE keV level using the accompanying arrows. These actions adjust the
associated viewports accordingly. Additionally, the default workspace layout for Vessel
Extraction includes a side-by-side display of the same anatomic region of two different spectral
datatypes (default types are Conventional and MonoE). These viewports are geometrically
linked.
Please refer to the following sections of the Advanced Visualization Workspace Spectral
Applications IFU for information on spectral results and processes:
• Understanding Spectral Results
• Common Spectral Processes
CT Studies
During the automatic bone removal process for a CT study, the following automatic functions
are also performed:
• Vessel centerlines are extracted.
• Major vessels are named.
For CT studies, you should verify the results of the automatic vessel segmentation. Verify that:

• The centerlines are complete, properly located, and positioned at the vessel centers.

MR Studies
Automatic vessel segmentation is not applied when you open an MR study. Therefore the
vessel list is empty the first time that you open an MR study. You should create centerlines as
described in “Create & Edit Centerlines” on page 52 or create local basic measurements (single
diameter or stenosis measurement) on MPRs using the Quick Inspection tools (refer to “Vessel
Inspection” on page 60) .
Two volume rendering presets are available when an MR data set is launched. One preset is
optimized for images with contrast and the other for images without contrast.
The application adjusts the preset’s opacity and color level windowing WW/WL dynamically for
each volume.
The Vessel list displays a list of labeled centerlines.
WARNING
Verify the accuracy of the centerlines and their labels. If needed, use the manual tools
provided in the Diagnosis mode.
NOTICE
The application may fail to create the combined vessel due to incomplete results of its
components.
Bone Removal Tools
The main vessels are extracted and segmented during Bone Removal. Results are displayed
once the process is completed. The first time that a study is launched in the application, the
results show the vessel view, the bone view, and MPR images.
Use the 
 Run Bone Removal tool to reapply bone removal and vessel segmentation if
necessary. From the menu, you can select whether to run the “Head & Neck” or “Body”
algorithms on the specific study.
A range of bone removal tools are available in Diagnosis mode. You can use these tools to clean
the vessel volume when needed. For more information, see the tools Remove Bone and
Remove Residuals in the section “Volume Tools” on page 41
WARNING
You should verify that bone removal does not affect vessel completeness. If necessary,
manually correct the vessel definitions using the correction tools provided.

Verify Vessel Extraction
Vessel List
This step allows you to review the automatically extracted vessels in high detail.
The vessel list is displayed at the top of the task guidance panel (also via the drop down menu
in the upper right corner) when you open the application. The vessel list contains an entry for
each segmented vessel.
Automatic vessel labeling of major vessels is performed, if detected (CT studies only).
If opening the application with results, a message appears requesting you to verify the
correctness of all automatic results: segmentations, vessel extractions, lumen & wall
segmentations and findings. If automatic bone removal was performed when launching the
application, a similar message requests that you review results once processing is completed.
Press Dismiss to continue.
NOTICE
If a failure occurs when using the automatic tools for vessel extraction and editing, a
notification appears in the upper right corner of the screen. If this occurs, either try again or
use manual tools.
• You can select a vessel directly from the list or click on the centerline in the Volume image.
• Review, edit and clean the volumetric image of the vessels.
• For CT studies, verify that the centerlines are complete, properly located and positioned in
the vessel centers.
• Verify that the vessels are correctly named.
To rename a vessel, select it, then right-click to open the context menu and select Rename.
The Vessel Naming dialog opens, pictured below, where you can either:
– Select a name from a predefined list based on the body type
– Manually enter a custom name.

content:
Icon | Tool | Use
 | Extend distally/proximally
(automatic) | When to Use
To extend an existing centerline from one of its edges, using an automatic algorithm.
How to Use
1. Allocate a seed to the expected extension end point. The seed can be located and
modified on the volume and MPRs images.
2. Either click Accept to continue or Cancel to exit the operation.
The application automatically calculates the route between the end of the centerline and
the new seed. In case of failure, try again with more than two seeds.
Note: To extend to a location, right-click on the centerline.
 | Extend distally/proximally
(manual) | When to Use
To extend an existing centerline from one of its edges, when there is no contrast in the
extended segments, or when the automatic tool fails.
How to Use
1. Allocate seeds along the route of the expected extension.
2. Either click Accept to continue or Cancel to exit the operation.
The application connects between the added seeds using a spline function, without
impacting image processing.

This tool lets you connect separate centerlines to create a new centerline. The vessels that you

new, combined centerline.
2. Click the other centerline at the desired end point.
3. Either click Accept to continue or Cancel to exit the operation.
4. Enter a name for the new centerline when prompted.
The new centerline is added to the vessel list.

The Volume and Tissue Editing mode provides a dedicated layout and set of tools for cleaning
and editing the volume image. The same tools that are available to clean up the vessel volume
are provided, alongside additional tools. The main purpose of this mode is to perform
corrections on the vessel volumetric image, such as remove bones or other compartments from
the vessel volume, or copy vessels from the bones volume to the vessel volume, if desired.

This is the most general tool. It includes a single ring, which is typically used to measure a
diameter on the location of a finding. Once you pick a diameter, you can click on any viewport –
the application allocates a ring on the selected centerline.
NOTICE

centerline is selected first. To create the ring, click the selected centerline.
The location of the ring is shown on the volume image as a ring, and on the cMPR, and sMPR
images, while the CS view shows the Cross-Sectional slice of the vessel in the location of the
ring. You can modify the location of the ring by:
• Scrolling in the CS viewport
• Drag the tracker on the volume, cMPR, or sMPR to another location along the centerline

• Max Diameter
• Area

mm above the finding. You can move each of the rings to a better location, according to your
understanding.

• Min Diameter: Finding & reference and %of change

Pre-procedural Vascular Planning

This mode requires the Planning module license.
Pre-procedural Vascular Planning, i.e., Planning mode, lets you create multiple measurements

defines rings and measurement between the rings. In addition, Planning mode lets you use pre-

undergo. The procedure templates are divided into subgroups according to procedure types.

The automatic ring markers rely on the prior segmentation, automatic or manual, of the
respective arteries. Thus, if no arteries are segmented, no ring markers are placed.
Once you select 
  Auto ring markers from the left panel, or by selecting a template that
includes this tool, the automatic algorithm runs and a measurement card is created, as pictured
below:
The volume rendering viewport displays the rings on the volume image. Each ring is associated
with a C-Arm angle that is perpendicular to the ring. Once the ring is selected from the list, the
volume is rotated and the focused ring appears as a straight line.
You can change the C-Arm angle in the volume viewport by rotating the image. Once one of the
ring markers is selected and the volume viewport is rotated, the measurement card is
automatically updated. You can fine tune the ring location on the ostia in the longitudinal and
cross-sectional viewports.
Click a ring annotation on the volume viewport to view the angle.
You can also manually add a ring. To manually add a ring:
1.
From the floating toolbar, select 
 Create Ring Marker.
2.
Review and mark a position on the volume viewport.
A ring marker appears on the measurement card, presenting its associated C-Arm angle.
3.
Edit the position of the ring as necessary on the longitudinal viewport. Changes appear on
the volume viewport.
You can also rename the manually-added measurement.
Changes to the C-Arm angle are automatically saved when you select the ring and rotate the
volume.
Clock Position
The Clock Position tool assists in planning a fenestrated or branched stent. This tool supports
determining where the holes or branches in an aortic stent need to be placed.

5 AV Cardiac CT applications
AV Cardiovascular Suite includes analysis applications for Cardiac CT data.
Performance characteristics
AV Cardiac CT is a software medical device that encompasses advanced visualization post-
processing software applications which provide the workflow and the capabilities needed to
view and analyze cardiac CT images, including spectral. The applications included are:
• CT Coronary Analysis application
– CT PCI Planning -- an interface module accessible via a licensed add-on within CT
Coronary Analysis.
• CT Functional Analysis application
For application-specific performance characteristics, refer to the Measurement Accuracy
section of each application that includes a measuring function. For performance characteristics
of applications that do not include a measuring function, refer to the Indications for Use
section. AV Cardiac CT provides measurement, annotation, and visualization tools. It presents
these measurements and visualizations without interpretation or recommendation and does
not perform automated analysis or decision-making. The physician retains the ultimate
responsibility for making the final diagnosis and procedure plan.
Indications for use
The AV Cardiac CT applications are intended to assist the user in viewing, processing, analysis of
CT datasets, and in preparation of cardiac interventions.
• The CT Coronary Analysis application is indicated to assist radiologists, cardiologists, and 3D
technologists in the analysis of coronary artery anatomy for patients with suspected or
diagnosed cardiac disease including coronary artery disease.
• The CT Functional Analysis application assessment is indicated to assist radiologists,
cardiologists, and 3D technologists in the analysis of heart anatomy and function, for
patients with suspected or diagnosed cardiac diseases.
Intended users
AV Cardiac CT is intended to be used by appropriately trained and qualified medical
professionals, including but not limited to the following users: Radiologists, 3D technologists,
Cardiologists, e.g., imaging cardiologists and interventional cardiologists.
Intended patient population
AV Cardiac CT is intended for assessment of patients with suspected or diagnosed coronary
artery disease.

Key features
AV Cardiac CT is designed to facilitate coronary and cardiac CTA diagnostics through essential
viewing, processing, and measurement functionalities.
Viewing
The software offers basic viewing capabilities specifically tailored for coronary/cardiac CTA,
leveraging the comprehensive features of the AV Viewer.
Processing
The software enables automatic segmentation and editing of the heart and coronary arteries
using advanced algorithms and tools:
General Segmentation:
• Automated segmentation of heart chambers and the aortic root
• Volume viewing functions including Globe Visualization
CT Coronary Analysis:
Coronary artery segmentation features include:
• Automated centerline extraction
• Automated labeling of major coronary arteries
• Automated lumen segmentation
• Automated wall segmentation
Additional editing capabilities include:
• Adding vessels and segments to the coronary tree.
• Editing centerlines, and lumen and wall contours, in cross-sectional and straightened
multiplanar reconstruction (MPR) views.
• Modifying vessel segment labels.
CT Functional Analysis:
• Perform 3D editing of heart chamber segmentation.
• Conduct 2D editing of cardiac chamber contours.
Measurements and calculations
General measurements:
• Conduct basic measurements including length, angle, diameter, and area.
CT Coronary Analysis:
• Measure coronary artery stenosis.
• Assess plaque presence.
• Utilize planning module features such as:
– Cross-sectional and straightened MPR views for planning the stent landing zone, and
determining stent length and diameter measurements.

Benefits
The AV Cardiac CT applications process clinical images from different modalities and enable
advanced visualization of the images, thus providing potentially useful diagnostic information.
These clinical applications support you in interpreting clinical image data by combining
processing, advanced visualization, and measurements, and by allowing you to plan for
subsequent procedures. When used as specified in the section “Intended use/purpose” on page
10, and under the circumstances and conditions specified in the section “Performance
characteristics” on page 83, AV Cardiac CT assists you with interpreting the clinical image data
according to the clinical context and on par with the state of the art, thus providing diagnostic
information from images and providing a positive impact on patient management.
Specifically, using the resulting radiological conclusions -- obtained from quantitative and
qualitative information on the heart and coronaries via the applications and noninvasive
medical imaging techniques -- the referring physician can advise the patient on his or her
current condition, determine whether additional investigations are warranted, present the
patient with treatment options to prevent reoccurrence or worsening of the presenting
symptoms, and optionally (if diagnosed) control the evolution of the cardiac disease by taking
action to manage risk factors with heart-healthy lifestyle changes, medication, and/or
interventional therapy.

WARNING
AV Cardiac CT applications should not be used as the SOLE incontrovertible basis for clinical

Overview of Cardiac CT applications
View and analyze heart anatomy—the aorta, the aortic valves, and the arteries—in high detail,
to review the coronary’s condition and analyze the heart's function, using the following
applications:
• Coronary Analysis
• Functional Cardiac CT
Use these applications to reform arteries into straightened views, and to view the heart in full
volume-rendered mode, including rotations, curved planes and Cine.
These Cardiac CT applications provide viewing and measuring tools for you to perform
dimensional and quantitative measurements of the coronary arteries, to help you identify and
examine patient studies for stenoses and plaque. There are also dedicated tools that support
pre-procedural planning for Percutaneous Coronary intervention (PCI), and additionally
quantify the heart function.
Coronary Analysis application
The Coronary Analysis application is comprised of two application stages:
• Diagnosis - assess the pathology.
• Planning - plan how to treat the pathology.

The Functional Cardiac CT application allows you to analyze a variety of heart functions,

Image types and spectral support
Both Cardiac CT applications (the Coronary Analysis application and the Functional Cardiac CT
application) offer the following image types and spectral support:
Image types
• Volume rendered images
• Curved MPR (cMPR) images
• Straightened MPR (sMPR) images
• Cross-section images of vessels
Spectral support

You can work on Conventional or MonoE images, however, you cannot switch image types.
When using MonoE images, the energy level cannot be adjusted.
Load study
When selecting and loading a study, keep the following in mind:
• A maximum of 5500 images may be loaded.
• If you intend to use the Functional stage, be sure to load at least two phases, the End
Systolic and End Diastolic phases.
WARNING
When loading several phases with different scan and/or reconstruction parameters (for
example: different zoom, pan, image number, FOV, matrix) the application performs
automatic alignment between the phases. Image quality may be reduced due to this
alignment.

Automatic Segmentation Sequence
When the study is opened, the application automatically performs segmentation. The
segmentation process is repeated for every phase that is being loaded.
NOTICE
The order of the segmentation is as following:
• first the segmentation is calculated for phase 75%;
• then all phases between 75% and 80% in ascending order;
• then all phases between 70% and 75% in ascending order;
• then phase 40%; and
• then the rest of the loaded phases are calculated in ascending order.

Calculations
Reference Diameter Calculation (Contours Mode)
If only one of the reference lines (proximal or distal) is active, the reference diameter is the
diameter at the location of the reference line. If both the proximal and distal reference lines are
active, the reference diameter is the average of the two diameters, weighted for their distance
to the lesion location, as shown below.
Ddist

Dprox
diameter, proximal reference
d1
distance between location of stenosis and
location of proximal reference
d2
distance between location of stenosis and
location of distal reference
The above explanation is relevant for Effective Diameter and Maximum Diameter calculations
for the reference location.
Reference Area Calculation (Contours Mode)
If only one of the reference lines (proximal or distal) is active, the reference area is the area at
the location of the reference line. If both the proximal and distal reference lines are active, the
reference area is the weighted average of the two areas, as shown below.

area, distal reference
Aprox
area, proximal reference
d1
distance between location of lesion and
location of proximal reference
d2
distance between location of lesion and
location of distal reference
% Stenosis Calculation

Dles
Lesion diameter or area
The above equation is relevant for the difference calculation in Effective Diameter, Current
Diameter and Area. If the value is negative, the result is shown as %Stenosis = 100 - (the
equation result).

content:
Evaluate the condition of coronary arteries, including plaque characterization and volumes.
From the floating toolbar, select 
 Add Plaque Finding.
Edit plaque
You can edit the plaque on each CS using the following tools:
•
 Erase plaque using the eraser.
•
 Draw plaque using the brush.
Set the Plaque Definition Method
Choose the method of defining plaque - Plaque is categorized as calcified or non-calcified,
based on the HU values in the finding. 
Two methods are available, the Threshold and Gaussian methods. You can specify the method
by selecting the dropdown, and then selecting Finding Contents Settings. 
You can also switch between methods by right-clicking the histogram in order to open the
shortcuts menu.
Low threshold parameter
There is an optional “Low threshold” parameter, with a default of 60 HU that lets you split the
non-calcified components into 2 parts. This low threshold can be applied to both the Gaussian
and Threshold methods.
Plaque definition methods
• Threshold - Select an HU threshold that distinguishes plaque components, where voxels
with HU values above this threshold are defined as calcified plaque, and those below this
threshold are defined as non-calcified plaque.
• Gaussian - This method assumes that different components exist within the lesion. Each
component is represented by a Gaussian attenuation distribution, where Gaussian
distribution analysis is based on a Gaussian mixture model. Each attenuation distribution is
linearly combined to simulate the entire plaque, so that its relative composition is
determined by the proportion of each attenuation distribution. 
If the high threshold set is lower than the mean value of one of the Gaussians, then all
voxels under that Gaussian curve are classified as calcified plaque, and the remaining voxels
are non-calcified.

Measurement Definitions for stenosis | 
Segment | The anatomical coronary segment where the finding is located (e.g., "13-dLCx" in the image
above).
Plaque | Indicates the type of plaque observed or selected (e.g., N/A, Calcified, Non-calcified, Mixed,
High Risk).
Finding name | A label or descriptor assigned to the specific finding (e.g., “F3” in the image above).
Stenosis | The severity classification of the stenosis (e.g., mild, moderate, severe), based on percent
narrowing.
Max. difference diameter | The maximum % of stenosis of the maximum diameter, calculated in relation to the reference
effective diameter at the lesion location.
Min. luminal diameter | Minimum luminal diameter. The smallest diameter detected within the lesion – used to
evaluate the tightest narrowing.
Area | The cross-sectional area of the lumen at the point of measurement, in mm².
Curr. Luminal diameter | Current luminal diameter. The current (measured) diameter of the lumen at the location of the
finding.
Effective Luminal Diameter | A calculated or corrected value representing the functional lumen size (can account for
irregular shapes or offsets).
Eccentricity | Describes the asymmetry of the lumen (0 = perfect circle; higher values = more eccentric).

chunk_id: Copy of Av Cardiovascular_p131_t164
content:
Measurement Definitions for plaque | 
Finding name | The identifier or label assigned to the specific plaque finding (e.g., "F2" in the image above).
Maximum Area | The largest cross-sectional area occupied by the plaque along its length.
Max. Burden | The highest plaque burden observed in the finding, often expressed as a percentage of vessel
area.
Volume ± Error | The estimated volume of the plaque with its associated error margin (measurement
uncertainty).
Content | Total plaque content/volume within the finding (may include both calcified and non-calcified
components).
HU (Mean/SD) | The average Hounsfield Unit (HU) value and standard deviation for the entire plaque—used to
characterize plaque density.
Min Lumen Area | The smallest luminal area within the segment where plaque is present—indicates the tightest
narrowing.
Non-Calcified Content | Volume or percentage of the plaque that is non-calcified.
Start Position | The starting point of the plaque along the segment, usually measured in millimeters from a
reference origin.
Length | The total length of the plaque lesion along the vessel.
Calcified HU (Mean/SD) | HU mean and standard deviation specifically for calcified plaque components.
Med-Att HU (Mean/SD) | HU values for medium attenuation components, often representing fibrous tissue or mixed-
density plaque.
Low-Att HU (Mean/SD) | HU values for low attenuation components—may indicate lipid-rich or high-risk (vulnerable)
plaque.
Threshold | This HU threshold distinguishes plaque components, where voxels with HU values above this
threshold are defined as calcified plaque, and those below the threshold are defined as non-
calcified plaque.

non-calcified components.
• Non-calcified content - Volume or percentage of the plaque that is non-calcified.
• Volume ± error - Estimated volume of the plaque with its associated error margin
(measurement uncertainty).
• Maximum area - The largest cross-sectional area occupied by the plaque along its length.
• Max. burden - The highest plaque burden observed in the finding, often expressed as a
percentage of vessel area.
• Min lumen area - The smallest luminal area within the segment where plaque is present—
indicates the tightest narrowing.
• Start position - The starting point of the plaque along the segment, usually measured in
millimeters from a reference origin.
• Length - The total length of the plaque lesion along the vessel.
• HU (Mean/SD) - The average Hounsfield Unit (HU) value and standard deviation for the
entire plaque—used to characterize plaque density.
• Calcified HU (Mean/SD) - HU mean and standard deviation. specifically for calcified plaque
components.
• Med-att HU (Mean/SD) - HU values for medium attenuation components, often
representing fibrous tissue or mixed-density plaque.
• Low-att HU (Mean/SD) - HU values for low attenuation components—may indicate lipid-rich
or high-risk (vulnerable) plaque.
• Threshold - The HU threshold values used to distinguish between different plaque types
during analysis (e.g., calcified vs. non-calcified).
On CS images, you can opt to show the minimum and maximum diameters, in addition to the
area of the lumen.

content:
Overview
The CT Functional Analysis application lets you analyze a variety of heart functions, including:
• Left and right ventricle volumes
• Left and right atria volumes
• Ejection fraction
• Stroke volume
• Cardiac output
• Left ventricle wall mass, motion, and thickening
• Using Simpson or Segmentation methods of calculation
• Normalizing functional results by Body Surface Area
The CT Functional Analysis application supports volumetric analysis of both the left and right
ventricles, as well as the left and right atria. You can also use this application to visualize the
mitral and aortic valve planes.
The application calculates cardiac functional parameters such as volumetric parameters, wall
motion, wall thickness, and thickening. Color maps also display the values of these functional
parameters for each part of the left ventricle, including wall thickness, wall motion, and
thickening.
You can configure the result tables, and the values indexed by Body Surface Area (BSA). You can
also report each parameter and the wall characteristics based on a 16-segment AHA model.
Additionally, you can collect, save, and export both manually- and automatically-calculated
results from the Findings Navigator.
For the Simpson method, the application uses contours-based analysis and provides both
spokes and polar maps representations, positioned and initiated using the AHA model by
default. 
For the Segmentation method, you can calculate the functional parameters of atrias and of
ventricles, based on tissue segmentation
NOTICE
The CT Functional Analysis application supports conventional and MonoE data.
Please refer to the following sections of the Advanced Visualization Workspace Spectral
Applications IFU for information on spectral results and processes:
• Understanding Spectral Results
• Common Spectral Processes
NOTICE
Loading NM images by themselves into the application is prevented.

Application methods
You can choose from two methods of functional analysis of the heart chambers.
Once all manual corrections and settings have been made, you can freely switch between the
Simpson and Segmentation methods.
Simpson
This method uses dimensions derived from heart contours to calculate Functional results.
Simpson's Rule is a fundamental mathematical principle. It is based on the idea that the volume
of an object can be determined by "cutting" the object into thin "slices." measuring the volume
of each slice and summing the volumes of all slices.
WARNING
Every time a heart tissue is modified, the axes and the relevant contours are recalculated and
require verification. Verify the correctness of the cardiac axes and contours every time you
modify one of the following tissues: left ventricle, myocardium, right ventricle.

content:
2. Verify correctness ED/ES
ED and ES phases are automatically calculated according to the volume of the segmented
tissue. As these results are based on an automatic segmentation, you are expected to review,
and modify these phases if needed. Each viewport is related to a specific phase, for example LV
ED.
To modify ED/ES:
• Scroll between phases using left and right arrow keys, or your mouse. Scrolling does not
modify the selected phase unless you click, for example, Set as LV ED on the image.
Optionally, set Diastasis, the phase which precedes the atrial contraction (mid-diastole).
• End-Systole is the end of the pumping (ejecting) phase of the left ventricle (LV). The
software recommends the phase which has the minimum LV volume between 30-50%. If no
phase is available in this range it recommends the minimum LV volume phase from the
available phases.
• End-Diastole is the end of the filling phase of the left ventricle (LV). The software
recommends the phase which has the maximum LV volume between 90-10%. If no phase is
available in this range it recommends the maximum LV volume phase from the available
phases.
• Diastasis is the phase preceding the atrial contraction phase. (This phase is used in atrial
volume calculations.) The software automatically recommends the first phase available
between 75-80%. If no phase is available in this range it displays “None” and you can
choose any other phase from the loaded phases.
Correct valve and apex planes
For the selected ED and ES phases, examine the position of the base and apex planes, and
correct them if needed. The long axis maintains the same position and orientation for all
phases.

Correct the apex setting by dragging the Apex (V-shaped dashed line) to the correct position. If

position.
Re-orient Long Axis
The Long axis can only be corrected in the ED phase.
1.
Click the ED phase tab.
2.
Examine the Short Axis image. If corrections are necessary, first correct the apex location
on the short axis image.
3.
Move the pointer to the green line (the long axis). The pointer will change to either a
Rotate pointer at the edges of the line, or to a Move pointer when it is closer to the center
of the line.
4.
Clicking and dragging the pointer causes the image to either rotate or pan relative to the
fixed green line.
Re-establish ED and ES Phases
Perform this procedure after correcting the apex plane and the Mitral valve plane.
Slightly rotate the long axis in the ED phase, offsetting it from its current position.
During the correction, an intended function will also automatically occur: the apex and valve
positions on all other phases will interpolate to locate between ED and ES.

6 AV Cardiac MR applications
Indications for use
The AV Cardiac MR applications are indicated to assist users in the analysis of cardiac MR
studies for patients with heart disease including cardiomyopathies, heart failure, coronary
artery disease, structural heart disease.
Cardiac MR apps overview
These six applications focus on Cardiac MR reading and diagnosis:
• Functional LV & RV (Left Ventricle and Right Ventricle) Analysis
• QFlow Analysis
• Functional LA (Long Axis) analysis
• Late Gadolinium Enhancement (LGE)
• Quantitative Mapping
• Perfusion Analysis
The applications launch from AVW, where they open in the AV Viewer.

content:
Upon launch from AVW, AV Cardiovascular Suite opens in the AV Viewer. The AV Viewer
displays studies that you selected for analysis in the main viewport.
For details, see the AV Viewer Instructions for Use document.
Functional LV & RV Analysis
Indications for Use
The Functional Left Ventricle & Right Ventricle (LV&RV) application is indicated to support
assessment of LV and RV function, using both multi-slice short axis and axial Cardiac MR cine
data.
Intended patient population
The AV Cardiovascular Suite and its clinical applications are intended for a cardiovascular
patient population and the related medical conditions to be diagnosed, treated and/or
monitored.
Overview
The Functional Left Ventricle & Right Ventricle (Functional LV & RV) application allows
volumetric analysis of both the left and right ventricles.
The application calculates cardiac functional parameters such as volumetric parameters, wall
motion, wall thickness, and thickening. You can configure the result tables, and the values
indexed by Body Surface Area (BSA). You can report each parameter based on a normal range
that you define, and report wall characteristics based on a 16-segment AHA model. You can
collect, save, and export both manually- and automatically-calculated results in a Findings
Navigator. For short axis, the application launches with contours, spokes, and polar maps
positioned and initiated using the AHA model by default.
NOTICE
To perform segmentation correctly, the analysis package requires multi-slice, multi-phase
images.
Auto Preprocessing
LV and RV segmentation:
• is performed automatically when a series is imported from either a scanner or PACS. The
results are saved in the Patient Directory.
• segments all volumes of short-axis, multi-slice multi-phase series, and saves the registered
series with the study.

Hanging Protocols for the application
In each working mode, the application provides several Hanging Protocols that fit the selected
ventricle. The Hanging Protocols vary by type of viewports (polar maps, number of reference
series, etc.). For optimal workflow, mark both your Favorite and Default hangings. The
application launches the selected default, and shows Favorites on the navigation bar as
shortcut buttons.
Modify ED/ES
When you launch Functional LV & RV, ED and ES phases are automatically calculated according
to the volume curve, when it exists. As these results are based on an automatic segmentation,
you are expected to review, and modify these phases if needed. Each viewport is related to a
specific phase, for example LV ED.
To modify ED/ES:
• Scroll between phases using left and right arrow keys, or your mouse. Scrolling does not
modify the selected phase unless you click, for example, Set as LV ED on the image.
• To navigate back to the original phase, on the Go to toolbar on the upper-right side of the
viewport, select LV ED, or any other option displayed according to the viewport.

Normal values
Background
Diagnosis is a summary of visual assessment, anamnesis, and parameters calculated by analysis.
A normal range displayed in analysis results does not have an effect on the analysis calculation
itself, and is not part of the "diagnosis chain".
Normal ranges can differ depending on age, gender, ethnic origin, and the CMR scan techniques
applied, such as scan protocols on site, vendor, analysis software (algorithms), with or without
papillary muscle extraction.

Recommendations
It is recommended to verify if the normal range used in this software, the factory settings, may
apply to the population group and scan techniques used. In order to set your own normal
ranges, use the Edit Normal Values panel from the right mouse menu in the table view. If you
do not need an overview of normal values, select Hide from the right mouse menu.
The methods and input data used to display the normal range values (factory settings) in this
software are described in detail in the following references:
Kawel-Boehm et al., 2020 
Kawel-Boehm N, Hetzel SJ, Ambale-Venkatesh B, Captur G, Francois CJ, Jerosch-Herold M, et al.
Reference ranges (“normal values”) for cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in adults and
children: 2020 update. Journal of Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance 2020;22:87. 
https://doi.org/10.1186/s12968-020-00683-3
Petersen et al., 2019
(EACVI) Petersen SE, Khanji MY, Plein S, Lancellotti P, Bucciarelli-Ducci C. European Association
of Cardiovascular Imaging expert consensus paper: a comprehensive review of cardiovascular
magnetic resonance normal values of cardiac chamber size and aortic root in adults and
recommendations for grading severity. Eur Heart J Cardiovasc Imaging 2019;20:1321–31. 
https://doi.org/10.1093/ehjci/jez232
Chuang et al., 2014
Chuang ML, Gona P, Hautvast GLTF, Salton CJ, Breeuwer M, O’Donnell CJ, et al. CMR reference
values for left ventricular volumes, mass, and ejection fraction using computer-aided analysis:
The Framingham Heart Study. J Magn Reson Imaging 2014;39:895–900. 
https://doi.org/10.1002/jmri.24239
Chuang et al., 2012
Chuang ML, Gona P, Hautvast GLTF, Salton CJ, Blease SJ, Yeon SB, et al. Correlation of
Trabeculae and Papillary Muscles With Clinical and Cardiac Characteristics and Impact on CMR
Measures of LV Anatomy and Function. JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging 2012;5:1115–23. 
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcmg.2012.05.015
The following tables indicate the values used as factory setting for normal range. The results are
normalized for age and gender.
NOTICE
For RV normal values, there are a low amount of studies available that provide normal values
in younger adults. We use a generic template offered by the RSNA committee. The application
offers the freedom to adjust these settings based on your own experience or study using the
application. Be aware that RV calculation is highly dependent on the accuracy of your
segmentation.

represents a slice. The slice at the apex is in the center. The direction is looking from atrium to

spoke wheel.
To display the following results, right-click the Polar map to open the shortcut menu. For
definitions of the terms listed below, in this document navigate within this chapter, "Functional
LV & RV Analysis", to the section “Terminology”.

Volume graph
Volume graphs show the volume curve of LV and RV during all phases. The X axis represents the
phases, and the Y axis represents the volume in milliliters (ml).
The ventricles' volume in each phase is calculated from the contours. When the contours are
changed, volume is recalculated and represented on the graph.
All information displayed on the curves is color-coded and described in the graph legend. The
graph legend also includes information regarding time to peak.
Trackers on the graph show the ED and ES locations:
• LV ED location
• LV ES location
• RV ES location
• RV ED location
• Current shows the location of the currently selected viewport.
• To display the location phase and volume, hover over the curve line.
• Drag trackers to change their phase location.
• When two locations merge, their trackers merge and can be dragged from the title.
• Hide or display each of the curves by clicking the legend, or by right-clicking the curve to
open the shortcut menu.
