content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 3 
Overview 
Prerequisite: To avoid technique-related artifacts, you must be thoroughly familiar with the 
techniques of 3D and 4D imaging. Read this entire chapter before performing 3D or 4D imaging. 
The cardiac volume imaging feature includes controls and parameters for optimizing three-
dimensional (3D) images and 4D continuously acquired clips. 
Volume imaging is a collection of sequential, parallel 2D-mode images also referred to as a 
volumetric data set. You can acquire the data in a continuous acquisition (4D). The volumetric 
data set creates a volume rendering and multiplanar reconstructions. 
Multiplanar reconstructions are two-dimensional image planes of the volume for simultaneous 
visualization of orthogonal scan planes and include imaging planes not obtainable by adjusting 
the transducer position during 2D-mode imaging, for example, the short axis (SAX) plane. A 
multiplanar reconstruction is also referred to as a plane or an arbitrary slice of the volume. 
Volume imaging includes settings and tools for defining the multiplanar reconstructions and 
volume, including shaping the volume and repositioning planes and volumes for visualization of 
otherwise occluded anatomical structures. The multislice function also provides simultaneous 
review of the anatomy of interest in parallel slices. 
You can activate cardiac volume imaging only with compatible transducers and studies. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and image presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use. 
See also: For instructions on using a catheter transducer, refer to the manufacturer's user manual for 
the catheter.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 4 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Workflow 
The clinical workflow for cardiac volume imaging includes setup, acquisition, and post-
acquisition steps. 
Step 1: Setting Up for Acquisition 
 
Connect a compatible transducer to the ultrasound system. 
 
Optimize the image while scanning during 2D-mode or 2D-mode with color. 
– 
Select a cardiac image preset. 
– 
Adjust the imaging parameters for the transducer. 
 
Define the volume and planes. 
– 
Size and position the region of interest to acquire large or small areas within the 2D 
field of view and volume rendering (VR). 
– 
Adjust the orientation of the volume and multiplanar reconstructions. 
Note: The area of interest in 4D acquisition matches the orientation of the 2D-mode image. 
Step 2: Acquiring and Viewing the Volume 
 
During 4D imaging, the ultrasound system processes the imaging data and simultaneously 
displays the volume and multiplanar reconstructions in real-time. 
– 
Optimize 4D images, for example, resize the VR and adjust imaging parameters to 
emphasize volume data. 
– 
Temporarily pause 4D acquisition to review the volume in CINE playback. 
– 
Store volumes and clips. 
Step 3: Reviewing and Storing Volumes 
 
Review the volume in CINE playback. 
 
View and define anatomical structures in the multiplanar reconstructions and volume. 
 
Measure structures in the multiplanar reconstructions. 
 
Annotate multiplanar reconstructions or volumes. 
 
Store volumes and clips.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 5 
Setting Up for Volume Acquisition 
Prepare for volume acquisition by scanning and optimizing the real-time 2D image. You can 
select an image preset and adjust the imaging parameters for the transducer. 
Note: You can magnify (zoom) and pan an image during the setup step. 
To set up for acquisition of 4D volumes: 
Prerequisite: Connect a 4D transducer, select a cardiac study, and then activate 2D-mode imaging. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and image presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use. 
1. 
Optimize the 2D-mode image. 
See also: For information about optimizing 2D-mode images, refer to Chapter 8 in the 
Instructions for Use. 
2. 
To activate color imaging with a compatible transducer, press C and then optimize the 
color imaging parameters. 
See also: For information about optimizing color images, refer to Chapter 8 in the Instructions 
for Use. 
3. 
Press 4D. 
The touch screen displays the 4D tab. If color is active, the touch screen also displays the 
Color (4D) tab. 
4. 
Define the area of interest for acquiring the volume, for example, reposition the area of 
interest or adjust the cut plane.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 6 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Acquiring Volumes 
Each 4D acquisition produces a volume rendering and multiplanar reconstructions. 
4D Acquisition 
During 4D acquisition, the ultrasound system processes the volume data and displays a volume 
rendering, providing a real-time view of the three-dimensional image as you scan. 
You can adjust settings during 4D acquisition to enhance visualization of anatomy within the 
volume rendering. You can also temporarily pause volume acquisition to play back and review 
CINE data at any time during 4D acquisition. 
To acquire a 4D volume: 
Prerequisite: Set up for acquisition of a 4D volume. 
1. 
Press 4D, if necessary. 
The ultrasound system continuously acquires and displays the volume and multiplanar 
reconstructions on the image screen. 
2. 
Review and optimize the volume during acquisition. 
Note: The following tasks are described on the page indicated within this chapter. 
To 
Page 
Change the image orientation to visualize anatomical structures within 
the volume 
D2-8 
Change the layout of the image screen 
D2-14 
Magnify an area of interest 
D2-15 
Adjust the imaging parameters 
D2-17 
3. 
To complete or temporarily pause 4D imaging and access CINE playback, press FREEZE. 
Note: Pressing FREEZE again exits CINE playback and resumes 4D acquisition. 
4. 
To exit 4D imaging, press 2D. Or, press 4D.

D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 7 
Reviewing a Volume in CINE Playback 
You can review a volume in CINE playback from a paused or completed 4D acquisition, or a 
retrieved stored volume. 
Cardiac volume imaging supports the following CINE functionality: 
 
Adjusting the left and right margin of the CINE frame set. 
 
Selecting frames or beats for CINE review. 
 
Viewing the current position of the end diastole or end systole. 
 
Playing back and editing clips and volumes, including adjusting the playback speed. 
 
Repositioning the current frame marker on the ECG trace when playback is paused. 
Note: A horizontal line displays on the time axis when ECG trace data is unavailable. 
 
Capturing clips and static volumes. 
See also: For information about CINE, refer to Chapter 7 in the Instructions for Use.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 10 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Positioning and Resizing the Volume and Multiplanar 
Reconstructions 
You can reposition and resize the volume, color region of interest, and multiplanar 
reconstructions. 
See also: For information about general imaging parameters for positioning images, refer to 
Chapter 8 in the Instructions for Use. 
To 
Do This 
Synchronize the orientation of the volume 
with MPR A 
 Tap Sync MPR A. 
Synchronize the orientation of the volume 
with MPR B 
 Tap Sync MPR B. 
Synchronize the orientation of the volume 
with MPR C 
 Tap Sync MPR C. 
Show or hide intersecting reference lines 
of the MPRs on the volume 
 Tap MPR Lines. 
Show or hide MPR lines on the MPR 
views 
 Tap Show MPR Lines. 
Align the MPR views to the MPR lines on 
the volume 
(Available only when MPR lines are shown on the volume) 
 Tap Slice Sync. 
Note: Activating Single V or Dual V disables synchronization. 
Lock or unlock rotation of MPR lines 
relative to one another in the MPR views 
 Tap MPR Lock and then select an option. 
– Unlocked unlocks all MPR views, for example, to freely rotate the 
MPR lines. 
– Lock All locks all MPR views, for example, MPR lines B and C 
rotate simultaneously in MPR A. 
– Lock Bi-Plane locks the MPR views for biplane imaging. 
Resize the volume 
 Press Size to select an option and then rotate the control to adjust 
the size. 
– Vol resizes the volume. 
– Lat adjusts the lateral width of the volume. 
– Elev adjusts the elevational width of the volume. 
Adjust the position of the volume 
 Press Position to select an option and then rotate the control to 
adjust the position. 
– Lat adjusts the lateral position of the volume. 
– Elev adjusts the elevational position of the volume.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 11 
To 
Do This 
Resize the color region of interest 
(Available only during Color 4D imaging) 
 Press C ROI Size to select an option and then rotate the control to 
adjust the size. 
– Lat adjusts the lateral width of the color region of interest. 
– Elev adjusts the elevational width of the color region of interest. 
– Axial adjusts the axial size of the color region of interest. 
Reposition the color region of interest 
(Available only during Color 4D imaging) 
 Rotate C ROI Position to select an option and then rotate the control 
to adjust the position. 
– Lat repositions the lateral position of the color region of interest. 
– Elev repositions the elevational position of the color region of 
interest. 
– Axial repositions the axial position of the color region of interest. 
Display a surgical view of the mitral valve 
(Available only for transesophageal transducers) 
1. Tap Mitral Valve. 
The system rotates the volume, syncs the volume to MPR C, and 
repositions the axis markers for optimized visualization of the valve. 
2. Adjust the rotation and orientation, if necessary. 
3. To return to the previous orientation, tap Reset Orientation. 
Display a surgical view of the mitral valve 
(Available only for the AcuNav Lumos 4D ICE catheter) 
1. Tap En Face. 
The system rotates the volume, syncs the volume to MPR C, and 
repositions the axis markers for optimized visualization of the valve. 
2. Adjust the rotation and orientation, if necessary. 
3. To return to the previous orientation, tap Reset Orientation.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 12 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Rotating the Volume and Multiplanar Reconstructions 
Rotation of the volume enables visualization of an anatomical structure from any angle. The 
volume rotates independently of the multiplanar reconstructions. 
In each multiplanar reconstruction, the rotation of a plane is along the intersecting axis of 
another plane. You can synchronize the position of the volume to the position of any multiplanar 
reconstruction. 
Note: When imaging with a transesophageal transducer in Dual V, the volumes rotate in opposite 
directions. 
To 
Do This 
Freely rotate the volume 
 Rotate a control: 
– X rotates the volume around the x axis. 
– Y rotates the volume around the y axis. 
– Z rotates the volume around the z axis. 
Rotate the volume on the X-Y axis 
1. Press a trackball key to select 3D Rotate, if necessary. Or, position 
the pointer over the inner 90% of the volume viewport to activate 3D 
rotation and then press a trackball key. 
The 3D rotate icon displays on the volume image. 
 
2. Roll the trackball to rotate the volume. 
3. To deactivate the tool, press a trackball key. 
Rotate the volume around the Z axis 
1. Press UPDATE, if necessary, to select Pointer. 
2. Position the pointer over the outer 10% of the volume viewport. 
The volume Z rotation icon displays on the volume image. 
 
3. Press a trackball key and then roll the trackball. 
4. To deactivate the tool, press a trackball key.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 13 
To 
Do This 
Rotate MPRs around the Z axis of MPR C 
Prerequisite: Activate the pointer. 
1. Position the pointer over the outer edge of MPR C to display the MPR 
image Z rotation icon. 
 
2. Press a trackball key and then roll the trackball. 
3. To deactivate the tool, press a trackball key. 
Rotate an MPR around the intersecting 
axis of another MPR 
Prerequisite: Activate the pointer. 
1. Position the pointer over the required MPR line on a multiplanar 
reconstruction to display the MPR line rotation icon. 
 
2. Press a trackball key and then roll the trackball. 
3. To deactivate the tool, press a trackball key.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 14 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Changing the Image Screen Layout 
You can change the layout of the image screen. 
Use the configuration settings to specify the initial display layout for the multiplanar 
reconstructions and volume during and after volume acquisition. 
To 
Do This 
Display MPRs A, B, and C and the volume 
 Tap the 4:1 stacked layout icon. 
 
 Tap the 2:2 layout icon. 
 
Display MPRs A and B and the volume 
 Tap the 3:1 horizontal layout icon. 
 
 Tap the 3:1 vertical layout icon. 
 
Display MPR A in the center of the image 
screen 
 Tap the MPR A icon. 
 
Display MPR B in the center of the image 
screen 
 Tap the MPR B icon. 
 
Display MPR C in the center of the image 
screen 
 Tap the MPR C icon. 
 
Display the volume in the center of the 
image screen 
 Tap the volume icon.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 15 
Magnifying or Panning an Area of Interest 
You can magnify or pan an area of interest in the volume during 4D acquisition or review. 
To 
Do This 
Magnify an area of interest 
1. Rotate ZOOM to adjust the magnification level. 
Z displays below the image on the image screen. 
2. To cancel magnification, press ZOOM. 
Pan a magnified area of interest on the 
volume 
Prerequisite: Magnify an area of interest. 
1. Press a trackball key to select Pan, if necessary. 
2. Roll the trackball and then press a trackball key. 
Pan an MPR line 
1. Press UPDATE to select Pointer. 
2. Position the pointer over an MPR line on an MPR to display the 
horizontal or vertical MPR line pan icon. 
 
 
3. Press a trackball key and then roll the trackball to reposition the line. 
4. To deactivate the tool, press a trackball key. 
Pan an MPR intersection point 
1. Press UPDATE to select Pointer. 
2. Position the pointer over the MPR intersection point on an MPR to 
display the MPR intersection pan icon. 
 
3. Press a trackball key and then roll the trackball to reposition the point 
of intersection. 
4. To deactivate the tool, press a trackball key.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 16 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Enhanced Resolution Imaging 
The 4D Zoom feature enhances the lateral and elevational resolution of the volume rendering. 
The 4D Z indicator displays below the image when 4D Zoom setup or 4D Zoom is active. 
To enhance the volume: 
1. 
Tap 4D Zoom. Or, during volume imaging, press ZOOM. 
An orange icon on the touch screen button indicates 4D Zoom setup is active. 
2. 
Reposition or resize the region of interest (ROI), if necessary. 
a. 
Press a trackball key, if necessary.  
 
Position indicates the trackball is assigned to repositioning the ROI. 
 
Size indicates the trackball is assigned to resizing the ROI. 
 
Elev Size indicates the trackball is assigned to resizing the elevation of the ROI. 
b. 
Roll the trackball to adjust the ROI and then press a trackball key. 
c. 
To adjust the ROI elevational position of the right plane, rotate Elev Position. 
3. 
Tap 4D Zoom again to display the 4D Zoom image. Or, press UPDATE. 
A white icon on the touch screen button indicates 4D Zoom is active. 
4. 
To return to 4D Zoom setup, tap 4D Zoom again. 
An orange icon on the touch screen button indicates 4D Zoom setup is active. 
5. 
To exit 4D Zoom to 4D, press ZOOM.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 17 
Adjusting Imaging Parameters 
You can adjust the imaging parameters to optimize the volume. 
See also: For information about adjusting general and color imaging parameters, refer to Chapter 8 
in the Instructions for Use. 
To adjust imaging parameters: 
 
Select the required tab, if necessary. 
– 
4D provides optimization selections during 4D volume imaging. 
– 
Color (4D) provides optimization selections during 4D volume imaging with color. 
Note: Imaging selections available for optimization are indicated on the touch screen in color; 
dimmed selections are unavailable. 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the gain (increase or decrease 
the brightness of the displayed image) 
 Rotate 4D. 
Adjust the overall contrast resolution 
(dynamic range) 
 Rotate DR. 
Select a processing curve for assigning 
echo amplitudes to gray levels in the 
image 
 Press Maps to select an option and then rotate the control to select 
a map. 
– MPR applies the selected map to the multiplanar 
reconstructions. 
– Volume applies the selected map to the volume. 
Optimize the volume rendering 
 Tap Volume Enhance and then select a setting. 
The system excludes low-level signal data and adjusts the opacity 
and transparency of the volume image. 
Change the thickness of the slices 
 Rotate MPR Thickness to select a setting: 
– Off indicates a thickness of zero. 
– Thickness settings are in 1 mm increments and range from 0 mm 
to 20 mm. 
Activate biplane imaging 
 Tap Bi-Plane+. 
See also: For information about biplane imaging, refer to 
Chapter D6 in this manual. 
Activate the 4D Heart AI feature 
(Available only during CINE playback or exam review) 
 Tap 4D Heart AI. 
See also: For information about 4D Heart AI, refer to Chapter D4 in 
this manual.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 18 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the color gain 
(Available only during Color 4D imaging) 
 Rotate C. 
Adjust the smoothness of the surface 
(Available only for volumes during Color 4D imaging) 
 Rotate Smooth. 
Apply a hue to the multiplanar 
reconstructions or volume 
(Available only during Color 4D imaging) 
1. Press Tint to select an option, if necessary. 
– MPR applies the tint to the multiplanar reconstructions. 
– Volume applies the tint to the volume. 
2. Rotate Tint. 
Select a processing curve for assigning 
velocity ranges to color ranges in the 
multiplanar reconstructions and volume 
(Available only during Color 4D imaging) 
1. Press Maps to select an option, if necessary. 
– MPR applies the map to the multiplanar reconstructions. 
– Volume applies the map to the volume. 
2. Rotate Maps. 
Adjust the amount of color pixel 
information overlaying the 2D image 
(Available only during Color 4D imaging) 
 Rotate Priority. 
Emphasize the blood flow, tissue, or 
both 
(Available only during Color 4D imaging) 
 Tap a selection: 
– 2D + Color combines the tissue and blood flow. 
– 2D Only emphasizes the tissue. 
– Color Only emphasizes the blood flow. 
Enhance the color volume 
(Available only during Color 4D imaging) 
 Tap C Vol Enhance and then select a setting. 
Restoring Original Acquisition Settings 
You can restore the original acquisition settings and factory-default settings of the volume and 
multiplanar reconstructions. 
To restore the settings: 
 
To restore the position, rotation, and slice to the factory-default settings, tap Reset 
Orientation.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 19 
Displaying Parallel Slices with Multislice 
The multislice function enables simultaneous review of anatomy of interest in multiple parallel 
slices of a multiplanar reconstruction. 
You can view slices of a 3D volume or freeze and then view a 4D volume CINE sequence with 
the multislice function. 
The point of intersection is the location of the central slice and is relative to the active 
multiplanar reconstruction. Parallel slices displaying in the multislice layout are planes in front of 
and behind the central slice. 
 
Example of the reference MPR with lines representing the slices available for viewing. 
1 
Numbers on the lines correspond to the numbers on the slices shown in the layout. 
2 
MPR line indicators with arrows indicating the view direction 
3 
A yellow line indicates the position of the active slice. 
In this example, the active slice is labeled with a zero to indicate the relationship of the other slices 
available for viewing. 
4 
White lines indicate the slices shown in the selected layout. 
A dashed white line indicates the slice is not visible in the selected layout.

chunk_id: Copy of User_and_Reference_Manuals,_ACUSON_Origin,_2.0,_ACUSON_Origin_ICE,_2.0_SAPEDM_11669746-ABS-800-01-01_Origin_VB30_URM_ENG_p566_c688
content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 20 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
To activate Multislice: 
 
Tap Multislice. 
To 
Do This 
Change the number of slices 
displayed on the image screen 
 Tap a selection: 
– 4:4 layout displays a reference MPR and 15 parallel slices. 
 
– 3:3 layout displays a reference MPR and eight parallel slices. 
 
– 2:2 layout displays a reference MPR and three parallel slices. 
 
– 2:1 layout displays a reference MPR and the selected slice. 
 
– 1:1 layout displays the selected slice in single image layout. 
 
View the multiple slice layout or the 
single image layout 
 Double-click a slice. 
Add or remove a pair of slices on 
either side of the central slice 
 Rotate Slices. 
Adjust the distance between slices for 
visualizing anatomy 
 Rotate Distance. 
Reposition the slices in the reference 
image 
 Rotate Position of Slices. 
Adjust a range of parallel slices within 
the volume 
 Rotate Range Position. 
Select the initial multiplanar 
reconstruction as the reference plane 
 Tap General. 
Display the slices parallel to the 
parasternal reference plane 
 Tap Parasternal. 
Display the slices parallel to the 
apical C reference plane 
 Tap Apical C. 
Exit Multislice 
 Tap Multislice.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 21 
Removing Data from a Volume 
Remove data to enable visualization of anatomical structures within a volume. Rotation of the 
volume and planes can help you visualize an anatomical structure and determine the position of 
the shapes to draw and remove from the volume. 
Shaping a Volume with Cut Plane 
The cut plane function enables removal of 4D data from the volume rendering (VR) using a 
plane oriented and synchronized with a multiplanar reconstruction (MPR). 
To shape a volume with cut plane: 
1. 
Tap Cut Plane. 
A border representing the MPR displays in the volume viewport. The color of the border 
identifies the MPR. 
2. 
Roll the trackball to pan the MPR line and remove extraneous data from volume. 
3. 
To show or hide the wireframe border around the volume rendering, tap Cut Plane 
Wireframe. 
Shaping a Volume with Color Crop 
The color crop function aligns the cropping of color data to the cropping of 4D data in the VR. 
To shape a volume with color crop: 
Prerequisite: Activate color during cardiac volume imaging. Shape a volume with cut plane. 
1. 
Tap Color Crop. 
The system crops color data outside the cut plane in the volume rendering. 
2. 
To disable the function, tap Color Crop again.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
D2 - 22 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Shaping a Volume with Free Plane 
The free plane function enables visualization within a volume rendering of anatomy of interest 
visible in a multiplanar reconstruction but not visible on the surface of the volume. 
As you reposition the free plane, the system crops the volume rendering to enable visualization 
of the anatomy of interest. Retaining the crop shapes and updates the volume rendering. 
The position of the free plane on the volume rendering displays as a synchronized line on each 
multiplanar reconstruction. 
The color of the free plane indicates the orientation of the plane in relation to the volume. 
 
Orange indicates the free plane is behind the volume. 
 
Turquoise indicates the free plane is in front of the volume. 
To shape a volume with free plane: 
 
Tap Free Plane. 
The free plane displays to the left of the volume. 
 
To 
Do This 
Visualize anatomy of interest within 
the volume 
1. Press UPDATE to select Free Plane, if necessary. 
– Pointer indicates the trackball is assigned to the pointer function. 
– 3D Rotate indicates the trackball is assigned to rotating the 
volume on the X-Y axis. 
– Free Plane indicates the trackball is assigned to the free plane for 
shaping the volume. 
– (Available only during CINE playback or review) Cine indicates the 
trackball is assigned to scrolling CINE data. 
2. Roll the trackball to rotate the volume or reposition the free plane. 
Define the distance of the plane from 
the center of the volume 
 Rotate Position Plane. 
Rotate the free plane 
 Press Rotate Plane to select an option and then rotate the control to 
rotate the free plane. 
– X rotates the free plane around the X axis. 
– Y rotates the free plane around the Y axis. 
Reshape the volume by removing the 
cropped data 
 Tap Retain Crop. 
Note: You can retain multiple crops to visualize the anatomy of 
interest within the volume. 
Restore the most recently cropped 
data to the volume rendering 
(Available only after retaining a crop) 
 Tap Undo Crop. 
Remove all cropping and display the 
original volume rendering 
 Tap Reset Cropping.

content:
D2  Cardiac Volume Imaging 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D2 - 23 
Shaping a Volume with Single V 
The Single V function enables a region of interest (ROI) box for shaping the volume rendering 
during real-time imaging, on a frozen image, or in review. 
Note: The Dual V function is available after activating Single V. 
To shape a volume with Single V: 
1. 
Tap Single V. 
The start point displays on MPR A. 
2. 
Define the shape of the volume. 
a. 
Roll the trackball to position the start point and then press a trackball key. 
Note: You can adjust the width and orientation after setting the start point. 
b. 
Roll the trackball to position the end point. 
 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the width of the volume 
 Rotate Box Width. 
Rotate the volume 
See also: For information about rotating the volume, refer to 
page D2-12. 
Note: During Dual V, the two volumes rotate in opposite directions. 
Reshape the volume 
1. Press UPDATE to activate Edit Single V. 
2. Press a trackball key to select an option, if necessary. 
– Set Start indicates the trackball is assigned to repositioning the 
start point of the ROI box. 
– Set End indicates the trackball is assigned to repositioning the 
end point of the ROI box. 
Turquoise identifies the active point on the ROI box. 
3. Roll the trackball to adjust the ROI box and then press a trackball 
key. 
4. Accept the shape and position. 
Restore the volume to the original 
shape and position 
 Tap Reset to Start. 
 Tap Single V.

Accept the shape and position and 
exit the feature 
 Press UPDATE to select Accept. 
 Tap Single V again.

Advanced Imaging Manual

Storing and Printing Images 
You can convert a volume to a DICOM multi-frame clip and store clips of the currently displayed 
volume. 
You can capture and store single-frame volumes. 
You can print individual images of a multiplanar reconstruction or a volume. A volume is a 
sequence of multiple-frame images and cannot be printed as a range of images. 
Use the patient browser to transfer volumes to external storage devices. 
See also: For additional information on capturing images and clips, refer to Chapter 5 in the 
Instructions for Use. 
See also: For information on recording a patient study, refer to Chapter 13 in the Instructions for 
Use. 
To store a volume as a clip: 
 
Press CAPTURE. Or, press the control assigned to the clip store function. 
The system displays an icon on the image. 
 
See also: For information about CINE and clip capture settings, refer to Chapter 7 in the Instructions 
for Use. 
Use the configuration settings to define additional clip capture settings for 4D volumes. 
To save a single frame of a volume: 
Note: The volume data is not stored when you store or print an image. You must store the volume for 
future review of the volume. 
 
Press FREEZE and then press CAPTURE. 
The system displays an icon on the image.

content:
D3  2D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D3 - 3 
Overview 
 WARNING: This feature uses ultrasound data collected prior to analysis. The quality of the data 
collected and used as input could have an effect on the output of this feature. Variability in 
ultrasound system performance, operator technique, patient characteristics, and other factors 
may affect the output. At all times, the clinician is advised to carefully review the output and 
confirm the information presented with clinical judgment and any other relevant sources of data. 
2D Heart AI 
The 2D Heart AI feature performs left and right heart volume measurements using 2D-mode 
data from two image frames. The feature detects and traces the contours of the endocardial 
borders on the end-diastolic (ED) and end-systolic (ES) images in an apical four-chamber 
(A4C), apical three-chamber (A3C), or apical two-chamber (A2C) view. 
Use the 2D Heart AI feature to perform the following tasks: 
 
Detect, contour, and analyze the left ventricle, right ventricle, left atrium, and right atrium. 
 
Detect and analyze end diastole (ED) and end systole (ES) and display ED-ES images in a 
side-by-side format. 
 
Edit or manually trace the contours. 
 
Analyze the results summary. 
2D Heart+ AI 
The 2D Heart+ AI feature includes all 2D Heart AI functionality. 
The 2D Heart+ AI feature visualizes, measures, and assesses myocardial motion and 
mechanics using acquired 2D clips during live imaging or from review. 
2D Heart+ AI tracks and estimates tissue velocity and other motion and deformation 
parameters on every frame in the cardiac cycle and illustrates tissue velocity and direction and 
provides quantitative data for velocity, displacement, strain, and strain rate. 
The tracking results summary, curve graph, and bullseye plot are based on every frame in the 
cardiac cycle. 
Use the 2D Heart+ AI feature to perform all tasks available with 2D Heart AI and the following 
tasks: 
 
Detect the apical two, three, and four chamber views. 
 
Track the contours of the left ventricle and the left atrium throughout the cardiac cycle. 
 
Analyze and compare up to three clips. 
 
Analyze the tracking results summary, curve graph, and bullseye plot. 
 
Perform strain analysis with contrast for the left ventricle. 
See also: For information about contrast agent imaging, refer to Chapter A3 in this manual.

content:
D3  2D Heart AI 
D3 - 4 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Workflow 
The clinical workflow includes the following steps. 
Step 1: Acquiring Cardiac Views 
 
During imaging, acquire clips of cardiac views with an ECG trace (a physio signal is 
present). 
Acquire up to five heart beats for analysis and include a minimum of one full R-R capture. 
Note: If available, include an additional heart beat or R-R acquisition. If necessary, optimize the 
ECG trace before activating the feature. 
See also: For information about using the physiologic function, refer to Chapter C1 in this 
manual. 
 
During imaging, acquire clips of cardiac views without an ECG trace (no physio signal). 
Note: If the feature does not identify ED and ES frames, you must identify the required end 
diastolic (ED) and end systolic (ES) frames to obtain analysis with contours and results. The 
feature analyzes a single beat without physio.  
 
During review, open the required cardiac clips. 
Step 2: Detecting and Analyzing the Cardiac Chambers 
 
To analyze the left and right heart chambers, freeze the image. 
 
To analyze the heart chambers, review a previously acquired cardiac clip, a group of 
chamber views, or an individual chamber view. 
 
2D Heart AI detects the view, places contours, analyzes the 2D ultrasound data, and 
displays the results. 
Note: Available results are dependent on the acquired views. 
Step 3: Reviewing, Adjusting, and Saving the Results 
 
2D Heart AI 
– 
Displays a two-frame analysis with contoured heart chambers in the ED-ES view. 
 
2D Heart+ AI 
– 
Displays apical chamber viewports (A4C, A2C, A3C). 
– 
Displays global longitudinal strain (GLS) in a curve graph and bullseye plot for the left 
ventricle and left atrium. 
– 
Displays tracking results, including volume, ejection fraction, cardiac output, stroke 
volume, GLS, quantitative data, for example, velocity and strain rate. 
– 
Provides viewports, a curve graph, a bullseye plot, and a tracking results summary for 
review. 
 
Confirm the contour placement and manually edit the contours, if necessary. 
 
Confirm and adjust the tracking parameters, if necessary. 
 
Save the tracking results.

D3  2D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D3 - 5 
Image Screen Layout 
The feature identifies each heart chamber by a color in the viewport, results, and curve graph. 
 
Green identifies the left ventricle. 
 
Blue identifies the left atrium. 
 
Orange identifies the right ventricle. 
 
Turquoise identifies the right atrium. 
 
A dashed line identifies the major axes of the chamber. 
The ED-ES view is available during pre-tracking. Accessing the bullseye view or single view 
activates left ventricle (LV) tracking, if available. 
Use the configuration settings to customize the default settings for the 2D Heart AI feature.

Advanced Imaging Manual 
ED-ES View Layout 
The end diastolic-end systolic (ED-ES) view displays when you activate 2D Heart AI from the 
CINE workflow or when you select a single clip or view for analysis. The ED-ES viewports are 
in a side-by-side format and includes a results summary. 
You can only edit contours in the ED-ES view. 
Use the configuration settings to customize the ED-ES view. 
 
Example of a 2D Heart AI screen, ED-ES view layout. 
1 
Viewport label 
2 
Contour 
3 
Active viewport 
A blue border outlines the selected viewport. 
4 
2D clip with contours 
5 
Results summary viewport 
Displays the tracking results for the heart rate and measurements. 
6 
ECG trace 
Available only when a physio signal is present. 
White flag markers identify the beginning and ending margins of CINE playback. 
Pink markers identify the end diastolic and end systolic frames.

D3  2D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D3 - 7 
Bullseye View Layout 
(Available only with 2D Heart+ AI) 
The bullseye view includes left apical chamber viewports with contours and segment values on 
the left ventricle and/or left atrium, a curve graph, a bullseye plot, and tracking results summary. 
Use the configuration settings to customize the bullseye view. 
 
Example of a 2D Heart+ AI screen, bullseye view layout. 
1 
Curve graph viewport 
Provides a view of the timing or phase, for example, segmental strain. 
2 
Tracking results viewport 
Displays tracking results for the apical chamber in a summary format. 
3 
Bullseye viewport 
Displays a bullseye plot with the following segment values: anterior, inferior, lateral, septal, coronal. 
Includes a color bar with colors assigned to the parameter ranges. 
4 
View controls 
Provides options to show or hide the segment values, display the ED-ES view for editing contours, 
delete the view, and display the single view for the selected chamber. 
5 
Image viewports 
Displays apical four, two, and three chamber views (A4C, A2C, A3C). 
Displays contours and segment values on the left ventricle and/or left atrium.

content:
D3  2D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D3 - 9 
Activating 2D Heart AI 
You can activate 2D Heart AI from the review function or during imaging with a compatible 
transducer and imaging preset. 
See also: For information about activating review, refer to Chapter B1 in this manual. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and imaging presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use. 
Prior to activating the feature, perform the following prerequisites, as applicable. 
 
During live imaging in 2D-mode, obtain an apical view and then freeze the image. 
– 
When an ECG trace is not available, the ED-ES Assist feature assesses a single beat, 
and the ED and ES frames are determined by largest and smallest sizes of the left 
ventricle. 
See also: For information on obtaining a physio signal, refer to Chapter C1 in this manual. 
 
Cardiac clips include at least five frames of 2D-mode data. If the clip contains more than 
700 frames, the feature analyzes the first 700 frames acquired. 
 
Single heart beat analysis requires confirmation of the end diastolic and end systolic 
frames. 
 
For 2D Heart+ AI, select up to three apical views to analyze the left ventricle and 
left atrium. 
To activate 2D Heart AI: 
To 
Do This 
Analyze the heart chambers in CINE 
1. During live imaging in 2D-mode, acquire the required apical view and 
then press FREEZE. 
2. Tap 2D Heart AI. 
The ultrasound system displays a progress bar as the feature 
activates, and the feature detects the contours, calculates the results, 
and displays the ED-ES view layout. 
Analyze a single clip or view in review 
Prerequisite: Acquire the required cardiac clips. 
1. Activate review. 
2. Tap Single Select. 
3. Select only one of the following apical views: A4C, A3C, A2C. 
4. Tap 2D Heart AI. 
The ultrasound system displays a progress bar as the feature 
activates, and the feature detects the contours, calculates the results, 
and displays the ED-ES view layout.

D3 - 10 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
To 
Do This 
Analyze multiple clips or views of the left 
heart chambers in review 
Prerequisite: Acquire the required cardiac clips. 
1. Activate review. 
2. Tap Multiple Select. 
3. Select one of each of the following apical views: A4C, A3C, A2C. 
Note: You cannot activate the feature if you select more than three

4. To review selected images before activating the feature, tap 
Compare and then select the images for comparison. 
5. Tap 2D Heart AI. 
The ultrasound system displays a progress bar as the feature

and displays the bullseye view layout.

 Click Cancel while the feature is detecting the contours and 
calculating the results. 
Exit the feature

content:
D3  2D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D3 - 11 
Detecting ED and ES Frames with ED-ES Assist 
The ED-ES Assist feature assesses a single beat and determines the end diastolic (ED) and 
end systolic (ES) frames using the largest and smallest sizes of the left ventricle. 
The feature activates during 2D Heart AI when an ECG trace is not available. 
You can also activate ED-ES Assist to analyze the final three seconds of a clip and obtain 
system-identified ED and ES frames. 
If the ED or ES key frames are not detected, you can analyze manually set key frames. 
To set key frames with ED-ES Assist: 
 
Tap ED-ES Assist. 
The feature detects the ED and ES key frames, displays a notification indicating the 
key frames are set by ED-ES Assist, and updates the results. 
If the feature is unable to detect the key frames, the system prompts you to set the 
key frames. 
To analyze manually set key frames: 
Prerequisite: Select the ED and ES key frames. 
See also: For information about positioning and assigning ED and ES frames, refer to Chapter 7 in 
the Instructions for Use. 
 
Tap Analyze. 
The system displays the summary view and the results.

content:
D3  2D Heart AI 
D3 - 12 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Analyzing the Results 
Saving the Results 
You can save the results to the patient report. After edits and updates are complete, be sure to 
reconfirm the results before saving the results to the report. 
To save the results to the report: 
1. 
Perform manual adjustments to the contours or tracking parameters, if necessary, and then 
confirm the results. 
2. 
Press the control assigned to the clip store function. 
Adjusting the Tracking Parameters 
Use the configuration settings to define the default parameters for analysis. 
Note: An asterisk (*) displays next to results with manual adjustments. 
To 
Do This 
Analyze a different number of heart beats 
(Available only for multiple beats) 
 Tap Beats Analyzed and then select the number of beats, up to five. 
The results display an average of the selected number of beats or an 
individual beat analysis. 
Note: Increasing the number of beats moves the ECG margin to the 
left to include prior beats. If the clip does not include the selected 
number of beats, the system analyzes the available beats. 
Exclude a heart beat from the analysis 
(Available only for multiple beats) 
 Select the beat and then tap Exclude Beat. 
The system removes the selected beat, including the contour and 
results. 
The results identify the excluded beat, for example, if the second beat 
is excluded, the results display *Beats Excluded: 2. 
 To include the beat, tap Exclude Beat again. 
Analyze an average of heart beats 
 Tap Average Result. 
An average of the beats displays in the results. 
The results indicate the number of beats averaged, for example, 
Average (3 beats). 
 To analyze individual beats, tap Average Result again. 
The results indicate the beat analyzed, for example, Beat 3 of 3. 
Analyze another heart beat  
1. Press Cine to select Beats, if necessary. 
2. Rotate Cine to select another location in the ECG trace. 
The beat in analysis displays in the viewports. 
Select the end diastolic and end systolic 
frames 
See also: For information about repositioning ED and ES markers and 
assigning ED and ES frames, refer to Chapter 7 in the Instructions for 
Use.

content:
D3  2D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D3 - 13 
To 
Do This 
Show or hide the left ventricle (LV) 
epicardium 
(Available only in in A4C and A2C viewports) 
 Tap LV Epi. 
The system shows the epicardium in mesh, and the LV mass updates 
in the results. 
 To remove the mesh, tap LV Epi again. 
 Excluding the mesh enables visualization of the segments on the LV 
endocardium model. 
Adjust the distance between the 
epicardium mesh and the left ventricle 
(Available when the left ventricle epicardium mesh is shown) 
 Rotate LV Epi Offset to increase or decrease the contour. 
Adjust the aortic valve closure time 
(Available only with 2D Heart+ AI) 
(Available only for the left ventricle when the image is in single or 
bullseye view) 
 Rotate AVC to adjust the time in milliseconds (ms) and then update 
the value. 
The values update in the report summary. 
Adjust the pre-atrial contraction time at the 
onset of the P-wave 
(Available only with 2D Heart+ AI)

D3  2D Heart AI 
D3 - 14 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
To 
Do This 
Select the timing or phase for the bullseye 
view 
(Available only for the left ventricle) 
1. Tap Curve and then select Segmental Strain. 
2. Tap Timing / Phase and then select an option. 
– Peak Systolic Strain (PSS) displays the peak strain value during 
systole as measured before aortic valve closure. 
– End Systolic Strain (ESS) displays the strain value at end systole 
measured at aortic valve closure. 
– Time to Peak (TTP) displays the time to reach peak strain. 
– Post Systolic Strain (PS) displays the strain value after end 
systole as measured after aortic valve closure. 
– Post Systolic Indexed (PSI) displays the ratio between strain 
(deformation) after end systole divided by total strain. 
Select the curve for the bullseye view 
 Tap Curve and then select an option. 
Note: All options are available for the left ventricle. Only Volume and 
Global Strain are available for the left atrium. 
– Volume displays the change in chamber volume from end diastole 
to end systole as derived from the left ventricle and left atrium. 
– Segmental Strain displays the average strain value in each 
segment of the cardiac chamber, for example, the left ventricle. 
Note: Selecting segmental strain when the left ventricle is 
disabled, changes the curve to volume. 
– Global Strain displays the overall global strain or deformation for 
the left ventricle and left atrium. 
– Strain Rate indicates the rate of strain or how fast the deformation 
occurs for the left ventricle.

D3  2D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D3 - 15 
Editing the Contours 
The 2D Heart AI feature displays contours for editing only on the end diastolic and end systolic 
frames for each heart chamber in the ED-ES view. You can manually adjust or delete and 
redraw the system-generated contours. When the contour is complete, the system reanalyzes 
the contour and updates the results. 
Note: You can also manually draw the contours if the system could not detect the contours. 
To edit a contour: 
 
Click the required viewport in the ED-ES view. 
 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the brightness of the contour 
 Rotate Contour Brightness. 
Show or hide the contours 
 Tap Hide Contours. 
Edit a contour 
1. Click the required viewport, if necessary. 
2. Position the pointer to activate the required segment of the contour. 
The segment displays in yellow with the active section in red. 
3. Move the pointer to adjust the contour and then click the image to 
anchor the contour. 
– To edit a smaller section of the contour, move the pointer near the 
contour. 
– To edit a larger section of the contour, move the pointer further 
from the contour. 
The segment displays in green(LV), blue (LA), yellow (RV), or 
turquoise (RA) as you adjust the contour.  
4. Click a trackball key to anchor the placement. 
Delete a contour 
 Tap Delete Contour and then select the chamber: LA, LV, RA, RV. 
The system deletes the selected contour and then displays options 
for manually adding a contour. 
Draw a contour 
1. Select a chamber and then tap Add Contour, if necessary. 
The system displays a message at the bottom of the image screen 
instructing the points to mark for drawing the contour. 
See also: On-Screen Messages, page D3-20 
2. Roll the trackball to position the first marker and then press a 
trackball key to set the position. 
3. Roll the trackball to position the second marker and then press a 
trackball key to set the position. 
4. Roll the trackball to position the third marker and then press a 
trackball key to set the position. 
The system draws the contour on the selected chamber. 
Undo the previous edit, deletion, or 
addition to a contour 
 Tap Undo. 
Note: You can undo up to ten changes.

Adjusting the Image Screen Layout 
Use the configuration settings to select the default layouts for the 2D Heart AI feature. 
To 
Do This 
Rename the selected viewport 
 Tap Rename View and then select an option. 
– A2C indicates apical two chambers 
– A3C indicates apical three chambers 
– A4C indicates apical four chambers 
The system updates the name of the viewport and results. 
Show or hide the right ventricle 
 Tap RV. 
Show or hide the right atrium 
 Tap RA. 
Show or hide the left ventricle 
 Tap LV. 
Show or hide the left atrium 
 Tap LA. 
Activate the next viewport 
 Press UPDATE. 
Activate a viewport 
 Click the required viewport.

(Available only with 2D Heart+ AI) 
 Tap Bullseye View. 
Display the ED-ES view layout 
(Available only with 2D Heart+ AI) 
 Tap ED-ES View. 
Display the single view layout 
(Available only with 2D Heart+ AI) 
 Tap Single View. 
Hide the segment values from the 
viewport image 
(Available only in the bullseye or single view) 
 Click the hide segment values icon. 
 
Access the ED-ES view to edit a contour 
(Available only in the bullseye or single view) 
 Click the edit icon. 
 
The system displays the ED-ES view. 
Delete the view from the analysis 
(Available only in the bullseye view) 
1. Click the delete icon. 
 
The system displays a message asking if you want to delete the view 
and all associated results. 
2. To delete the view and results, click OK. 
3. To retain the view and results, click Cancel.  
View the analysis of an apical chamber 
(Available only in the bullseye view) 
 Click the single view icon. 
 
View the bullseye layout 
(Available only in the single view) 
 Click the bullseye view icon.

The feature supports the following functionality: 
 
Selecting frames or beats for CINE review. 
 
Viewing the current position or changing the position of the end diastole or end systole. 
 
Playing back and editing clips and volumes. 
– 
As you scroll CINE, the frame marker in the curve graph moves in synchronicity with 
CINE scrolling. 
 
Repositioning the current frame marker on the ECG trace when playback is paused. 
Note: A horizontal line displays on the time axis when ECG trace data is unavailable. 
 
Capturing clips and static images. 
See also: For information about playing back CINE data and clips during review, refer to Chapter 7 
in the Instructions for Use. 
Reviewing Results in the Curve Graph 
You can display the measurement results for a curve in the summary results and display the 
corresponding segment in the bullseye viewport. 
To display data about a curve: 
 
Position the pointer over a curve.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D4 - 3 
Overview 
 WARNING: This feature uses ultrasound data collected prior to analysis. The quality of the data 
collected and used as input could have an effect on the output of this feature. Variability in 
ultrasound system performance, operator technique, patient characteristics, and other factors 
may affect the output. At all times, the clinician is advised to carefully review the output and 
confirm the information presented with clinical judgment and any other relevant sources of data. 
The 4D Heart AI feature is a four-dimensional (4D) image processing feature for detecting, 
evaluating, and quantifying the shape, size, and function of the heart chambers. The feature 
provides volume and strain analysis. 
4D Heart AI detects the cardiac view, identifies borders (contours), and measures cardiac 
function for the left ventricle, left atrium, right ventricle, and right atrium. Contours indicate the 
positions of the three-dimensional (3D) model for the multiplanar reconstructions (MPR) or 
volume slice. 
Measurement results are based on contours from the end diastole (ED) and end systole (ES) 
frames. 
Use the feature to perform the following tasks: 
 
Visualize the left ventricle and left atrium and quantitative analysis of ejection fraction, 
volumes, and mechanical dyssynchrony. 
 
Visualize the right ventricle and right atrium for evaluation and quantification of size and 
function. 
 
Confirm the contour placement and make any adjustments, if necessary. 
 
Analyze measurement results based on 4D volume ultrasound data. 
Data is available in multiple formats: a curve graph for measurements over time, a bullseye 
plot with a graphical representation of the heart, and a textual report format. 
 
Analyze a single heart beat after confirming end diastole and end systole frames. 
 
Analyze all frames of the cardiac cycle for multiple beats captured during a physio study 
using a visual representation of heart motion and function. 
See also: For information about using the physiologic function, refer to Chapter C1 in this 
manual. 
Use the configuration settings to customize the default settings for the 4D Heart AI feature. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and imaging presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
D4 - 4 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Workflow 
The clinical workflow includes the following steps. 
Step 1: Acquiring Cardiac 4D Volumes 
 
During cardiac 4D volume imaging, freeze the image. 
 
During review, open the required cardiac 4D volume clips. 
Note: For volume clips in review, tracking is only available for the left ventricle and left atrium 
chambers. 
 
4D volume imaging or clips can include an ECG trace (a physio signal is present) or 
exclude an ECG trace (no physio signal). 
See also: For information about using the physiologic function, refer to Chapter C1 in this 
manual. 
Note: Without a physio signal, the feature analyzes only one beat. You must identify the ED and 
ES frames and select analyze for detection. 
Step 2: Detecting and Analyzing the Cardiac Chambers 
 
4D Heart AI detects the view, places contours across all frames for the selected beats, 
analyzes the 4D ultrasound data, and displays the results. 
Note: Available results are dependent on the acquired views. 
Step 3: Reviewing, Adjusting, and Saving the Results 
 
Analyze the results for single or multiple heart chambers. 
 
Select a heart chamber or beat to analyze. 
 
Select different view layouts: ED-ES, detailed, or bullseye. 
Note: Bullseye view is only available for cardiac 4D volume clips in review. 
 
View the multiplanar reconstruction or volume from another orientation. 
 
Redefine the diastolic or systolic frame. 
 
Edit, delete, or redraw contours on the LV, LA, RV, or RA. 
 
Reanalyze the views to update the results. 
 
Review the clips or volume in playback. 
 
Save the tracking results.

ED-ES View Layout 
The end diastolic-end systolic (ED-ES) view displays when you activate 4D Heart AI from the

The ED and ES viewports provide the apical four chamber (A4C) view and either the apical two 
chamber (A2C) or the parasternal short axis (PSAX) view. 
Note: The freeze control is unavailable in the ED-ES view. Use the CINE feature to review the 
frames.

D4 - 8 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Detailed View Layout 
The detailed view displays multiple viewports for a single frame for additional representations of 
the contours. 
The layout of the detailed view is based on the selected chamber. 
 
Left ventricle: apical three chamber (A3), apical two chamber (A2), apical four chamber 
(A4), short axis (SAX) 
 
Left atrium: A3C, A2C, A4C, SAX 
 
Right ventricle: A4C, coronal, SAX 
 
Right atrium: A4C, right heart apical two chamber (RH A2), SAX 
Note: The freeze control is available in the detailed view. 
 
Example of the 4D Heart AI screen, detailed view layout.

D4  4D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D4 - 9 
Bullseye View Layout 
 
Example of the 4D Heart AI screen, bullseye view layout. 
1 
Volume model viewport 
2 
Volume 
3 
Model 
You can show or hide the epicardium mesh on the left ventricle. 
Displays segments on the left ventricle endocardium as you position your cursor over or select a 
segmental strain curve or segment on the bullseye. 
4 
ECG trace 
During playback, includes the current frame marker. 
During pause of playback, displays the ED and ES markers. 
5 
Curve graph viewport 
Provides a view of the timing or phase, for example, segmental strain. 
Includes volume curves, the current frame marker, aortic valve closure (AVC) time, and pre atrial 
(Pre-A) contraction time. 
6 
Thumbnail panel 
Displays reference images of previously saved images and clips. 
7 
Results summary view 
Displays the tracking results for the heart rate and measurements. 
Displays an asterisk (*) and footnote when the body surface area (BSA) is indexed or a beat is 
excluded. 
8 
Bullseye color bar 
Provides colors assigned to the parameter ranges. 
9 
Bullseye viewport 
Displays a bullseye plot with the following segment values: anterior, inferior, lateral, septal, coronal.

D4  4D Heart AI 
D4 - 10 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Activating 4D Heart AI 
You can activate 4D Heart AI during 4D cardiac volume imaging or from the review function. 
See also: For information about cardiac volume imaging, refer to Chapter D2 in this manual. 
See also: For information about activating review, refer to Chapter B1 in this manual. 
To activate 4D Heart AI: 
To 
Do This 
Analyze the heart chambers during live 
imaging in 4D-mode 
1. Activate cardiac volume imaging. 
2. Acquire the required view and then press FREEZE. 
3. Tap 4D Heart AI. 
The ultrasound system displays a progress bar as the feature activates, 
and the feature detects the contours, calculates the results, and displays 
the ED-ES view. 
Analyze the heart chambers during 
review 
Prerequisite: Acquire the required cardiac clips. 
1. Activate review. 
2. Select the required volume clip. 
 
Example of an icon identifying a volume clip in the thumbnail panel. 
3. Tap 4D Heart AI. 
The ultrasound system displays a progress bar as the feature activates, 
and the feature detects the contours, calculates the results, and displays 
the ED-ES view.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D4 - 11 
Analyzing the Results 
Saving the Results 
You can save the results to the patient report. After edits and updates are complete, be sure to 
reconfirm the results before saving the results to the report. 
To save the results to the report: 
1. 
Confirm the results after performing any manual adjustments to the contours or tracking 
parameters, if necessary. 
2. 
Press the control assigned to the clip store function. 
Adjusting the Analysis Parameters 
Use the configuration settings to define the default parameters for analysis. 
Note: An asterisk (*) displays next to results with manual adjustments. 
To 
Do This 
Analyze a different number of 
heart beats 
(Available only for multiple beats) 
 Tap Beats Analyzed and then select the number of beats, up to five. 
The results display an average of the selected number of beats. 
Note: Increasing the number of beats moves the ECG margin to the left 
to include prior beats. If the clip does not include the selected number of 
beats, the system analyzes the available beats. 
Exclude a heart beat from the analysis 
(Available only for multiple beats) 
 Select the beat and then tap Exclude Beat. 
The system removes the selected beat, including the contour, results, 
aortic valve closure (AVC) time, pre-atrial (Pre-A) contraction time, and 
bullseye plot. 
The results identify the excluded beat, for example, if the second beat is 
excluded, the results display *Beats Excluded: 2. 
 To include the beat, tap Exclude Beat again. 
Analyze an average of heart beats 
 Tap Average Result. 
An average of the beats displays in the results. 
The results indicate the number of beats averaged, for example, 
Average (3 beats). 
 To analyze individual beats, tap Average Result again. 
The results indicate the beat analyzed, for example, Beat 3 of 3. 
Analyze another heart beat 
 Rotate Cine to select another location in the ECG trace and then tap 
Analyze. 
The beat in analysis displays in the viewports.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
D4 - 12 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
To 
Do This 
Select the end diastolic and 
end systolic frames 
See also: For information about repositioning ED and ES markers and 
assigning ED and ES frames, refer to Chapter 7 in the Instructions for Use. 
Show or hide the left ventricle (LV) 
epicardium 
Prerequisite: Display the LV viewport. 
 Tap LV Epi. 
The model shows the epicardium in mesh, and the LV mass updates in 
the results. 
 To remove the mesh, tap LV Epi again. 
Excluding the mesh enables visualization of the segments on the LV 
endocardium model. 
Adjust the aortic valve closure time 
(Available only for the left ventricle when the clip is frozen in bullseye view) 
 Rotate AVC to adjust the time in milliseconds (ms). 
The values update in the report summary. 
Note: During analysis of multiple beats, the aortic valve closure time 
displays only for the current beat. 
Adjust the pre-atrial contraction time at 
the onset of the P-wave 
(Available only for the left atrium when the clip is frozen in bullseye view) 
 Rotate Pre-A to adjust the time in milliseconds (ms). 
The values update in the report summary. 
Note: During analysis of multiple beats, the pre-atrial contraction time 
displays only for the current beat. 
Perform a single-beat analysis 
Prerequisite: Acquire volumes with a minimum of one cardiac cycle. 
1. Position the ED and ES markers, if necessary. 
The system calculates and displays the results after you verify the ED 
and ES frames. 
See also: For information about positioning the ED and ES markers, 
refer to Chapter 7 in the Instructions for Use. 
2. Tap Analyze. 
The system displays a progress bar, calculates the results, and updates 
the results summary.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D4 - 13 
To 
Do This 
Select the timing or phase for the 
bullseye view 
(Available only for the left ventricle) 
1. Tap Curve and then select Segmental Strain. 
2. Tap Timing / Phase and then select an option. 
– Peak Systolic Strain (PSS) displays the peak strain value during 
systole as measured before aortic valve closure. 
– End Systolic Strain (ESS) displays the strain value at end systole 
measured at aortic valve closure. 
– Time to Peak (TTP) displays the time to reach peak strain. 
– Post Systolic Strain (PS) displays the strain value after end systole 
as measured after aortic valve closure. 
– Post Systolic Indexed (PSI) displays the ratio between strain 
(deformation) after end systole divided by total strain. 
Select the curve for the bullseye view 
Prerequisite: The left ventricle is required for Segmental Strain. The left 
ventricle and/or left atrium are required for Volume and Global Strain. 
 Tap Curve and then select an option. 
Note: All options are available for the left ventricle. Only Volume and 
Global Strain are available for the left atrium. 
– Volume displays the change in chamber volume from end diastole to 
end systole as derived from the left ventricle and left atrium. 
– Segmental Strain displays the average strain value in each segment 
of the cardiac chamber, for example, the left ventricle. 
Note: Selecting segmental strain when the left ventricle is disabled 
changes the curve to volume. 
– Global Strain displays the overall global strain or deformation for the 
left ventricle and left atrium. 
Change the direction of strain analysis 
for the bullseye view 
(Available only for the left ventricle) 
1. Tap Curve and then select Segmental Strain. 
2. Tap Direction and then select an option. 
– Longitudinal displays the strain results in the longitudinal direction. 
– Circumferential displays the strain results in the circumferential 
direction.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
D4 - 14 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Editing the Contours 
You can manually adjust or delete and redraw the system-generated contours. After the 
contour is drawn, the system reanalyzes the contour and updates the results. 
Note: You can also manually draw the contours if the system could not detect the contours. 
To edit a contour: 
To 
Do This 
Show or hide the contours in the 
selected viewport 
 Tap Hide Contours. 
Edit a contour 
1. Tap Edit Contour. 
2. Select a viewport. Or, press UPDATE. 
3. Position the pointer to activate the required segment of the contour. 
The segment displays in yellow with the active section in red. 
The model displays with mesh. 
4. Move the pointer to adjust the contour and then click the image to 
anchor the contour. 
– To edit a smaller section of the contour, move the pointer near the 
contour. 
– To edit a larger section of the contour, move the pointer further from 
the contour. 
The segment displays in green (LV), blue (LA), yellow (RV), or turquoise 
(RA) as you adjust the contour. 
The mesh on the model repositions as you adjust the contour. 
5. Click a trackball key to anchor the placement. 
Adjust the distance between the 
epicardium mesh and the left ventricle 
(Available only when the left ventricle epicardium mesh is shown) 
1. Tap Edit Contour. 
2. Rotate LV Epi Offset and then select a setting.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D4 - 15 
To 
Do This 
Delete a contour 
1. Select the ED or ES viewport. 
2. Tap Delete Contour and select a heart chamber: LV, LA, RV, RA. 
The system deletes the selected contour and then displays options for 
manually adding a contour. 
Draw a contour 
1. Select either the ED or ES viewport and then tap Add Contour, 
if necessary. 
The system displays the detailed view layout and a message at the 
bottom of the image screen instructing the points to mark for drawing the 
contour. 
See also: On-Screen Messages, page D4-20 
2. Roll the trackball to position the first marker and then press a trackball 
key to set the position. 
3. Roll the trackball to position the second marker and then press a 
trackball key to set the position. 
4. Roll the trackball to position the third marker and then press a trackball 
key to set the position. 
The system draws the contour on the selected chamber. 
Undo the previous edit, deletion, or 
addition to a contour 
 Tap Undo. 
Note: You can undo up to 10 changes.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
D4 - 16 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Changing the Image Screen Layout 
Use the configuration settings to select the default layouts for the 4D Heart AI feature. 
See also: For additional information about changing the image screen layout, refer to Chapter D2 in 
this manual. 
To 
Do This 
Hide or show the volume data in the 
model viewport 
 Tap Hide VR. 
Hide or show the model on the volume 
 Tap Hide Model. 
Show or hide the right ventricle 
 Tap RV. 
Show or hide the right atrium 
 Tap RA. 
Show or hide the left ventricle 
 Tap LV. 
Show or hide the left atrium 
 Tap LA. 
Activate the next viewport 
 Press UPDATE. 
Display the detailed view layout 
 Tap Detailed View. 
Display the ED-ES view layout 
 Tap ED-ES View. 
Display the bullseye view layout 
Prerequisite: Select the left ventricle, or select both the left ventricle and 
the left atrial. Select a heart cycle of one to five beats. 
 Tap Bullseye View. 
See also: For information about the bullseye view, refer to page D4-18. 
Rotating the Volume and Multiplanar Reconstructions 
Rotation of the volume enables visualization of the anatomical structure from any angle. The 
volume rotates independently of the multiplanar reconstructions (MPR). 
During rotation of a multiplanar reconstruction, the rotation of the three orthogonal planes is 
synchronized along the axis of the active plane. You can synchronize the position of the volume 
to the position of any multiplanar reconstruction. 
The axis markers display in the ED-ES and detailed views. 
See also: For information about rotating the volume and multiplanar reconstructions, refer to 
Chapter D2 in this manual. 
Magnifying or Panning an Area of Interest 
(Not available for the bullseye view) 
You can adjust the magnification level for the volume model viewports. You cannot magnify the 
bullseye view. 
See also: For information about rotating the magnifying or panning an area of interest, refer to 
Chapter D2 in this manual.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D4 - 17 
Reviewing CINE Playback 
The feature supports the following functionality: 
 
Selecting frames or beats for CINE review. 
 
Viewing the current position or changing the position of the end diastole or end systole. 
 
Playing back and editing. 
– 
During playback the volume model viewport displays the active frame or beat. 
– 
As you scroll CINE, the frame marker in the curve graph moves in synchronicity with 
CINE scrolling. 
Note: CINE playback is not available for the ED-ES view. 
 
Repositioning the current frame marker on the ECG trace when playback is paused. 
Note: A horizontal line displays on the time axis when ECG trace data is unavailable. 
 
Capturing clips and static images. 
See also: For information about CINE, refer to Chapter 7 in the Instructions for Use. 
Reviewing Results in the Curve Graph 
You can display the measurement results for a curve in the summary results and display the 
corresponding segment in the volume model and bullseye viewports. 
To display data about a curve: 
 
Position the pointer over a curve.

D4  4D Heart AI 
D4 - 18 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Reviewing Results in a Bullseye Plot 
(Available only during review) 
Each segment in the bullseye view is represented by a curve in the curve view. 
Note: If all four chambers are active, selecting the bullseye view hides the right ventricle (RV) and 
right atrium (RA). The RV and RA are shown again when accessing the ED-ES or detailed view. 
See also: For information about 4D Heart AI result labels, refer to Appendix D in the System 
Reference. 
To review results in a bullseye plot: 
Prerequisite: Select the left ventricle, or select both the left ventricle and the left atrial. Select a 
heart cycle of one to five beats. 
 
Tap Bullseye View. 
 
To 
Do This 
Activate or deactivate individual 
segments on the bullseye plot 
 Click the required segments in the bullseye plot. 
The analysis results include segments in color and exclude segments 
in gray. The deactivated segments are excluded from the segmental 
strain curve. The deactivated segments display in gray on the volume 
model. 
Display a corresponding segment in 
the volume model and segmental 
strain curve 
 Position the pointer over a segment in the bullseye plot.

content:
D4  4D Heart AI 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D4 - 19 
Restoring Original Acquisition Settings 
You can restore the original acquisition settings and factory-default settings of the volume and 
multiplanar reconstructions. 
Use the configuration settings to specify the default layout for orientating the volume model. 
To 
Do This 
Restore the position and rotation to the 
factory-default settings 
 Tap Reset Orientation. 
Restore the feature to the last state of 
successful detection 
 Tap Reset Home. 
Reviewing the Report 
Prerequisite: Save the results to the report. 
The bullseye displays the timing or phase value selected in system configuration or during the 
study and the last single beat analysis. You cannot remove segments from the bullseye in the 
report. 
See also: For information about viewing the report, refer to Chapter 12 in the Instructions for Use. 
See also: For information about 4D Heart AI result labels, refer to Appendix D in the System 
Reference.

D4  4D Heart AI 
D4 - 20 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
On-Screen Messages 
The system displays informational messages in dialog boxes, progress bars, or the message 
area on the bottom of the image screen. 
Message 
Description 
Place AntSept, Post, Apex points in 
A3C view 
Draw the left ventricle with three points. 
Place the anterior-septal, posterior, and apex points in the apical three 
chamber view. 
Place AntSept, Post, Roof points in 
A3C view 
Draw the left anterior with three points. 
Place the anterior-septal, posterior, and roof points in the apical three 
chamber view. 
Place Sept, FW, Apex points in A4C 
view and Infund, Post, Lat points in 
SAX view 
Draw the right ventricle with six points. 
Place the septal, free wall, and apex points in the apical four chamber 
view and the infundibular, posterior, and lateral points in the short axis 
view. 
Place Sept, FW, Roof points in A4C 
view 
Draw the right anterior with three points. 
Place the septal, free wall, and roof points in the apical four chamber 
view. 
Verify the ED, ES frames and tap 
Analyze 
Verify the end diastole and end systole frames and then tap Analyze. 
Set ED frame with ED control 
Use the ED control to set the position of the end diastole frame. 
All ED-ES frames must have LV 
contours (or LA contours) for Bullseye 
View. Please correct and proceed. 
Confirm contours are drawn on the left ventricle and left atrium in the 
ED-ES view before selecting the bullseye view. 
Current beat excluded. Contours 
hidden. 
The current beat is excluded. The contours are hidden. 
Current beat included. Contours 
shown. 
The current beat is included. The contours are shown. 
Failed to detect configured chambers. 
Correct manually. 
Unable to detect the configured chambers. Manually correct the 
chambers. 
Thumbnail captured. Results not sent 
to report. 
The thumbnail image was captured, but the results were not saved to 
the report. Try again. 
Calculating results 
The feature is calculating the results. 
Detecting contours. Calculating results. 
The feature is detecting the contours and calculating the results. 
Detecting contours. Calculating results. 
Wait for completion or exit. 
The feature is detecting the contours and calculating the results. You 
can wait for the results or exit the feature. 
Loading application to captured state 
The feature is launching with the selected capture data. 
Low Volume Rate < 15vps 
Displays under the curve viewport when the volume rate is low. 
Indicates the acquisition is less than 15 volumes per second (vps).

content:
D5  ICE Workflow 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D5 - 3 
Overview 
The intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) workflow streamlines image optimization and 
measurements during use of a 2D ICE catheter by providing simplified selections on the 
touch screen. 
Access to full controls is available during the study, for example, image optimization selections 
for adjusting the flow angle or the angle of the Doppler cursor. 
You can activate the ICE workflow only with compatible transducers and studies. 
See also: For a list of compatible transducers and image presets, refer to Appendix A in the 
Instructions for Use. 
 
Example of the touch screen with the ICE workflow function during 2D-mode with color. 
1 
Lock screen 
Locks the touch screen and trackball. Pressing the freeze key unlocks the touch screen and trackball. 
2 
Imaging mode, freeze, and capture selections 
3 
Selection for accessing full controls or the ICE workflow 
4 
Size and position controls 
During imaging, provides pinch control for sizing the region of interest (ROI) and drag control for 
positioning the ROI or Doppler cursor 
During the measure function, displays an image of the trackball with a reminder to use the trackball 
when performing measurements 
5 
Plus and minus buttons 
Performs fine adjustments to the region of interest (ROI) 
6 
Slide controls

content:
D5  ICE Workflow 
D5 - 4 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Activating the ICE Workflow 
See also: For information about preparing the catheter and connector for use in an ultrasound exam, 
refer to the instructions for use shipped with your catheter and your catheter connector. 
See also: For information about beginning a study and registering the patient, refer to Chapter 5 in 
the Instructions for Use. 
To activate the ICE workflow: 
Prerequisite: Power on the ultrasound system. Prepare the catheter and connector for use in an 
ultrasound exam. Register the patient and begin the study. 
 
Connect a compatible catheter to the ultrasound system. 
The ultrasound system displays the ICE workflow selections on the touch screen. 
Note: If the selections are not available, activate ICE from the additional selections. 
Freezing the Image 
Freeze the image when the catheter is not in use or prior to performing a measurement. 
To freeze or unfreeze ultrasound imaging: 
 
Tap Freeze. 
 
Tap Freeze again to unfreeze the image and resume imaging. 
Selecting Imaging Modes 
Activate an imaging mode for access to the associated image optimization settings. 
 
2D imaging activates a two-dimensional grayscale image and a grayscale bar on the image 
screen. 
 
Color imaging applies color to the velocities and directions of blood flow within the region of 
interest and displays the color bar on the image screen. 
 
Pulsed wave (PW) Doppler imaging displays a Doppler spectrum below the 2D image and 
Doppler cursor and gate on the image. The cursor represents the acoustic line for 
gathering Doppler information, for example, volume flow data. 
Note: Tap more than one selection to activate combined imaging modes. 
To 
Do This 
Activate 2D imaging 
 Tap 2D. 
Activate or exit color imaging 
 Tap Color. 
 To exit color imaging, tap Color again. 
Activate or exit pulsed wave (PW) Doppler 
 Tap PW. 
 To exit PW Doppler, tap PW again.

content:
D5  ICE Workflow 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D5 - 5 
Optimizing Images 
The ultrasound system retains the image optimization settings when you freeze or unfreeze the 
image or optimize the image with full controls and then activate the ICE workflow. 
Prerequisite: Activate the ICE workflow and begin imaging. Activate the required imaging mode. 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the imaging depth 
 Adjust the Depth setting. 
– Drag the dot on the slide control. 
– Tap a new location on the slide control. 
– Tap the plus button to increase the depth. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the depth. 
Adjust the 2D gain (increase or decrease 
brightness of the image) 
 Adjust the Image Gain setting. 
– Drag the dot on the slide control. 
– Tap a new location on the slide control. 
– Tap the plus button to increase the brightness. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the brightness. 
Adjust the color gain (increase or 
decrease flow detection in the image) 
(Available only during color imaging) 
 Adjust the Color Gain setting. 
– Drag the dot on the slide control. 
– Tap a new location on the slide control. 
– Tap the plus button to increase the amount of color. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the amount of color. 
Enhance the cardiac image 
 Select an Enhance Image setting.

content:
D5  ICE Workflow 
D5 - 6 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
Optimizing the Doppler Spectrum 
To display the real-time Doppler spectrum: 
Prerequisite: Activate PW Doppler. 
 
Tap Activate Doppler. 
 
To 
Do This 
Adjust the Doppler gain (increase or 
decrease brightness of the spectrum) 
 Adjust the Doppler Gain setting. 
– Drag the dot on the slide control. 
– Tap a new location on the slide control. 
– Tap the plus button to increase the brightness. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the brightness.  
Adjust the scrolling speed of the Doppler 
spectrum 
 Adjust the Speed setting. 
– Tap the plus button to increase the speed. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the speed. 
Adjust the velocity scale factor of pulse 
repetition frequency (PRF) 
Note: Adjusting PRF may improve velocity range sensitivity or control 
aliasing. 
 Adjust the Scale setting. 
– Tap the plus button to increase PRF. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease PRF. 
Adjust the display of blood flow velocity 
 Adjust the Baseline setting. 
– Tap the plus button to move the baseline upward for emphasis of 
negative velocities. 
– Tap the minus button to move the baseline downward for 
emphasis of positive velocities. 
Adjust the Doppler audio volume 
 Tap a volume selection. 
 
– Tap the plus button to increase the volume. 
– Tap the minus button to decrease the volume. 
Note: Activate full controls to access the mute option. 
Pause the Doppler spectrum and refresh 
the 2D image 
 Tap Update.

content:
D5  ICE Workflow 
Advanced Imaging Manual 
D5 - 7 
Positioning and Resizing the Area of Interest 
Note: You can also access full controls to perform additional adjustments, for example, adjust the 
angle of the Doppler gate. 
Prerequisite: Activate the imaging mode, if necessary: 2D for the region of interest (ROI), color for 
the color ROI, or Doppler for the Doppler cursor and gate. 
To 
Do This 
Reposition the region of interest (ROI) or 
the color ROI 
 Drag the ROI on the touch screen. 
 Roll the trackball. 
Resize the region of interest (ROI) or the 
color ROI 
Note: When the color ROI is active, the plus and minus buttons include 
the following label: Color Size. 
 Pinch and drag the ROI representation on the touch screen. 
– Vertical pinch and drag resizes the height. 
– Horizontal pinch and drag resizes the width. 
– Angled pinch and drag resizes both the height and width. 
 To perform fine adjustments, press the plus and minus buttons below 
the ROI. 
Reposition the Doppler cursor 
 Drag the Doppler cursor on the touch screen. 
 Roll the trackball. 
Reviewing CINE Playback 
You can review CINE playback on a frozen image. 
To play back CINE data: 
Prerequisite: Freeze the image. 
To 
Do This 
Start continuous playback 
 Tap the play icon. 
 
Stop continuous playback 
 Tap the pause button. 
 
Display one frame to the left 
 Tap the frame-left button. 
 
Display one frame to the right 
 Tap the frame-right button. 
 
Scroll the frames 
 Drag the dot on the slide control.
